articles.title: Noticias SOL: Los informes de errores en Solana ahora cuestan 1 SOL mientras la IA inunda a los equipos de seguridad con spam
articles.text:
Los informes de errores en Solana ahora cuestan 1 SOL mientras la IA inunda a los equipos de seguridad con spam
Los investigadores deben ahora quemar permanentemente 1 SOL por cada envío después de que un concurso de un mes atrajera 809 reportes, con la creencia de que la IA ayudó a generar o redactar casi todos ellos.
- Firedancer requerirá que los investigadores quemen 1 SOL, valorado en aproximadamente $100, por cada informe de error para disuadir el spam y reducir la carga de revisar las presentaciones asistidas por IA.
- Una reciente competencia de auditorías recibió 809 informes pero generó solo 127 hallazgos de seguridad únicos, con casi la mitad de las presentaciones válidas duplicando informes anteriores.
- Jump Crypto está aumentando temporalmente las recompensas, con fallas críticas en el sistema de votación Alpenglow de Solana que son elegibles para pagos de hasta $300,000.
Una avalancha de reportes de errores asistidos por IA ha llevado al equipo detrás del software Firedancer de Solana a cobrar a los investigadores 1 SOL, valorado en aproximadamente $100, por cada envío, con el objetivo de reducir el spam y otorgar a los ingenieros más tiempo para investigar fallas de seguridad genuinas.
Los tokens deben ser quemados, lo que los elimina permanentemente de la circulación. Bajo términos actualizados el lunes, el costo no es reembolsable incluso si un informe es inválido, está fuera del alcance del programa o duplica un hallazgo anterior. Los informes enviados sin una quema no son elegibles para recompensas.
La firma de trading Jump Crypto desarrolló Firedancer como una alternativa a Agave, el software principal utilizado por los ordenadores que verifican y procesan las transacciones de Solana.
Una falla grave puede impedir que esos ordenadores procesen pagos o causar discrepancias en los saldos de las cuentas, interrumpiendo operaciones y transferencias. Cientos de informes duplicados o inviables desvían el tiempo de los ingenieros de la investigación y solución de esas vulnerabilidades.
Por qué los nuevos términos
Una competencia de auditoría de 1 millón de dólares realizada entre el 9 de abril y el 9 de mayo atrajo 809 informes de 162 investigadores. Estos generaron 127 hallazgos de seguridad únicos, excluyendo observaciones no explotables. Casi la mitad de las presentaciones válidas fueron duplicadas.
Jump considera que los agentes de IA ayudaron a descubrir o redactar casi todas las presentaciones.
“La IA ha hecho que encontrar errores sea económico, pero evaluarlos sigue siendo costoso,” escribió Ishan Bhatt de Jump en un Revisión del 16 de octubre.
Los ingenieros aún debían reproducir los problemas reportados y verificar si los ataques propuestos podían funcionar. Algunas presentaciones señalaron debilidades aparentes mientras que faltaban protecciones en otras partes del software.
La acumulación alcanzó su punto máximo con 299 informes abiertos. A medida que las revisiones se ralentizaron, otros investigadores redescubrieron errores que ya habían sido reportados pero que permanecían sin corregir o sin divulgar. Aproximadamente el 80% de los duplicados llegaron más de tres días después del informe original.
La competencia ya había cobrado $100 por presentación y limitaba a los investigadores a un informe diario. Jump señala que cobrar desanima a los investigadores a enviar un gran número de hallazgos especulativos y dejar que sus ingenieros los validen.
Su nueva plataforma también limita cada sección principal del informe a 3,000 caracteres.
La competencia descubrió vulnerabilidades graves, incluyendo un error de programación que podría hacer que Firedancer ejecutara transacciones en un orden incorrecto y discrepase con otros validadores de Solana sobre el estado resultante de la red.
Mientras tanto, Jump está aumentando las recompensas junto con el costo de presentación. Las vulnerabilidades elegibles reciben el doble del pago estándar hasta el 20 de noviembre, o el triple para errores específicos de Alpenglow, el nuevo sistema de votación de Solana. Las vulnerabilidades críticas de Alpenglow pueden calificar para hasta $300,000.

articles.title: Noticias ETH: Ethereum corrige el error Glamsterdam que podría haber enviado depósitos de staking a los constructores
articles.text:
Ethereum corrige el error Glamsterdam que podría haber enviado depósitos de staking a constructores
Los desarrolladores inicialmente rechazaron el cambio antes de revertir su postura, ya que los retrasos en las pruebas les otorgaron más tiempo para examinar una falla en la próxima actualización Glamsterdam de Ethereum.
- Los desarrolladores de Ethereum corrigieron un fallo en la próxima actualización Glamsterdam que podría haber permitido a un operador retirar ETH destinado a nuevos validadores.
- La vulnerabilidad involucraba depósitos del constructor y del validador que compartían una clave pública, lo que podría acreditar ambos depósitos al constructor y dejar a los servicios de staking sin la posibilidad de recuperar sus fondos.
- No se han reportado pérdidas, y los equipos de clientes deben ahora incorporar las normas revisadas de depósitos antes de que Glamsterdam pueda avanzar hacia un lanzamiento en la mainnet.
Los desarrolladores de Ethereum han corregido un fallo en la próxima actualización Glamsterdam que podría haber permitido a alguien apropiarse del ETH que los servicios de staking destinaban a nuevos validadores.
La solución, que cambió las reglas para el manejo de los depósitos de validadores, fue fusionado el lunes, una semana después de que los desarrolladores lo rechazaran.
Glamsterdam separa dos funciones que hoy están agrupadas. Los constructores agrupan transacciones en bloques, y los validadores, quienes apuestan ETH para ayudar a asegurar la red, las seleccionan y confirman. Ambos pueden depositar ETH, y se supone que su dinero debe ser rastreado por separado.
Cómo podría desaparecer el dinero
El problema apareció durante la propia actualización, cuando Ethereum procesaba depósitos que aún estaban pendientes de ser acreditados.
El investigador Avsetsin identificó un escenario en el cual un operador primero se registra como constructor utilizando una clave pública específica, el identificador vinculado a un validador o constructor. Si un servicio de staking deposita ETH para iniciar un validador bajo esa clave, las normas preliminares acreditarían ambos depósitos al constructor.
“El operador puede retirar los fondos del protocolo,” escribió Avsetsin. No se crea ningún validador, por lo que el servicio de staking no puede generar la prueba que necesitaría para recuperar su dinero.
Avsetsin, registrado como miembro de la organización GitHub de Lido, examinó cómo podrían verse afectados Lido, Origin y Rocket Pool en lo que el investigador denominó “investigación rápida de IA.” Los hallazgos dependieron de cómo cada protocolo maneja los depósitos.
“Estos son hallazgos de código condicional, no exploits activos confirmados,” escribió avsetsin, agregando que las verificaciones existentes que rechazan un depósito anterior del constructor podrían detener el ataque. No se han reportado pérdidas.
Rechazado, luego fusionado
Desarrolladores cerró la solución propuesta el 19 de octubre. “No hubo suficiente apoyo por parte de los clientes para realizar este cambio en este momento,” escribió Justin Traglia, quien mantiene las especificaciones de consenso de Ethereum. Los clientes son los programas de software separados que los validadores ejecutan para participar en la red.
La corrección se reabrió tras una revisión adicional, avsetsin añadió pruebas el 23 de octubre y Traglia la fusionó el lunes.
Bajo las nuevas reglas, los depósitos pendientes se ordenan según sus credenciales de retiro, el ajuste que indica a dónde puede ir eventualmente el dinero de un depósito. Los depósitos de validadores permanecen con los validadores incluso si un constructor está utilizando la misma clave.
El cambio ahora forma parte de las especificaciones de consenso de Ethereum, y los equipos de clientes aún deben incorporarlo en su software. Glamsterdam ya se ejecutó en la red de prueba Sepolia, pero su lanzamiento el 26 de octubre en Hoodi, una segunda red de prueba, fue pospuesto.
Glamsterdam necesita una nueva fecha para Hoodi antes de que se pueda programar el lanzamiento en la mainnet.

articles.title: El cofundador de Zcash propone terminar con la financiación de subvenciones, citando un tesoro de 125 millones de dólares
articles.text:
El cofundador de Zcash propone acabar con la financiación mediante subvenciones, citando un tesoro de 125 millones de dólares
La propuesta de Sean Bowe enviaría el 8% de la participación del comité en el ZEC recién creado a una reserva para futuros mineros. El comité conservaría el dinero que ya ha recibido.
- El cofundador de Zcash, Sean Bowe, propuso finalizar la asignación automática del 8 % de los nuevos ZEC creados a las Subvenciones de la Comunidad Zcash y redirigirlos a una reserva para futuras recompensas de minería.
- Bowe estima que el programa de subvenciones dispone de alrededor de 125 millones de dólares después de los compromisos existentes, suficiente para financiar años de gastos incluso si el precio de ZEC cae considerablemente.
- La propuesta, que requeriría un cambio en las reglas de la red de Zcash, surge en medio del escrutinio de una subvención para actividades de divulgación en una convención de la industria adulta, pero se fundamenta en las grandes reservas del programa y los flujos continuos.
El cofundador de Zcash, Sean Bowe, ha propuesto terminar con la financiación automática del programa de subvenciones comunitarias de la red de privacidad, argumentando que su tesorería ahora es lo suficientemente grande como para cubrir años de gastos sin necesidad de que ingresen nuevos fondos.
Su borrador de propuesta, publicado a última hora del lunes, detendría la asignación automática y redirigiría su participación restante del 8 % de los nuevos ZEC a una reserva para futuras recompensas de minería.
El comité mantendría sus activos existentes y continuaría otorgando subvenciones con ellos. El cálculo de Bowe sitúa esos activos, después de las obligaciones pendientes de subvenciones, en aproximadamente 125 millones de dólares, utilizando un precio ilustrativo de ZEC de 1,300 dólares.
It's time to turn off the ZCG funding stream.
ZCG has over $125M in funding, and will receive millions more before the spigot is turned off. The program was never designed to handle this amount of funding.
Draft ZIP:https://t.co/GAkRBeplwO
— Sean Bowe (@ebfull) October 27, 2026
El comité de cinco miembros de ZCG, elegido por un panel asesor comunitario, selecciona las subvenciones sin una votación separada de los poseedores de monedas.
Un segundo programa de financiamiento recibe el 12 % de los ZEC recién creados. Los titulares votan trimestralmente sobre sus subvenciones, sujetas a requisitos de participación y aprobación.
Bowe desea preservar esa asignación mayor. Su propuesta sostiene que continuar acumulando fondos en los arreglos separados de custodia y gobernanza de ZCG añade riesgo cuando el programa ya cuenta con reservas sustanciales.
La asignación redirigida ingresaría al Mecanismo de Sostenibilidad de la Red, diseñado para respaldar las futuras recompensas de minería, y permanecería allí durante el resto del plazo existente del flujo de subvenciones.
El comité tablero mostró aproximadamente 91,453 ZEC y $8.8 millones, con $2.4 millones comprometidos a beneficiarios. Bowe valora el saldo restante en $125.3 millones utilizando un precio de ZEC de $1,300.
La asignación automática continúa independientemente de cuánto posea ya el comité. Al ritmo objetivo de la red, recibe aproximadamente 144 ZEC al día, con un valor de alrededor de 68 millones de dólares al año.
Para efectos de comparación, la Financial Privacy Foundation, que administra los fondos de ZCG, reportó un poco más de $1.5 millones en gastos de programas durante el primer trimestre. Anualizado, eso equivale a aproximadamente $6 millones, menos de una décima parte del ingreso anual.
Las cifras en dólares se mueven con ZEC. Incluso a 500 dólares por moneda, Bowe estima que el tesoro existente cubriría aproximadamente cinco años de gastos, asumiendo 10 millones de dólares al año.
El gasto en divulgación atrae escrutinio
La propuesta llegó en medio de críticas a un programa de divulgación financiado por ZCG que demostró pagos privados en una convención de la industria para adultos durante el fin de semana.
ZECsy, el equipo detrás del programa, solicitó $550,000 para trabajos que abarcan eventos de la industria para adultos, conferencias de criptomonedas y talleres. La propuesta incluía ayudar a los trabajadores que enfrentan restricciones bancarias a aceptar pagos sin exponer información financiera personal.
Day 2: Zcash at @EXXXOTICA . @rollergirlVi and @kate_stapes in Mama's zcash kitchen. Giving away protections for your body and your money. 
Privacy is ZECsy. pic.twitter.com/dkSY3GjhlC
— Mylo (@zReadyMouse) October 25, 2026
El comité aprobó la financiación inicial y los primeros nueve hitos, con un total de aproximadamente $461,500. Fotos de su stand en Exxxotica en Edison, Nueva Jersey, circularon en X el domingo.
Como tal, la aprobación de agosto fue dividida. La integrante del comité Hanh se opuso a la subvención, cuestionando su costo y la evidencia de una adopción duradera. Otros miembros respaldaron la capacidad del equipo para alcanzar nuevos usuarios, mientras que el límite de nueve meses permitió una evaluación antes de un financiamiento adicional.
El borrador de Bowe no menciona la subvención ZECsy, y se basa en las reservas del programa y en los flujos continuos.
La propuesta no tiene una fecha de activación y requeriría un cambio en las reglas de la red de Zcash. Pero hasta que una entre en vigor, la asignación de ZCG continúa en aproximadamente 144 ZEC diarios.

articles.title: Ripple recibe la aprobación final para lanzar su propio banco fiduciario nacional en EE.UU.
articles.text:
Ripple recibe la aprobación definitiva para lanzar su propio banco fiduciario nacional en EE. UU.
La Oficina del Contralor de la Moneda ha aprobado a Ripple National Trust Bank (RNTB), anunció el CEO de Ripple, Brad Garlinghouse, en X.
- La Oficina del Contralor de la Moneda ha aprobado a Ripple National Trust Bank, permitiendo que la empresa de criptomonedas opere un banco especializado bajo supervisión federal.
- El banco gestionará las reservas que respaldan la stablecoin RLUSD de Ripple y proporcionará servicios de custodia regulados para clientes institucionales, mientras que RLUSD seguirá siendo emitida por la unidad de Ripple regulada en Nueva York.
- RLUSD, lanzado en diciembre de 2024, ha crecido hasta alcanzar aproximadamente 2.500 millones de dólares en valor de mercado y cuenta con el respaldo de depósitos en dólares, valores gubernamentales estadounidenses y otros activos similares a efectivo.
Ripple, una empresa fintech que desarrolla blockchain y criptomonedas para transacciones transfronterizas y tokenización, ahora puede operar un banco especializado bajo la supervisión federal de EE. UU.
La Oficina del Contralor de la Moneda, el regulador que supervisa los bancos nacionales, ha aprobado a Ripple National Trust Bank (RNTB), el CEO de Ripple, Brad Garlinghouse anunció en X tarde del lunes.
En otras palabras, uno de los actores más importantes del criptomercado cuenta ahora con una licencia al estilo bancario tradicional, lo que señala que los activos digitales están siendo integrados cada vez más en el sistema financiero tradicional regulado. Ripple solicitó por primera vez la licencia bancaria en julio de 2025, y la OCC le otorgó una aprobación condicional ese diciembre antes de aprobarla completamente esta semana.
La aprobación es coherente con la propuesta de larga data de Garlinghouse de que las empresas de criptomonedas deben desarrollar productos que los bancos y las grandes instituciones puedan utilizar realmente.
“Durante años, hemos afirmado que las criptomonedas y los bancos funcionan mejor juntos. La aprobación final para Ripple National Trust Bank es lo que eso significa en la práctica,” dijo Garlinghouse en el comunicado de prensa. “Hemos pasado más de una década construyendo una infraestructura financiera regulada que las instituciones pueden realmente usar a gran escala. Una carta nacional de fideicomiso nos brinda una base aún más sólida para RLUSD y los productos institucionales que estamos desarrollando en pagos, custodia y mercados de capitales.”
El RNTB tendrá la responsabilidad de gestionar las reservas que respaldan la stablecoin RLUSD de Ripple. Estas reservas son esencialmente dinero real y activos que proporcionan valor al token.
El banco también actuará como fiduciario de estas reservas y ofrecerá servicios de custodia regulados, lo que significa que mantendrá de forma segura activos digitales para grandes empresas mientras utilizan criptomonedas en pagos, comercio y gestión de tesorería.
RLUSD seguirá siendo emitido por la unidad regulada por el estado de Nueva York de Ripple, Standard Custody & Trust Company. El nuevo banco añade otra capa de supervisión: RLUSD ahora cuenta con la vigilancia tanto de reguladores estatales como federales sobre partes de su estructura.
RLUSD debutó en diciembre de 2024 y desde entonces ha crecido hasta alcanzar un valor de mercado de aproximadamente 2.500 millones de dólares, posicionándose entre las 50 principales stablecoins del mundo. Se utiliza en el negocio de pagos de Ripple y como garantía en Ripple Prime. La stablecoin está respaldada por depósitos en dólares estadounidenses, valores gubernamentales de EE. UU. y otros activos líquidos. BNY posee la mayor parte de esas reservas. Ripple también utiliza XRP, el quinto activo digital más grande del mundo, para facilitar transacciones transfronterizas.
Ripple afirmó que continuará colaborando con la OCC, los reguladores de Nueva York y otros, a medida que el banco comience a operar, especialmente mientras Estados Unidos implementa sus nuevas normas sobre stablecoins bajo la Ley GENIUS.

articles.text:
VanEck launches diversified ETF combining stocks, bonds and Bitcoin exposure
VanEck’s new Wealth Builder ETF targets a 2% Bitcoin allocation, with a permitted range of 1% to 5%, gaining exposure through a spot Bitcoin ETP.
US asset manager VanEck has launched an actively managed exchange-traded fund (ETF) that combines stocks, bonds and real assets with a targeted allocation to Bitcoin.
According to Tuesday’s announcement, the VanEck Wealth Builder ETF (NYSE: WBMO) invests in both VanEck and third-party ETFs, with a target Bitcoin allocation of 2% and a permitted range of 1% to 5%, according to the company’s website. Bitcoin exposure comes through a spot Bitcoin ETP rather than direct holdings of the cryptocurrency.
The fund builds on VanEck’s existing Wealth Builder model portfolios, previously available to financial advisers through third-party wealth management platforms. Its strategy incorporates exposure to global equities, fixed income, gold and other real assets, with allocations managed and rebalanced by VanEck.
“The traditional 60/40 portfolio was built for a different investment landscape,” said David Schassler, VanEck’s head of multi-asset solutions.
He said adding real assets alongside stocks and bonds could help investors navigate a wider range of economic conditions.
The launch follows VanEck’s March partnership with retirement platform Basic Capital, which made a selection of the asset manager’s digital asset exchange-traded products available through US employer-sponsored 401(k) plans. VanEck managed about $244.1 billion in assets as of Sept. 30, according to the company.

articles.title: China's Stock Market Has Lost $2.4 Trillion as Investors Doubt Its AI Boom Will Ever Pay Off - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Stocks on China's mainland have lost about $2.4 trillion in market value since May, and the STAR 50 index of tech and chip companies is down 40% in under four months.
- AI companies make up 42% of the market value of Chinese shares and 57% of trading, per Goldman Sachs, while U.S. curbs now target Chinese robots and data center parts.
- Brent crude above $111 and 10-year Treasury yields near 5% are pressuring risk assets worldwide, with Bitcoin briefly under $80,000 ahead of the Fed's October 28 decision.
Stocks on China's mainland have lost about $2.4 trillion in market value, the total worth of all their shares, since May, as investors lose faith that Beijing's AI boom will ever turn a profit.
That is more than South Korea's entire economy produces in a year.
AI companies now make up 42% of the market value of Chinese shares listed on the mainland and in Hong Kong, and 57% of trading, according to Goldman Sachs. So when AI stocks fall, the whole market falls with them.
The CSI 300, an index of China's 300 biggest listed companies, entered a bear market on October 22, meaning a drop of at least 20% from its peak.
The sharpest damage hit Shanghai's STAR 50, an index of 50 large tech and chip companies. It fell 40% in less than four months, erasing about $480 billion.
It still trades at roughly 100 times earnings, a ratio that shows how many years of current profit investors are paying for, down from nearly 250 at its peak. The Nasdaq 100, the U.S. tech benchmark, sits around 30.
DeepSeek, a Chinese startup, released a cheap and powerful chatbot in January 2025, and Nvidia, the U.S. company whose chips power most AI, lost nearly $600 billion in market value in a single day. Moonshot AI's Kimi K3, also produced by a Chinese AI lab, sent chip stocks tumbling again in July.
Beijing then pushed its tech giants toward homegrown chips: According to the Financial Times, its internet regulator reportedly told companies including ByteDance and Alibaba to stop buying Nvidia chips in September 2025. Z.ai, a Beijing lab, says it trained its GLM-5.2 model entirely on Huawei chips.
Analysts blame weak spending by Chinese consumers and doubts that AI companies can earn back what they have invested. Robot maker Unitree drew retail orders for 8,000 times the shares on offer when it listed in August, and its stock has since lost almost half its value since launch even after a significant recovery this week.
“The stock market later evolved into a speculative crazy bull,” said Dong Baozhen, a Beijing-based fund manager. “And now we see the bubble bursting.”
The U.S. Federal Communications Commission banned imports of new foreign-made humanoid robots in July on national security grounds. Washington is also moving to ban Chinese-made optical parts from U.S. data centers, and the makers Zhongji Innolight and Eoptolink are down about 60% from their peaks.

articles.title: More Companies Join List to Those Objecting to OKX-ICE Tokenized Stock Plan
articles.text:
Intel, IBM, Oracle and IonQ latest to object to OKX-ICE tokenized stocks
More than 40% of the companies initially proposed to have their stocks listed in tokenized form have asked to opt-out.
Four companies have joined the list of those filing objections to listings on a tokenized stock exchange proposed by cryptocurrency exchange OKX and the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange, Intercontinental Exchange (ICE).
In a Monday update to its proposed OKXICE exchange, the crypto company reported that Intel, IBM, Oracle and IonQ were the most recent companies to object to having their US stocks listed in tokenized form. With the addition of the four, 26 companies have now filed to raise objections to OKXICE’s plans, including Alphabet, Wells Fargo and Goldman Sachs.
The proposed offering came just a few weeks after the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) approved temporary innovation exemptions for tokenized US stocks. Under the SEC exemption, Tokenized Securities Venues (TSVs) can offer limited trading for tokenized National Market System (NMS) stocks.
Many of the companies to opt out of the OKXICE plans currently have US listings on Nasdaq and the New York Stock Exchange. In September, Nasdaq released guidance for companies considering the innovation exemption, saying issuers should be “cautious” about participating. The exchange invested $100 million in Kraken parent Payward in September as part of its own push into tokenized assets.
OKXICE proposed 62 companies listing tokenized stocks when it filed with the SEC under the exemption, meaning about 41% of the entities have chosen not to participate as of Monday. Former New York Governor Andrew Cuomo, co-chair of the tokenization venture, said it was a “very natural response” for some companies to object, and he expected to see more names added to the list.
Related: Winners and losers of the SEC’s new tokenized stocks rules

articles.title: Robinhood Misses Q3 Earnings as Crypto Revenue Rises and Prediction Market Bets Grow - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Robinhood reported record third-quarter revenue of $1.42 billion, slightly below the roughly $1.43 billion expected, and earnings of $0.51 per share versus $0.55 expected.
- Event contracts revenue rose to $173 million from $156 million in the second quarter, and crypto revenue rose to $120 million from $100 million but fell 55% from a year earlier.
- Robinhood trimmed the top of its 2026 cost guidance to a range of $2.675 billion to $2.75 billion, and shares slipped in after-hours trading.
Robinhood, the trading app where more than 28 million people keep money to buy stocks and crypto and now bet on sports and elections, reported third-quarter revenue of $1.42 billion billion on Tuesday, missing the roughly $1.43 billion Wall Street expected
Earnings came in at $0.51 per share, missing the $0.55 analysts projected and down from $0.61 a year ago. Earnings per share is profit divided by the number of shares outstanding, and it is the figure investors use to call a quarter a beat or a miss.
Robinhood is the app that brought commission-free trading to a generation of first-time investors, which makes its quarterly report one of the clearest readings of what ordinary people are doing with their money. When customers trade more, deposit more or pile into new products, the shift shows up in these numbers.
Net income was $476 million, down 14% from $556 million a year earlier and 17% from $573 million in the second quarter. The quarter included a $67 million unrealized loss, meaning a drop in value on paper, on Robinhood Ventures Fund I, which cost $0.07 per share. Adjusted earnings per share, which exclude certain items, came to $0.60, down 3% from a year ago.
Event contracts, the yes-or-no bets that pay out $1 if a game, an election or an economic report goes a certain way, brought in $173 million, up from $156 million in the second quarter, when they overtook crypto revenue for the first time. Customers traded a record 16.4 billion of them, more than seven times a year earlier.
“I believe we’re at the very beginning of a prediction market supercycle,” CEO Vlad Tenev said in December last year, when Robinhood added NFL player contracts and parlay-style combos that pay only if every outcome hits.
Crypto trading revenue rose to $120 million from $100 million in the second quarter, but remained down 55% from the $268 million Robinhood earned in the third quarter of 2025. Customers traded $50 billion in crypto during the quarter, down 38% from a year earlier, with $21 billion on the Robinhood app and $29 billion through Bitstamp, the crypto exchange it acquired
Robinhood Chain went live on July 1 as a layer-2 network, meaning a blockchain that runs on top of Ethereum to make transactions cheaper and faster. Its first weeks were driven by meme coins, joke-themed tokens, rather than the tokenized stocks it was built for, which are digital versions of company shares that trade on a blockchain.
By the end of August the chain had earned about $3.13 million in fees over 30 days, more than Ethereum and Base, which came in at $2.47 million and $2.89 million.
Hours before the report, Robinhood announced a deal with Ripple that brings RLUSD, a stablecoin (a crypto token designed to stay worth one dollar), to Robinhood Chain and Bitstamp, with an in-app rollout planned later this year. RLUSD has a market value above $2.5 billion, and Ripple will also supply Robinhood’s treasury software and lending for Bitstamp traders.
Robinhood shares closed Tuesday at about $94.61 and slipped in after-hours trading- The stock is down roughly 18% this year and about 37% below its 52-week high of $150.47.
Robinhood narrowed its 2026 outlook for adjusted operating expenses and stock-based pay to $2.675 billion to $2.75 billion, trimming the top of the $2.675 billion to $2.775 billion range it set in July.

articles.title: Stacks Founder Warns of Bitcoin’s Quantum Security Timeline
articles.text:
Quantum fears already limiting Bitcoin’s growth, Stacks founder says
Speaking on Cointelegraph’s Chain Reaction podcast, Muneeb Ali warned that uncertainty over Bitcoin’s quantum security could deter institutional investors.
Concerns about quantum computing are slowing institutional investment in Bitcoin, according to Stacks founder Muneeb Ali, who warned that the network needs a credible roadmap for security upgrades to restore investor confidence.
“There is already a ceiling on the growth of Bitcoin because of quantum fears,” Ali said during an interview on Cointelegraph’s Chain Reaction podcast. He argued that uncertainty could lead risk-averse institutional investors to delay large Bitcoin purchases until developers establish a credible path toward quantum-resistant security.
Stacks is a Bitcoin layer-2 network designed to bring smart contracts and decentralized applications to Bitcoin. Ali co-founded the project, which uses Bitcoin as its underlying settlement layer.
Chain Reaction Podcast. Source: Cointelegraph
Ali warned that Bitcoin could enter a riskier period if developers fail to make meaningful progress toward quantum-resistant security by 2028. He said upgrades typically take years to implement, with additional time needed for users to move their holdings to new addresses.
Ali pointed to 2030 as a target for transitioning to quantum-resistant security, citing guidance from the US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). He suggested advances in artificial intelligence could accelerate the development of quantum computers, potentially bringing that timeline forward to 2029.
Ali acknowledged that some Bitcoin proponents believe the quantum computing threat remains distant and concerns are overblown. He argued, however, that disagreements over the urgency of the threat could themselves undermine investor confidence, particularly without a credible upgrade roadmap.
Related: Justin Sun says Tron’s post-quantum cryptography has gone live on testnet
Bitcoin’s quantum security debate
Despite his concerns, Ali said a sufficiently powerful quantum computer would more likely emerge from a major research laboratory than an unknown attacker. He suggested companies such as Google or Microsoft would have little incentive to use the technology to steal Bitcoin, given the potential legal consequences.
Ali also said a quantum security threat to Bitcoin would affect the broader cryptocurrency industry, even projects developing their own protections. “If Bitcoin gets hit, everyone gets hit downstream as well,” he said.
Meanwhile, developers are exploring ways to protect Bitcoin against quantum attacks. In September, StarkWare reported that researchers had reduced the estimated computing cost of preparing an experimental quantum-resistant Bitcoin transaction by 79%, following a weeklong optimization challenge.
The approach requires no changes to Bitcoin’s consensus rules, but the latest cost reductions have been demonstrated only in benchmark tests. StarkWare has described the technology as a last-resort measure and continues to advocate for a protocol-level upgrade as a longer-term solution.

articles.title: Robinhood Taps Ripple's Stablecoin, Treasury Software and Trading Loans - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin went live Tuesday on Robinhood Chain and Bitstamp, and is expected to reach the main Robinhood app later this year.
- Robinhood will adopt Ripple Treasury to run its global cash operations and will use RLUSD on the XRP Ledger for institutional settlement at Bitstamp.
- Ripple Prime already provides Bitstamp with lending across roughly 20 digital assets and is set to add perpetual futures trading there later this year.
Robinhood, the trading app with 28.6 million funded customers, is adding a digital dollar built by Ripple, the company whose founders created the XRP cryptocurrency. Ripple's RLUSD token went live Tuesday on Robinhood's own blockchain and on its Bitstamp exchange, and is expected to reach the main Robinhood app later this year, according to Ripple's announcement.
RLUSD is a stablecoin, a crypto token designed to always be worth one U.S. dollar, which lets money move across a blockchain without waiting for banks to open. It launched in December 2024, and Ripple said its market capitalization, meaning the combined value of every token in circulation, now tops $2.5 billion.
Robinhood will also run its global treasury operations on Ripple Treasury, software that manages a company's cash, from payments to cash-flow forecasts and risk. That includes intercompany netting, which offsets what a company's own divisions owe one another so fewer payments have to move.
Ripple Prime, a prime broker that lends money and clears trades for hedge funds and other large institutions, already provides Bitstamp with lending and margin financing, meaning borrowed money for trading, across roughly 20 digital assets. Ripple paid $1.25 billion for the firm in a deal announced in April 2025, when it was still called Hidden Road.
Ripple Prime clients also get access to spot trading on Bitstamp, which means buying at the current market price, and later this year Prime will support perpetual futures there, contracts that bet on a coin's future price and never expire. Robinhood closed its purchase of Bitstamp, one of the world's longest-running crypto exchanges, in June 2025 for about $200 million, and most of the exchange's volume comes from institutions.
Robinhood will use RLUSD on the XRP Ledger, the blockchain behind XRP, for institutional settlement, the step where a large trade is finalized and paid for, across Bitstamp's institutional business.
“Utility is what moves stablecoins forward. Working with Ripple, Bitstamp and Robinhood will have access to RLUSD for institutional settlement, Ripple Treasury for our operations, and Ripple Prime for financing,” said Johann Kerbrat, senior vice president and general manager of Robinhood Crypto and International. “That is what a connected, global financial system looks like.”
Robinhood, which pared back its crypto listings during the SEC crackdown on Ripple and other crypto companies, added XRP for U.S. customers in November 2024. Now Ripple's software will help run Robinhood's own treasury department.
Robinhood cut about 10% of its staff in June, after revenue fell 34% in its crypto transaction business in the first quarter to $134 million. It will report its third-quarter results after the market closes on Tuesday, the first report to cover a full quarter since the July 1 launch of Robinhood Chain.

articles.title: Ripple Unveils Robinhood, BNY and C2FO Deals at Swell 2026
articles.text:
Ripple, Robinhood expand partnership to bring RLUSD to retail and institutional markets
Ripple also expanded its collaboration with BNY on digital asset custody and partnered with C2FO to bring trade finance settlement onto the XRP Ledger.
Ripple and Robinhood have expanded their partnership to bring the RLUSD stablecoin to Robinhood’s retail and institutional businesses, alongside new integrations spanning treasury management, lending and trading services.
RLUSD is already available on Robinhood Chain and Bitstamp by Robinhood, with a launch in the Robinhood app planned for later this year, according to a Tuesday announcement coinciding with Ripple’s Swell 2026 conference in New York. Robinhood also plans to use the stablecoin on the XRP Ledger for institutional settlement.
Robinhood will also adopt Ripple Treasury to manage its global cash and liquidity operations, including payment processing, cash flow forecasting and intercompany transactions. The integration extends the partnership beyond customer-facing services to Robinhood’s internal financial infrastructure.
The partnership also expands Robinhood’s existing relationship with Ripple Prime, which provides financing services to Bitstamp by Robinhood and plans to introduce perpetual futures trading on the exchange later this year.
Launched in December 2024, RLUSD has reached a market capitalization of $2.57 billion, with nearly $1 billion issued on the XRP Ledger, according to DeFiLlama data. Robinhood reported 28.6 million funded customers globally as of August, offering a potentially significant distribution channel for the stablecoin.
Related: Majority of Americans want candidates who support US-based financial technology: Poll
Ripple expands into custody and trade finance
Ripple also announced on Tuesday an expanded partnership with financial services giant BNY, which now supports custody of XRP and RLUSD through its Digital Asset Custody platform. The companies plan to work together to allow BNY clients to mint and redeem RLUSD directly through the bank and broaden support for tokenized assets issued on the XRP Ledger.
Separately, Ripple partnered with working-capital platform C2FO to bring financing and settlement for its new Instant Pay service onto the XRP Ledger, using RLUSD. The service is designed to let suppliers receive payments against approved invoices in seconds rather than waiting days for traditional bank settlement.
A C2FO spokesperson told Cointelegraph the service is currently in testing, with a controlled launch and the first RLUSD transactions on the XRP Ledger expected by the end of the year.
The string of announcements on Tuesday followed Ripple’s receipt of final approval from the US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency on Monday to establish a national trust bank. The institution will manage reserves backing RLUSD and provide digital asset custody services, while stablecoin issuance will remain with Ripple’s New York-regulated subsidiary.

articles.title: Anchorage Positions Itself as Custody Backbone of US-Mexico Stablecoin Corridor - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Anchorage Digital expanded a custody-and-listing arrangement with Bitso covering both sides of the US-Mexico corridor.
- The deal targets the US-Mexico remittance corridor, one of the world’s largest, which moves tens of billions yearly.
- It extends a Latin America stablecoin race, including Circle’s recent Colombia settlement pilot.
Anchorage Digital is planting itself at the center of one of the world’s largest money-transfer routes, expanding a custody-and-listing arrangement with Latin American crypto platform Bitso to hold the stablecoins moving between the United States and Mexico.
Announced Tuesday, the deal puts Anchorage Digital Bank’s custody beneath both sides of the corridor. MXNB, Bitso’s Mexican peso stablecoin, is now custodied by the federally chartered crypto bank across six blockchains: Arbitrum, Base, Ethereum, Polygon, Avalanche, and Arc.
In turn, Bitso has listed USDPT and USAT, the U.S. dollar stablecoins from Western Union and Tether, both of which Anchorage issues and custodies. The companies did not disclose financial terms.
The target is the U.S.-Mexico remittance corridor, which moves tens of billions of dollars a year and ranks among the biggest cross-border payment flows on earth. Much of that money still travels over correspondent banking, wire transfers and cash-pickup networks that are slow and costly, while about 15% already runs through Bitso’s infrastructure.
Anchorage is betting that stablecoins, which settle onchain in seconds around the clock, will increasingly replace those legacy rails, and that doing so requires custody that is regulated and sits wherever the liquidity is.
“The US-Mexico corridor is where stablecoins stop being a thesis and start moving real money at scale,” said Nathan McCauley, Anchorage’s CEO and co-founder, arguing the firm is now “the institutional custody layer on both sides of that flow.” Ben Reid, Bitso’s head of stablecoin, said clients can now access the full dollar-peso corridor fully onchain, backed by a federally chartered bank.
The move extends a broader race to wire stablecoins into Latin America’s payments plumbing. Circle recently pushed deeper into the region with a USDC settlement pilot in Colombia, part of a wider expansion into dozens of emerging markets as stablecoins go mainstream.
For Anchorage, the deal builds on its deepening stablecoin footprint. The bank issues Tether’s U.S.-regulated USAT stablecoin, while Bitso has been pushing its MXNB peso coin across networks like Arbitrum. By anchoring both ends of the corridor, Anchorage is aiming to become the default custodian for any issuer or bank entering the route.

articles.title: AI Agents Are Creating a New Layer of Cybersecurity Spending - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Akamai launched Agent Sandbox and Akamai Inference in beta on Oct. 27, adding WebAssembly-based isolation for code that AI agents write and run.
- A 2026 Palo Alto Networks survey of 2,930 security leaders found 109 machine identities per human, 79 of them AI agents.
- Palo Alto, Cisco, CrowdStrike, Okta and Zscaler have all bought or launched AI-agent security products this year.
AI-focused cloud service provider Akamai launched a sandbox for AI agents on Tuesday, a sealed environment where code an agent writes can run without touching the rest of a company's systems. Agent Sandbox is in beta, alongside Akamai Inference, a service for running open AI models on Akamai's cloud.
The launch may be small but the problem behind it is not. Software is no longer just answering questions—it logs into accounts, writes code, moves money and acts on its own, and every one of those powers is something a hacker, or the software itself, can abuse.
This is what’s known as agentic AI, and it’s taking over the internet. A 2026 Palo Alto Networks survey of 2,930 security leaders found an average of 109 machine identities for every human, the logins and keys software uses to access other software. Of those, 79 are AI agents.
Agentic AI comes with a lot of perks, but also some serious dangers, especially when those agents have too much freedom, or are so intelligent they can bypass their own restrictions.
For example, Hugging Face, a major hub for open AI models, disclosed an intrusion on July 16, and OpenAI confirmed five days later that its own models were responsible. The research group METR later investigated the incident and found about 1,200 OpenAI agents had coordinated on a hidden message board, with roughly 700 joining the attack.
Turns out the agents escaped their sandbox and chained a previously unknown software flaw with stolen credentials to reach live systems. OpenAI called it a "warning shot." It said a monitor that reads a model's written reasoning was not running during the tests.
In simple terms, AI safety usually ends up being a tug of war game between alignment (the guys in charge of making sure AI is safe) and development (the guys in charge of making sure AI is powerful), with each team wanting the other to play a minor role in order to secure its own goals.
That is what Akamai wants to treat. “Enterprises should not have to choose between speed and control when they put AI into production,” Jon Alexander, Senior Vice President of Cloud Technology at Akamai said in a press release.
“Some teams want to ship an AI feature this quarter on a managed platform. Others need dedicated GPUs to run frontier-class open models on their own terms. Every team running agents needs a boundary around the code those agents write,” he said.
Hijacking is another fear. In July, Zscaler found web pages hiding instructions meant for AI agents, a trick called indirect prompt injection. One fake documentation page told agents to pay a $3 "license fee" in about 0.0012 Ethereum to a hardcoded wallet, and four of the 26 models Zscaler tested complied.
Back in May cybersecurity firm Bugcrowd saw submissions more than quadruple in three weeks in March, most of them fake. HackerOne and Nextcloud suspended paid programs in April.
The machines also find real bugs. Mozilla said an early version of Anthropic's Claude Mythos helped find 271 vulnerabilities in Firefox, all patched within the week. That flood of real and fake findings is what security companies are now racing to manage.
Palo Alto closed its CyberArk purchase on Feb. 11 to extend privileged-access controls to AI agents. In April it bought Koi, which secures AI coding agents running on employee machines. Cisco announced a planned acquisition of Astrix Security in May, a firm that governs the keys and tokens agents use, and completed the deal June 29.
Akamai's piece is the fence around the code itself. Its sandbox uses WebAssembly, a format that runs programs in a tightly walled box, to cap an agent's computing power, memory and outbound connections. Akamai's Alexander said every team running agents "needs a boundary around the code those agents write."
Palo Alto's survey found organizations expect AI agents to grow 85% over the next 12 months, against 56% for human identities.

articles.title: Crypto Today: USDC Tops USDT in Europe, Binance Files in Brazil, Ripple Wins Approval
articles.text:
Here’s what happened in crypto today
Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
Today in crypto, Circle’s USDC overtook Tether’s USDT in euro stablecoin trading as EU regulations reshaped local markets, Binance applied for a crypto license in Brazil ahead of an Oct. 30 deadline and Ripple secured final US regulatory approval to establish a national trust bank.
USDC overtakes USDT in euro trading as MiCA reshapes stablecoin market
Circle’s USDC has overtaken Tether’s USDt in stablecoin trading against the euro, capturing 56% of the market as European exchanges adjust to the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA), according to Kaiko.
In a new report, Kaiko said USDC’s share has surged from just 10% in January 2024, with the shift accelerating after major exchanges restricted USDT trading for customers in the European Economic Area.
USDC has also gained a liquidity advantage, with euro trading order books now roughly 40% deeper than USDT’s. However, Tether remains the dominant stablecoin globally, with a circulating supply approximately 2.5 times larger than USDC’s.
The findings follow the European Banking Authority’s decision to classify USDC as the EU’s first significant e-money token under MiCA, placing it under direct regulatory supervision.
Kaiko suggested a similar shift could emerge in the United States as regulators implement the GENIUS Act. The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency recently finalized reserve and redemption requirements for supervised stablecoin issuers, effective January 2027.
Further restrictions on noncompliant stablecoins are scheduled for July 2028, potentially benefiting Circle while Tether pursues the US market through its separately regulated USAT stablecoin.
Binance files for Brazil crypto license ahead of Friday deadline
Binance has applied for a cryptocurrency service provider license in Brazil, seeking to maintain its operations in one of Latin America’s largest crypto markets ahead of a regulatory deadline on Friday, Oct. 30.
The exchange submitted its application to the Central Bank of Brazil on Friday, Oct. 23, through its local entity, BBrasil, according to a statement shared with Cointelegraph.
The company said the filing would allow Brazilian users to continue accessing crypto assets, stablecoin trading, payments and investment services.
Binance has also announced changes for Brazilian users effective Tuesday, including restrictions on crypto lending, margin trading and other services. The exchange is also delisting 22 crypto assets in the country.
Brazil requires existing crypto service providers to submit authorization applications by Oct. 30 to continue operating under transitional arrangements. Filing an application does not constitute regulatory approval.
Ripple wins final US approval for national trust bank
Ripple announced Monday that its national trust bank has secured final approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC).
The approval completes the chartering process for Ripple National Trust Bank (RNTB), which received conditional approval from the OCC in December 2025.
The federally supervised trust bank is authorized to manage reserves backing Ripple USD (RLUSD), act as collateral trustee for the benefit of RLUSD holders and provide digital asset custody services, according to Ripple.
RLUSD will continue to be issued by Standard Custody & Trust Company, Ripple’s limited purpose trust company regulated by the New York Department of Financial Services.
“We’ve always said crypto and banks work better together — this is what that looks like. Real innovation, real accountability, federal oversight,” Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse said on X on Monday.

articles.title: Intel, Oracle, IBM Join Objections to OKX-ICE Tokenized Stock Venue, Bringing Total to 26 - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Intel, Oracle, IBM and IonQ joined the list of companies objecting to trading of their shares on OKXICE TSV, according to its Oct. 26 notice.
- The total has climbed from nine on Oct. 15 to 26, though the notices don’t explain the objections or their effect.
- The notice says it’s uncertain whether tokenized shares in self-custodied wallets would be protected by SIPC if the tokenizer’s broker-dealer failed.
The tech sector’s resistance to tokenized stocks keeps building.
Intel, Oracle, IBM, and quantum computing firm IonQ are the latest companies to object to having their shares traded on OKXICE TSV, according to an updated public notice from the venue dated Monday.
The planned platform, a 50-50 joint venture between NYSE owner Intercontinental Exchange and OKX’s U.S. holding company, now lists 26 objecting issuers.
That’s up from 22 in its Oct. 23 notice, which added Wells Fargo, Cisco, and Marvell. The tally stood at 16 on Oct. 19 and nine on Oct. 15, when the first batch included Verizon, Broadcom and UnitedHealth Group. In less than two weeks, the list has nearly tripled.
Technology companies dominate the roster. Microsoft, Alphabet, Broadcom, Qualcomm, Arm, Cisco, and now Intel and Oracle have all objected, along with banks Goldman Sachs and Wells Fargo.
IBM and IonQ add two quantum computing players. As before, the notices don’t explain the companies’ reasons or what an objection means for whether a stock can trade on the platform.
OKXICE TSV plans to let approved users trade tokenized U.S. stocks 24/7 through permissioned Uniswap v4 liquidity pools on OKX’s XLayer blockchain, paired with stablecoins such as USDC.
Users must pass identity and sanctions checks and hold a nontransferable “soulbound” token to trade. The venue is set to operate under the SEC’s innovation exemption, which the agency unveiled in September after the Clarity Act stalled in the Senate.
The latest notice highlights a key risk for investors. Each token represents a claim on a real share held by a third-party “tokenizer” through a registered broker-dealer. If that broker-dealer failed, the notice says, it’s uncertain whether tokenized shares in a self-custodied wallet would count as customer property or be covered by the Securities Investor Protection Corporation, which protects brokerage customers when firms fail.
The notice also says trades must be fully funded, with no margin or borrowing. Liquidity providers don’t have to be registered market makers and can pull their liquidity at any time.
OKX and ICE first teamed up on tokenized securities earlier this year before unveiling plans for the venue this month.

articles.title: CFTC Files Lawsuit Against Utah Over Prediction Markets
articles.text:
CFTC sues Utah to block action against prediction markets
The US state filed a lawsuit against Kalshi last week, seeking to recover up to $60 million in profits related to event contracts on prediction markets.
The US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) announced legal action against Utah officials after the state’s attorney general said he would sue to compel Kalshi and its affiliates to return up to $60 million in profits allegedly obtained illegally.
In a Monday filing in the US District Court for the District of Utah, lawyers for the commodities regulator sued the State of Utah and its Attorney General Derek Brown a week after officials announced legal action against prediction market platform Kalshi and its affiliates over allegedly illegal betting.
According to the CFTC, Utah was attempting to bypass congressional intent to “federally preempt state law” by “restrict[ing] the functioning of CFTC-registered exchanges.” CFTC Chair Michael Selig has been claiming for months that the regulator has “exclusive jurisdiction” over prediction markets, leading to several lawsuits between state and federal authorities.
“The event contracts targeted by Utah are ‘swaps’ under the federal [Commodity Exchange Act], and the exchanges that offer these event contracts for trading are CFTC-regulated Designated Contract Markets [DCMs],” said the lawsuit. “Utah’s efforts to prevent a CFTC-regulated DCM from offering CFTC-approved financial products intrude on the exclusive federal scheme Congress designed to oversee United States commodity derivatives markets.”
Kalshi spokesperson Jacki McGavick told Cointelegraph in response to the Utah lawsuit:
“As a national derivatives market overseen by the CFTC, Kalshi answers to federal law, and no single state should have a veto over it.“
The case is another dispute between federal and state authorities over prediction markets that may be resolved only by a Supreme Court decision. In September, New Jersey officials petitioned the high court to weigh in on their case against Kalshi, similar to other lawsuits pending in Michigan, Ohio, Kentucky, Nevada, Massachusetts, Wisconsin and New York. As of Tuesday, the Supreme Court has not announced whether it will hear arguments in the case.
Related: NBA names Kalshi, Polymarket preferred exchanges, signs CFTC deal

articles.title: Bitcoin Wallet Maker Keystone Pulls Devices as Stolen Key Opens Door to Fakes - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Keystone will destroy 18,835 unsold hardware wallets and has suspended shipping after an attacker obtained the permanent factory key used to verify its devices are genuine.
- The breach, detected October 20, also affected 25,964 buyer records from Keystone's Shopify store, covering 2024 to 2026 and including names, contact details and shipping addresses.
- Keystone says recovery phrases and private keys were not involved, and that devices delivered before October 20 are unaffected.
Keystone, a maker of Bitcoin hardware wallets that keep the secret codes controlling your crypto offline, said Monday it will destroy 18,835 unsold devices after attackers obtained the key that proves its hardware is genuine. The company has also suspended shipping of all unshipped orders from its website.
For buyers, the risk is a counterfeit wallet that looks brand new and passes Keystone’s own verification check, because the attacker obtained the key that the check relies on. A criminal could then sell such a device to someone who loads real savings onto it.
“If it is exposed, an attacker could use it to produce counterfeit devices that pass authentication checks,” Keystone said in its statement. “These devices could then be sold or shipped to customers, who might unknowingly use them as genuine products, potentially resulting in asset theft.”
Keystone calls it a WebAuth key, a secret code written into each device at the factory so a page on the company’s website can confirm the hardware is real. It cannot be erased or rewritten, and the 18,835 units in inventory that carry it are being destroyed rather than sold.
Keystone first said Saturday that a third party had obtained customer shipping information. Monday’s statement added the stolen key and a count of 25,964 affected buyer records, but it does not say who is responsible or when the attacker first got in.
The incident affected records from Keystone’s Shopify store, the e-commerce platform that handled its online sales. Keystone says 51,083 buyer records were involved, but 25,119 had already had their personal information erased, leaving 25,964 from 2024 to 2026 that still held names, contact details, shipping addresses and order information. Purchases through Amazon and other channels were not affected.
Some of that data should already have been deleted. Keystone’s policy was to erase buyer records after 180 days, and the automated bulk-deletion tool it built for the job did not work reliably.
“Some erasure tasks failed, and we did not detect and address these failures in time, resulting in certain personal information being retained beyond the permitted period,” Keystone said. “We failed to fulfill our commitment to erase customer data on time, and we accept responsibility for this failure.”
Customer lists are a recurring weak point for wallet makers. Ledger’s 2020 leak eventually reached about 292,000 customers, and those who received phishing emails afterward worried they could become targets of home invasions.
— Keystone Hardware Wallet (@KeystoneWallet) October 26, 2026
Trezor and SafePal each disclosed customer-data breaches in August, affecting 13,689 customers and about 39,798 customers, respectively.
Names and addresses matter because of wrench attacks, in which criminals use threats or violence to force owners to hand over their crypto. Chainalysis counted 46 violent attacks in the first half of 2026, with more than $30 million stolen.
The manufacturer also warned of scammers offering “asset migration,” “wallet verification” or “investigation assistance.”
“We will not ask you to return your device,” the company said. “Anyone contacting you under the pretext of a ‘recall’ and asking you to ship your device to them should be treated as a scammer.”
Sales on Keystone’s website will switch to preorders until production of devices with a new key is complete, and the company says it has submitted reports to authorities in the EU, UK, and other jurisdictions.
Keystone cut its retention period for customer data from 180 days to 90 and asked Shopify on October 24 to erase all overdue buyer data, a process with a 10-day waiting period. The company expects the erasure to finish on November 3.

articles.title: Ipsos Poll Finds More Americans Support FinTech Not Tied To Crypto
articles.text:
Majority of Americans want candidates who support US-based financial technology: Poll
The September survey offered a possible window into US voters who could consider fintech and digital asset policies on Election Day.
A new poll from the DeFi Education Fund and Ipsos found that 72% of people surveyed said it was “somewhat” to “extremely” important for politicians to be supportive of policies encouraging financial technology built in the US.
On Tuesday, Ipsos released the results of a poll of 1,545 people conducted in September, showing that 35% of respondents said it was “very” or “extremely” important for political candidates to support the idea of “ensuring that those who are building the next generation of financial technology are encouraged to do so in the United States.” An additional 37% of those surveyed said that the fintech policy was “somewhat important.”
Notably, only 9% of the Ipsos poll respondents said that they were familiar with crypto, and 5% with stablecoins. A majority, 87%, said that they had not held any digital assets in the previous 12 months. Only 13% said it was “very” or “extremely” important for a political candidate to encourage growth in blockchain, crypto, and DeFi.
“Ownership of crypto and openness to DeFi are largely consistent with 2025, and interest looks consistent across party lines,” said Ipsos.
The poll was conducted about two months before Americans were set to vote on the next session of Congress in the 2026 midterm elections, in which crypto policies and laws could be a factor at the polling stations. Political action committees backed by crypto companies have already spent tens of millions of dollars in an attempt to influence voters in key races.
Related: Ripple wins final US approval for national trust bank

articles.title: Circle Pushes Deeper Into Latin America With USDC Settlement in Colombia - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Circle has tapped ACI Worldwide to integrate USDC settlement into existing banking infrastructure across Latin America, starting with a pilot in Colombia built on ACI’s Bre-B instant-payments system.
- The effort pairs Circle’s USDC with ACI’s Connetic orchestration platform to show banks how stablecoin settlement can run alongside traditional rails.
- It extends Circle’s regional push into dozens of emerging markets and an earlier USDC foothold via Mercado Pago.
Circle is extending its reach across Latin America, teaming up with payments-technology firm ACI Worldwide to fold USDC settlement into the region’s existing banking rails, starting with a pilot in Colombia.
Announced Tuesday, the collaboration pairs Circle’s USDC infrastructure with ACI Connetic, ACI’s cloud-based payments orchestration platform, to show financial institutions how stablecoin settlement can run alongside traditional payment systems rather than replace them.
The initial focus is Colombia, where ACI built the central infrastructure behind Bre-B, the country’s interoperable instant-payments network. The idea is to test how a digital dollar like USDC can slot into that real-time, account-to-account system to create what the companies call a multi-rail ecosystem.
The framing reflects a shift in how banks are approaching stablecoins. Rather than debating the technology itself, institutions increasingly want to know how digital dollars fit into the treasury operations, governance and settlement processes they already run.
“The conversation around stablecoins is moving from possibility to practicality,” said Craig Ramsey, ACI’s global head of account-to-account payments, describing the effort as a way to integrate regulated stablecoins into workflows banks already trust.
Kash Razzaghi, Circle’s chief commercial officer, said financial institutions across Latin America are increasingly looking at how stablecoins can support the evolution of payments “within the infrastructure they already use,” framing USDC as a bridge between traditional finance and the digital economy.
The move builds on Circle’s steady regional expansion. The company has pushed into dozens of emerging markets as stablecoins go mainstream, and earlier gained a Latin American foothold when Argentina’s Mercado Pago added USDC.
Colombia is a logical next target, given high cross-border remittance volumes and a population well-acquainted with dollar-denominated savings as a hedge against inflation.
Circle positioned the pilot as technology-agnostic: while it runs on USDC, ACI’s platform is built to support other payment networks and digital-asset providers over time. For Circle, the deal is another step in weaving its stablecoin into the plumbing of mainstream finance, this time in a fast-growing payments market where instant-payment adoption is already accelerating.

articles.title: Stellar Gains Nasdaq-100 Fund as Tokenization Expands
articles.text:
Janus Henderson, Centrifuge launch tokenized Nasdaq-100 fund on Stellar
The blockchain-based fund offers eligible non-US investors exposure to the Nasdaq-100 as Janus Henderson expands its institutional tokenization business.
Asset manager Janus Henderson and tokenization platform Centrifuge have launched a blockchain-based fund tracking the Nasdaq-100 Index on Stellar, offering eligible investors outside the United States exposure to the benchmark.
Called JQQQ, the fund uses Centrifuge’s tokenization infrastructure and seeks to track the Nasdaq-100 under a licensing agreement with the exchange, according to a Tuesday announcement.
The launch expands Janus Henderson’s onchain investment offerings beyond US Treasurys and structured credit into equity-index exposure. The asset manager said its institutional onchain strategies now exceed $1 billion.
JQQQ is structured as a segregated portfolio of a British Virgin Islands investment company and provides indirect exposure to the Nasdaq-100 rather than ownership of the underlying stocks. The fund targets eligible professional investors outside the US, according to the Wall Street Journal, which reported a minimum investment of $100,000.
The launch follows Nasdaq’s decision in April to expand licensing of its Nasdaq-100 Index to additional asset managers, including BlackRock and State Street, while maintaining its longstanding partnership with Invesco, which operates the $499 billion market cap Invesco QQQ Trust exchange-traded fund.
Related: US Bank tests proprietary stablecoin in cross-border Stellar transaction
Stellar expands institutional tokenization footprint
The Janus Henderson launch expands Stellar’s growing tokenization business. The Layer-1 blockchain currently ranks fourth among blockchains by distributed real-world asset value, with approximately $3.8 billion in tokenized assets, behind Ethereum, BNB Chain and Solana, according to RWA.xyz.
The network hosts tokenized assets from major issuers including Spiko, Franklin Templeton and Ondo. In July, tokenization platform Tradable announced plans to bring up to $1 billion in private credit assets to Stellar, with $500 million expected at launch.
Stellar is also part of a planned expansion by the Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC), which announced in May that it would connect its tokenization service to the network. DTCC-tokenized assets are expected to become available in the first half of 2027, potentially including US Treasurys, major index ETFs and Russell 1000 stocks.
Despite the expansion of Stellar’s tokenized asset market, its native token, XLM, has fallen about 16% year to date, trading near $0.17 on Tuesday, according to CoinGecko data.

articles.title: A $3M Hedge, a Midterm Test and Retail's Rise: Prediction Markets at NEXTPredict - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- NEXTPredict brought prediction market exchanges, trading firms and policymakers together in New York on October 22 and 23, less than two weeks before the U.S. midterms.
- Chuck Todd, who moderated a panel pitting polls against markets, said he was "bullish on prediction markets for the future of journalism."
- Executives from Kalshi, Polymarket and Robinhood pointed to hedging, financial contracts and regulation as the next frontiers beyond elections and sports.
Prediction markets spent two days in the spotlight at NEXTPredict, which brought the industry's biggest exchanges, trading firms and policymakers to Convene Hudson Yards in New York on October 22 and 23.
With the U.S. midterms less than two weeks away, elections dominated the conversation, but executives were just as keen to talk about what comes next.
The hedge that lost
The conference opened with a trade that didn't pay out. NEXTPredict had paid a $12,000 premium on Kalshi for contracts that would have returned around $3 million if more than half of scheduled arrivals at New York's JFK airport were cancelled the day before the event.
"We ended up losing that trade yesterday, right?" NEXTPredict co-founder Pierre Lindh said on Thursday's "Hedging the Unhedgeable" panel. "And I can only say I'm very happy that we lost that trade, because that means we're all here today."
Traditional event insurance covers cancellation, Lindh explained, but "most of these type of force majeure situations won't cancel the event. It will severely damage the event."
Joe Grubb, head of business development at Susquehanna, which took the other side of the trade, said the firm modeled the risk in-house in about a day or two. "It's sort of in our DNA at Susquehanna to price strange things," he said.
Kalshi's director of business development, Nicolas Hull, said small businesses were now hedging on the exchange, starting with a New York bar that covered a Knicks playoff promotion. As long as a contract is certified with the CFTC and has a verifiable data source, "we can list almost anything on our exchange," he said.
This is the team behind NEXTPredict Summit New York.
Months of planning. More late nights than we'll admit. And then, last week, it all came together at Convene, 30 Hudson Yards.
2,000+ of you in the room. 180 speakers. 47 countries. Two weeks before the midterms, the… pic.twitter.com/KCA9TpDCV4
— NEXTpredict (@nextpredictio) October 26, 2026
Chuck Todd and the midterms
Todd, the former NBC News political director, had told Lindh before the event that he was "open minded" about whether markets or pollsters would call the midterms better. By Friday's "Who Calls the Midterms" panel, he sounded closer to a convert.
"This is my argument of why I'm bullish on prediction markets for the future of journalism and that it should be this, in its own way, a fact checker," Todd said. "With money being involved, there's more incentive to get it right."
He argued that prediction markets have effectively replaced exit polls on election night, but pushed back on the idea that polling is broken. "You can still do a good poll. It just costs a lot," he said.
His panelists were more cautious. "Speed is not necessarily the same as accuracy," said Columbia University professor Rajiv Sethi, while PredictIt CEO John Phillips reminded the audience that "it's called wisdom of crowds, not wisdom of whales."
That caution looked well placed days later. Before Brazil's presidential runoff on Sunday, Polymarket gave Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva only about a 20% chance of beating Flávio Bolsonaro, but he went on to win a fourth term, Decrypt reported. Experts blamed Brazil's ban on prediction markets, which left the odds largely to traders outside the country.
Beyond elections
For Robinhood, elections were only the starting point. "When I started doing this two years ago, it was about elections," JB Mackenzie, the brokerage's vice president and general manager for futures and prediction markets, told CNBC's Contessa Brewer, one of several working journalists the organizers booked for the program. "Then it transformed into politics and sports, and now it's moving into economics and financials."
Sports remain the biggest category, Mackenzie said, but contracts on Bitcoin, crude oil and gold are now the fastest-growing. "The simplicity of a probability is much more consumable for customers," he said.
Polymarket's Bailey Springer, who works on regulatory strategy outside the U.S., said regulators in global financial hubs increasingly recognize that "prediction markets aren't going away" and have real uses for investment and hedging. "At Polymarket, our position is that these are derivatives and should be regulated as such," she said.
Trading the news
Speed was another theme. On Thursday's "Race to Zero Latency" panel, Farokh Sarmad, president and co-founder of Decrypt Media, said ordinary traders are usually a step behind professional firms when news breaks. "By the time you open Polymarket or Kalshi or Myriad or all the other prediction markets, you're usually a little too late," he said.
His answer is to cut out the gap between reading and trading, which Decrypt is doing with its Solana-based Information Exchange. "The best way to reduce that latency is to be able to consume it and trade it directly on the same platform," Sarmad said, adding that for any of this to work, "everything has to move on chain."
Institutional money also featured heavily, with Morgan Stanley leading sessions on the second day.
Lindh, for his part, sees the industry's next debate already taking shape. "I think the next step will be the comparison between prediction markets and insurance," he said.
Disclosure: Myriad is a prediction market developed by Decrypt's parent company, Dastan.
