articles.title: USDC Overtakes USDT in Euro Trading as MiCA Rules Take Hold
articles.text:
USDC overtakes USDT in euro stablecoin trading as EU rules reshape market: Kaiko
USDC’s share of euro stablecoin trading has climbed to 56% since January 2024, with deeper liquidity as exchanges restrict USDT under MiCA.
Circle’s USDC (USDC) has overtaken Tether’s USDt (USDT) in stablecoin trading against the euro, as European Union regulations increasingly favor bloc-compliant stablecoins, according to a new Kaiko report.
USDC now accounts for 56% of stablecoin trading against the euro, up from just 10% in January 2024, according to Kaiko data. The shift accelerated after major exchanges restricted USDT trading for customers in the European Economic Area under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA).
USDC has also overtaken USDT in euro-denominated trading liquidity, with its order books now roughly 40% deeper than its rival’s. Tether remains the larger stablecoin globally, with a circulating supply about 2.5 times that of USDC.
Kaiko described stablecoin-to-euro trading pairs as a “main on-ramp and off-ramp for European customers,” allowing them to exchange euros for US dollar-pegged stablecoins when entering or exiting cryptocurrency markets.
USDC-to-euro trading pair overtakes USDC-to-USDT. Source: Kaiko
The findings come about two weeks after the European Banking Authority designated USDC as the EU’s first “significant e-money token” under MiCA, a classification that places the stablecoin under direct EBA supervision and subjects its issuer to additional regulatory requirements.
Related: Germany leads MiCA crypto authorization race as Europe’s deadline looms
US stablecoin rules could shift the balance between Circle and Tether
Kaiko said the US is taking a similar approach to stablecoin regulation under the GENIUS Act, raising the possibility that American exchanges could see the same shift in trading activity observed in Europe.
On Oct. 21, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency issued its first final rule under the law, establishing reserve and redemption requirements for stablecoin issuers under its supervision, effective Jan. 18, 2027.
Beginning in July 2028, US platforms will also face restrictions on offering stablecoins from issuers that do not meet the law’s approval requirements.
The regulatory changes could favor Circle, which has pursued authorization in both Europe and the US. Tether has taken a different approach, launching a separate US-focused stablecoin, USAT.
Related: Treasury Secretary Bessent likens GENIUS Act to Lincoln-era banking reform

articles.title: OpenAI Proves ETH Is False, and Crypto Twitter Has Questions - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- OpenAI says its AI has proven that ETH is false—but it’s not the “ETH” crypto traders are thinking about.
- The company says its AI models have found a way to disprove the Exponential Time Hypothesis, a computer-science conjecture from 1999.
- Here’s what all that means, and what mathematicians are doing about it.
OpenAI says ETH is false, and Crypto Twitter reacted exactly the way you would expect. “Damn algo traders just slaughtered $ETH,” a user called Takumi posted on X, while Andrew Jiang quipped: “Vitalik has been real quiet since this came out.”
But chill out, degens, the ETH in question is the Exponential Time Hypothesis, a computer-science conjecture from 1999 that has nothing to do with Ethereum, its price, or co-founder Vitalik Buterin. So, crypto bros, you can breathe.
OpenAI published a 67-page paper claiming its AI found a way around the hypothesis, and the people who proposed it are now checking the work.
Computer scientists Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi proposed ETH with Francis Zane, and it says a classic logic puzzle called 3-SAT (finding true-or-false settings that satisfy a pile of rules, three options at a time) cannot be solved much faster than by trying every combination. Hundreds of papers assume it to show that problems in graph theory, computational biology, databases and geometry cannot be solved quickly, per OpenAI.
In other words, ETH is a map of what computers will probably never do fast, and OpenAI says its model just redrew it. “The refutation of the ETH reopens questions about how much faster these tasks could become,” the company wrote on its blog, “and may help guide the search for better algorithms.”
The paper, dated October 17 and revised October 25, describes a deterministic algorithm (one with no randomness) that counts every satisfying assignment of such puzzles in subexponential time, meaning the work grows more slowly than any exponential in the number of variables. Counting solutions is harder than deciding if one exists, so the harder job brings the easier one along for free.
OpenAI says its AI found the disproof on October 16 and that it was formalized in Lean, software that verifies every logical step mechanically, on October 17. Both sit on GitHub, the same route as its 722 math manuscripts earlier this month, of which only 162 came with a computer-checked main result.
Impagliazzo, Paturi, and MIT’s Ryan Williams lead the independent examination, and they are careful about their role. “Our involvement should not be taken as certification of the claim,” the three wrote in an open letter, adding that “a result of this significance requires careful, independent scrutiny and an understanding that others can reconstruct, question, and build upon.”
OpenAI says participants signed no non-disclosure agreements and work unpaid, and the company agreed to publish all raw data and fund a conference on the result.
Practical payoffs are far off: “Finding such algorithms, and turning theoretical advances into practical improvements, will require significant further research,” OpenAI wrote. The paper itself says the result does not show that every NP problem can be solved in subexponential time, so P versus NP, the question of if every problem with an easy-to-check answer is also easy to solve, stays open.
In simple terms, P is the class of problems that computers can solve efficiently, while NP is the class of problems whose proposed solutions can be checked efficiently. So P versus NP — the question of whether every problem whose answer is easy to check is also easy to solve — stays open.
Anthropic, not wanting to lose the math wars, then posted a paper credited to Claude titled “A 2^o(n) Time Algorithm for 3-SAT” and dated October 26. The repository, which also tackles the ETH problem, says an internal research Claude model discovered the algorithm, and “the result is purely asymptotic and says nothing about solving formulas in practice.”
Claude formalized Fermat’s Last Theorem in Lean in September, and Terence Tao saw this kind of overlap coming. “We have now seen that even the rumor of someone working on a problem can trigger a massive amount of AI-powered effort to flatten it before the original research project has time to reach its full potential,” the mathematician wrote in September.
OpenAI’s recent $5 million contribution to the Simons Foundation will fund workshops, conferences and special programs to help researchers examine and build on AI-produced results.

articles.title: Crypto Could Outperform AI Stocks: Wall Street’s Jordi Visser
articles.text:
Crypto could outperform AI stocks: Wall Street veteran Jordi Visser
Former Morgan Stanley and Weiss executive Jordi Visser says AI agents are boosting demand for crypto as he expands his holdings beyond Bitcoin, Ether and Solana.
Cryptocurrencies could deliver a better payoff from the artificial intelligence boom than AI stocks themselves, according to Visser Labs founder Jordi Visser.
Explosive gains in AI stocks are becoming harder to repeat, Visser tells Cointelegraph’s Trade Secrets. At the same time, AI agents are creating demand for crypto payments and tokenized assets.
“Without AI, I don’t think crypto would be going through this bull market,” he says.
Hyperscaler capital spending and free cash flow (left), and forward valuations compared with the S&P 500 (right). Source: JPMorgan Asset Management
As a result of his thesis, he has expanded his own holdings beyond Bitcoin, Ether and Solana into a broader basket of tokens.
Visser’s three-decade career includes stints as managing director at Morgan Stanley and chief investment officer at Weiss Multi-Strategy Advisers. He now heads 22V’s AI Macro Nexus Research.
AI is crypto’s smartphone moment
The Wall Street veteran’s broader bet is that AI agents will allow people to instruct software to execute trades and other financial transactions on their behalf.
“AI agents are effectively the same as the App Store or the smartphone for crypto,” he says.
In that scenario, users would direct their agents while the software handles execution. The growing use of those agents will drive more activity in tokenized assets and crypto payments, extending the investment opportunity beyond the companies supplying computing power.
Related: AI potential to drive crypto demand remains ‘underappreciated’: BlackRock
But Visser’s crypto outlook still carries exposure to the AI trade he has grown more cautious about. He identifies a severe AI downturn that drags down equity markets as one threat to his bullish case.
“I don’t think that would end the bull market, but I definitely think it would retest the lows that we just saw,” he says.
The AI “fireworks show” is over
Visser says he began reducing his exposure to memory chipmaker Micron in mid-May after concluding that hedge funds and retail investors had crowded into the AI trade.
“One of the reasons that Bitcoin and Ethereum were having such a hard time is because the focus was completely on AI,” he says.
AI offered investors potentially greener pastures backed by rising business revenue. Microsoft’s quarterly report on April 29 claimed that its AI business was generating revenue at an annualized rate of $37 billion, more than double a year earlier. Meanwhile, Micron reported in March that its fiscal second-quarter revenue had nearly tripled to $23.86 billion.
But AI investors now face a less forgiving market, according to Visser. The 100-stock AI portfolio he tracks is up about 40% this year, but has become more volatile than Bitcoin on a rolling 126-day measure.
Related: Agents can trade 24/7 — but Yat Siu warns you could lose access at any time
Financing concerns have since hit AI infrastructure, as building them costs more than companies generate from their existing businesses at present.
For example, Oracle spent $55.7 billion on capital expenditures in fiscal 2026 against $32 billion in operating cash flow, and raised $43 billion in debt financing.
“I didn’t say AI was over. AI fireworks show is over,” Visser says.
He still sees several years of growth ahead in computing demand from AI agents, but says investors should temper their expectations for stock returns.
Visser widens his crypto bets
Until August, Visser’s crypto holdings consisted solely of Bitcoin, Ether and Solana. While Bitcoin remains his largest position, he has since started to acquire a broader range of tokens.
Dogecoin is a clear signal he watches for returning retail enthusiasm, which he considers essential to sustaining a broader rally.
“They’re the energy of the space and they’re the ones that are going to fuel this as other people get involved,” he says.
To track that broader market, Visser maintains an equally weighted index of 42 tokens and four publicly traded stocks. He says it has outperformed Bitcoin since June and plans to hold all its constituents.
Privacy is a theme he has already invested in.
“I’m not betting on one company, but I believe in privacy,” Visser says.
He says AI will make privacy and identity protection more important as fraud and other forms of abuse grow. Zcash and Monero among projects that fit that investment thesis.

articles.title: McDonald's McRib Doesn't Actually Boost Bitcoin's Price, Sorry Everyone - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Some crypto traders believe that the McRib’s return to McDonald’s menus precedes a rise in Bitcoin’s price.
- Experts say there is "no correlation” between the two at all, as believers often omit the times the McRib has failed to pump prices.
- Analysts think the Fed’s rate decision on Wednesday is a far more likely driver of Bitcoin’s next move.
The McDonald's McRib has become a crypto meme in recent years, due to many traders believing that its reintroduction to the menu precedes a boost in Bitcoin's price. And, with the tangy pork sandwich back in certain states across the U.S., crypto traders are getting excited.
But experts have taken the McRib theory off the menu, saying that those parroting the theory are forgetting all of the times that the McRib hasn't coincided with a Bitcoin price increase.
The McRib is back on 10/27. BTC historically goes up >2x after the McRib returns. Don't fade the McRib.
Not financial advice. pic.twitter.com/RxBuzcVht5
— internbrah (@internbrah) October 22, 2026
"There is no correlation at all," Luke Nolan, senior researcher at CoinShares, told Decrypt. "Whilst it is a fun exercise, it seems to be that people omit McRib returns when it doesn't fit the narrative."
Nolan shared a chart tracking the McRib's return compared to Bitcoin's weekly close, and only three out of 10 McRib returns posted clear positive Bitcoin returns. In fact, it often comes before major drops in valuation.
Carlos Guzman, vice president of research at crypto trading firm GSR, told Decrypt that there is "no causal mechanism” and that any price increases following the McRib's reintroduction is just a "funny coincidence."
"Let's say, hypothetically, it did indicate the start of a bull run, it would be quite nonsensical, similar to when people overlaid the Dune movie releases," Nolan said. "So yes, it's fun, generates some excitement, but even in the best case, purely coincidental."
Guzman agreed, adding that the crypto community likely just clings to the theory as it's "silly," "obviously absurd," and because people find it funny.
This year's McRib return comes as Bitcoin sits in what André Dragosch, head of research at Bitwise Europe, called "wait and see mode," with traders waiting for the Federal Reserve's next moves before making big bets.
What will actually move Bitcoin?
Bitcoin has seen fairly limited activity over the past month, according to Decrypt data, dropping just 6% as it sits at $79,750.
The Fed raised rates in September for the first time since 2023, and CPI then rose 0.6% for the month. Its next rate decision is on Wednesday.
That decision is one of three catalysts coming in the next two weeks, Jake Koch-Gallup, senior research analyst at Blockworks, told Decrypt. The other two are an options expiry of $11.69 billion worth of Bitcoin on October 30 and the U.S. midterms on November 3.
"If the Fed keeps rates the same and ETF inflows keep coming, I’d expect the break to be upward," Koch-Gallup told Decrypt last week. "If the Fed hikes again, the $75,000 to $77,000 floor comes back into play."
So if the Fed gives the market what it wants, then Bitcoin's price could actually jump over the coming days… just as the McRib returns to McDonald's stores. Coincidence? Experts think so.

articles.title: Hayes Details FLOP’s AI Compute Derivatives Vision After Selling Altcoins
articles.text:
Hayes details FLOP’s AI compute derivatives vision after selling his altcoins
Arthur Hayes revealed the derivatives market design for Flop Network and how he expects its native token could transform AI compute into a tradable commodity.
BitMEX co-founder and Flop Labs CEO Arthur Hayes shared new details about the Flop Network and how he expects its native token could turn AI computing power into a tradable commodity, two days after selling his altcoin holdings.
Hayes proposed measuring the computing power delivered for each AI inference task and using transaction data to derive a spot price for compute denominated in Flop (FLOP) tokens. He cited a lack of a universal benchmark price for AI computing power.
“If Flop becomes the payments network for AI agents, then it follows that the $FLOP/compute exchange rate will be the global benchmark for spot compute,” wrote Hayes in a Monday Substack essay, adding that a liquid spot compute market would enable derivatives based on that price.
Analysts at BCG in a July 2026 report considered how soon AI computing power could become a commodity. The consultancy projected that the market for AI compute will reach roughly $2.3 trillion by 2030 climbing from $360 billion in 2025.
Flop Labs is developing a network that allows AI agents to pay for computing and decentralized memory services. In August, Hayes said Flop was planning a “massive airdrop” in the fourth quarter of 2026 and announced that he would be the company’s CEO.
Hayes’ Flop explainer came in the wake of his statement on Saturday that he “dumped it all” and took profits from the Ether (ETH), Ethena (ENA) and Uniswap (UNI) token holdings in Maelstrom’s directional trading book, citing “dicey” macroeconomic and geopolitical conditions.
Lookonchain later flagged about $22 million worth of tokens sold by Hayes-linked wallets, including $15 million in ETH, $2.7 million in ENA, $2.2 million in UNI, $1.2 million in Ether.fi (ETHFI), $398,000 in Aerodrome Finance (AERO), $244,000 in Pendle (PENDLE) and $214,000 in Zama (ZAMA) tokens.

articles.title: Polymarket Has Investigated 'Dozens' of Midterm Election Bets: Report - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Polymarket has investigated "dozens" of bets on midterm election markets, its head of global intelligence and investigations, Shana Bautista, told NPR.
- At least two of those cases have been referred to the CFTC, according to a person familiar with the probes cited by NPR.
- Bautista said a new surveillance system draws on campaign finance, crypto and banking data and generates "hundreds of alerts a day" ahead of the November 3 vote.
Polymarket has investigated "dozens" of bets on its midterm election markets for possible insider trading and manipulation, the company's head of global intelligence and investigations, Shana Bautista, told NPR.
At least two of those investigations have been referred to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, NPR reported, citing a person familiar with the probes.
Bautista, a former FBI official and crypto analyst who joined Polymarket in June, said her team of 16 is policing election bets with a new surveillance system ahead of the November 3 vote.
"If you have information that you have a duty to protect, don't trade on it," she said. "It's explicitly against our terms of use on both platforms, but also is against the law. If you decide that you are smarter and can do it, we will find you."
Her team monitors both Polymarket's U.S.-regulated exchange, which requires users to verify their identities, and Polymarket International, where users can trade anonymously with crypto. Even so, Bautista said crypto trades are rarely fully anonymous. "There's never been a case that we work where we haven't been able to identify, potentially, who these people are," she said.
The system pulls in data from social media, Federal Election Commission filings, crypto companies, banking partners and statistical models, and alerts Bautista when a user trips enough internal red flags. "We're getting hundreds of alerts a day," she said. She declined to share the specific criteria, citing system security.
Election markets are especially vulnerable, Barnard College economics professor Rajiv Sethi told NPR, because they "have the possibility of being a self-fulfilling prophecy," with perceptions of a candidate's momentum able to influence the result.
Kalshi, Polymarket's main rival, launched its own FEC-based system in May to block campaign staffers from betting on elections. In June, it added employment disclosures for high-risk markets and a risk-scoring framework, saying it had opened more than 150 investigations that year and referred more than 20 cases to law enforcement. One campaign staffer told NPR they had found a way around Kalshi's block.
Insider trading on prediction markets
Election insider trading drew scrutiny in May, when campaign staffers told NPR they had made "thousands" betting on their own candidates using tips about unreleased polls. "Because you have all this information and knowledge that isn't publicly available yet, it's almost foolish not to bet on it before it's made public," one said. Jeff Le Riche, a former CFTC trial lawyer, told the outlet that such trades "could potentially be a violation" of the law.
Polymarket partnered with blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis on market surveillance tools in April, days after an active-duty U.S. Army soldier was charged with using classified information about the raid to capture Nicolás Maduro to bet on Polymarket. The soldier, who has pleaded not guilty, allegedly placed more than $33,000 in bets and won nearly $410,000. Polymarket said it detected the activity and reported it to authorities before the arrest.
NPR reported that the CFTC has done little to police prediction markets, largely leaving the work to the companies. In September, though, CFTC staff warned that "mention markets," contracts on whether a named person says certain words or attends an event, should be presumed readily susceptible to manipulation. The advisory came three weeks after the agency fined a teleprompter operator who traded on speeches he had already read.

articles.title: Luxor Raises $16M from CMT Digital Amid AI-Bitcoin Miner Compute Convergence
articles.text:
Luxor raises $16M from CMT Digital amid AI-Bitcoin miner convergence
Luxor aims to use the proceeds to scale its existing AI infrastructure business and expand its GPU sourcing services as global chip supply chains become constrained.
Full-stack compute company Luxor Technology raised $16 million in a strategic round led by CMT Digital.
The investment round also saw participation from Canaan, MicroBT, Halo, Steelhead, and additional angel investors, according to a Tuesday announcement shared with Cointelegraph.
The company aims to use the proceeds to scale its agentic cloud platform, grow its AI hardware business, expand its compute derivatives trading capabilities and hire more staff.
Luxor serves Bitcoin miners such as Canaan and TeraWulf and has expanded its hardware business to source GPUs and AI servers for the AI computing market, as global chip supply chains become “increasingly hard to navigate.” The raise will help scale its existing AI infrastructure business and capitalize on the convergence of Bitcoin miners and AI firms through computing markets.
“Compute markets are converging: the same miners, power sites and capital that served digital mining are now powering AI,” said Luxor’s co-founder and CEO Nick Hansen.
In September, the company launched Luxor AI, a business segment that extends its hardware, software, and compute trading stack built for Bitcoin miners into the AI and high-performance computing market.
In June 2021, Luxor raised $5 million in a Series A funding round led by institutional Bitcoin technology and financial services firm NYDIG, to fund the expansion of its North American BTC mining services. Earlier seed round investors included Celsius, Valour and Bitnomial, according to startup data tracker Tracxn.

articles.title: Bitcoin Mining Firm Luxor Raises $16 Million to Scale Its AI Compute Push - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Luxor Technology raised $16 million in a strategic round led by CMT Digital, with participation from Canaan, MicroBT, Halo, Steelhead and angels, to scale its push into AI computing power.
- The raise follows the September launch of Luxor AI, which extends Luxor’s Bitcoin-mining stack—energy, hardware, software and trading—into AI.
- Funds will scale its cloud platform, AI hardware business and compute-derivatives desk, fitting a broader miner-to-AI pivot.
Luxor Technology, a company that built its business around Bitcoin mining, has raised $16 million to expand into the fast-growing market for AI computing power, the latest sign of crypto infrastructure firms pivoting toward artificial intelligence.
The Seattle-based company said the strategic round was led by CMT Digital, the venture arm of Chicago’s CMT Group, with participation from mining-hardware makers Canaan and MicroBT, as well as Halo, Steelhead, and angel investors.
The round combined primary and secondary capital, and Luxor framed each backer as an operating partner already embedded in the compute supply chain it serves, across hardware, capital, and power.
The raise follows the September launch of Luxor AI, a segment that extends the energy, hardware, software and trading stack Luxor built for Bitcoin mining into the AI and high-performance computing market. The company brings a sizable operating history to the effort: its hardware desk has traded $1 billion of mining ASICs, its energy arm services more than 75 megawatts of load across two U.S. grid regions, and its cloud platform had processed 1.8 million workloads so far this year as of September.
Luxor said it will use the funds to scale that cloud platform, provide working capital for its AI hardware business, grow its compute-derivatives trading, and make engineering and go-to-market hires.
A notable piece is its over-the-counter desk, which already offers cash-settled options, forwards and backstops on compute-rental indexes, turning AI computing power into something that can be priced and hedged like a financial instrument.
“Compute markets are converging: the same miners, power sites and capital that served digital mining are now powering AI,” said Nick Hansen, Luxor’s CEO and co-founder.
The move fits a broader Bitcoin mining industry stampede towards AI.
Bitcoin miners have increasingly repurposed their power and infrastructure for AI, with some signing billion-dollar hyperscaler deals and others selling Bitcoin to fund the shift. Analysts at VanEck and Bernstein have cast miners as unlikely power brokers in the AI race, given their rare access to the electricity and sites that data centers need.

articles.title: Analysis Sees New Bitcoin Bull Market as Older Coins’ Realized Cap Share Drops
articles.text:
Bitcoin price analysis sees ‘strong rally’ as old coins become dormant
A decline in the share of Bitcoin’s realized cap held by coins unmoved for 18 months or longer points to the ‘early stages’ of a bull market, analysis says.
Bitcoin (BTC) onchain transaction data is hinting at the start of a new uptrend as long-term holders retreat from selling.
Key points:
- The percentage of Bitcoin’s realized cap involving coins dormant for 18 months or longer has remained broadly stable since mid-September, dropping from 26.98% to 26.59%.
- CryptoQuant analysis showed that longer reductions in the cohort’s onchain activity accompanied the start of previous Bitcoin bull markets.
- Coins that last moved at least five years ago account for around 34,000 BTC in monthly onchain volume — half that of 2024.
Old coin dormancy points to “early stages” of Bitcoin bull market
Data from onchain analytics platform CryptoQuant shows that investors holding coins for 18 months or longer are starting to become less active.
On Sept. 16, the 18-month-plus cohort’s share of realized cap — the value of all coins at the price they last moved onchain — hit 26.98%, its highest since mid-November 2024.
Analyzing the data, CryptoQuant sees a historical trend that preceded Bitcoin bull markets now repeating.
“The pattern has always been the same: when the proportion of Bitcoin held for more than 18 months across the entire network rises and then starts to decline, a strong rally follows,” it wrote in a blog post.
It included a chart of UTXO (Unspent Transaction Output) age bands, sized according to their contribution to the realized cap.
Bitcoin realized cap by UTXO age. Source: CryptoQuant
Reduced onchain spending by long-term investors reflects a move to maintain BTC exposure to increase profitability in the long term. The contribution by these investors remained in a broad uptrend beginning in November 2025, with profit-taking activity rising as BTC/USD fell further from its current all-time high of $126,200.
CryptoQuant noted that the UTXO trend reversal remains modest, implying that the market is witnessing only the very start of more bullish conditions.
“The market has now shifted into a bullish cycle, but we still appear to be in the early stages of the cycle, where such a signal has not even begun yet,” it commented.
“This looks like a point where we can remain positive about both the potential upside and the duration of the rally.”
Bitcoin drawdown from all-time highs still shallowest on record
Among long-term holders, only the 18-month-to-two-year cohort is currently in net loss, with a cost basis of $93,193. Its cost basis currently sits at $93,193.
Related: BTC price risks $80K loss into FOMC, earnings: Three things to know in Bitcoin this week
Since its 2025 all-time highs, Bitcoin has fallen below this cohort’s cost basis, while older cohorts have remained in aggregate profit. The year 2026 thus marks the first bear market in which price has stayed above the 2-3-year cohort’s cost basis, CryptoQuant shows.
Bitcoin realized price by UTXO age. Source: CryptoQuant
In a report released last week, crypto investment company Galaxy Digital described the “shallowest” bear market on record, with a maximum drawdown versus all-time highs of -53%.
BTC in custody for five years or more, meanwhile — coins that Galaxy says were responsible for the supply glut that halted price upside at $126,200 — are now also supporting the case for a fresh long-term uptrend.
“Coins unmoved for five years or more moved at 67k BTC a month in 2024 and 47k in 2025… totaling 1.11 million BTC since October 2024, the largest old-coin distribution of any cycle, most of it absorbed by the spot ETFs and BTC digital asset treasury (DAT) companies,” it wrote.
In 2026, the volume supplied by the five-year-plus cohort has averaged 34,000 BTC per month, half as much as in 2024.
Five-year dormant BTC supply UTXO data (screenshot). Source: Galaxy Digital

Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.

Tokenized Stock Battle Looms Over Robinhood’s Earnings Call
Somebody bought a full-page ad in the Wall Street Journal this weekend to tell public company CEOs that crypto is coming for their shares.
“YOUR STOCK. THEIR TOKENS. YOUR PROBLEM,” it read, paid for by the Common Sense Leadership Fund, a conservative nonprofit. They listed eight risks - pricing disparities, obscured ownership, impaired capital raising, cybertheft, market manipulation, AML and KYC loopholes, absent investor protections, legal liability. And the call to action was blunt: the SEC has given you the right to opt out, you have 30 days, this is your only chance.
The war against tokenized stocks is brewing.
Nine companies objected to having their shares tokenized on the OKX-ICE venue on October 15. By October 19 it was 16. By October 23, the list hit 22, including Wells Fargo, Cisco, Marvell, Arm, Moderna and Intuit joining Microsoft, Alphabet, Goldman Sachs, Verizon, Broadcom and UnitedHealth. That’s a two-and-a-half-fold increase in eight days, and 35% of the 63 companies the venue planned to list.
OKXICE even amended its rules on October 19 to let issuers tokenize their own shares, which would hand them control. Not one objector has taken it. They don’t want a better version of the product. They don’t want it.
Which brings us to today.
Robinhood reports third-quarter results after the bell, and no company has more riding on how this fight resolves.
Robinhood Chain launched its public mainnet on July 1. In its debut quarter it generated roughly $51 million in revenue. That’s more than Ethereum’s $41 million, while Ethereum’s own network revenue fell 35%. It processed about $65 billion in DEX volume, fourth among all networks.
Of that, $13.7 billion was tokenized equities. One fifth of everything trading on the chain, in a single quarter, from a zero start.
Robinhood’s stock tokens have already drawn fire (AMC’s CEO called them “contemptible”) and the company is building an entire ecosystem on top of them. Long.xyz pairs memecoins against tokenized NVDA and TSLA, and meme-versus-stock pairs now drive most stock-token volume on the chain. Orbio funds AI inference credits with creator fees paid in tokenized NVDA. Pull the stock tokens out, and a lot of that architecture has nothing to stand on.
So will Vlad Tenev address the tokenized stock war? It’s the billion-dollar question. A tweet from Monday makes it seem like perhaps he will. We will find out soon enough...

articles.title: Zcash Co-Founder Proposes Ending ZCG’s Funding Stream
articles.text:
Zcash co-founder calls to stop funding ‘over $125M’ grants program
Sean Bowe says ZCG has enough money to keep funding projects and wants its share of new ZEC redirected to a reserve for the network.
Zcash co-founder Sean Bowe proposed ending the automatic funding stream to Zcash Community Grants (ZCG), saying its treasury was large enough to continue funding projects without further automatic payments.
“ZCG has over $125M in funding, and will receive millions more before the spigot is turned off,” Bowe said Tuesday on X. “The program was never designed to handle this amount of funding.”
Bowe shared a draft GitHub proposal that would redirect ZCG’s 8% share of the Zcash (ZEC) block subsidy to the network’s sustainability reserve, while leaving its existing funds untouched.
The allocation would flow to the Network Sustainability Mechanism until the current funding period ends in 2028. The mechanism is designed to hold ZEC out of circulation and gradually reissue it through future block rewards.
In September, Haseeb Qureshi, managing partner at crypto venture capital firm Dragonfly, proposed ending the Zcash developer fund when its current funding period expires, saying that it risks being “politicized” as it approaches $100 million in value.
ZCG’s dashboard listed 91,453 ZEC and $8.8 million in cash as of Wednesday, with $2.4 million in outstanding grant commitments. The ZEC holdings alone were worth about $111 million at press time.
The network’s separate development lockbox held 72,351 ZEC, worth roughly $89 million, according to ZecStats.

articles.title: Why This Team of Ninjas Is Tripling Down on Mining Bitcoin - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- NIP Group, which owns esports team Ninjas in Pyjamas, has bought a third batch of Bitcoin miners in exchange for more than 247 million shares.
- The company says it now has roughly 13.85 EH/s of capacity, enough to mine around 195 Bitcoin a month, or $2.8 million at today's prices.
- The CEO told Decrypt the company could shift capacity to AI computing if the returns beat mining.
Ninjas in Pyjamas Group, the company behind the legendary esports team, has acquired a third batch of Bitcoin miners in exchange for over 247 million Class A ordinary shares.
Hicham Chahine, the founder and CEO of NIP Group, told Decrypt that he wants to bet on Bitcoin mining while the market is "cooling," rather than when it's hot and competition is higher. He added that the facilities could be used for artificial intelligence in the future.
"Now that this tranche is closed, we're at roughly 13.85 EH/s. That puts us among the largest publicly listed miners in the world, roughly 195 Bitcoin a month," Chahine said. "That's real revenue, and it supports everything else we're building. This year we reviewed every single piece of NIP Group, not just mining. We made decisions with one goal: better margins and a clear path to profitability. Mining had to earn its place in that review, and it did."
It comes after the esports team expanded its Bitcoin operation last year as it looked to mine 160 Bitcoin a month. This most recent acquisition brings that target up by 35 Bitcoin to 195 Bitcoin a month, or $2.8 million at today's prices.
Chahine told Decrypt that NIP Group is "optimistic about where this is heading," adding that the third batch of Bitcoin miners will require "minimal ramp time."
NIP Group is a digital entertainment company known for esports and gaming ventures. It owns Ninjas in Pyjamas, which fields professional esports teams in games like Counter-Strike 2, Valorant, League of Legends, and Rocket League.
The firm's stock, NIPG, has dropped 40.7% from $6.74 to $4 since the Bitcoin announcement last week, according to Yahoo Finance data. This marks an all-time low for the stock. Bitcoin has dropped 2% to $79,820 over the same period of time, per Decrypt data.
An AI future
Chahine explained that the purchased facilities could shift to focus on artificial intelligence infrastructure if the market demands.
"We look at what AI and [high-performance computing] customers will actually pay, how long they'll commit and whether that demand is sustained or temporary," Chahine told Decrypt. "When those workloads clearly beat mining on returns, consistently and not just for a week or two, that's when we may move capacity. If the numbers say shift, we shift."
Of course, any sort of future pivot would require notable legwork, as Bitcoin miners can't simply be turned into AI data centers at the flick of a switch. But, Chahine said, the infrastructure around the mining facilities is a good foundation for what AI and high-performance computing need.
"When we talk about AI, we mean using that footprint and that know-how for compute-heavy work when the economics make sense," he said. "We're a gaming and entertainment company at heart, and our fans already live on compute, bringing infrastructure and entertainment under one roof makes sense."

articles.title: Bloom Bot Hackers Loot $953K Faster than You Can Microwave Popcorn
articles.text:
Bloom bot hackers loot $953K faster than you can microwave popcorn
Bloom pledged to reimburse nine traders after $953,000 was drained from 48 wallets, saying no private keys were accessed or compromised.
Hackers stole nearly $1 million from wallets linked to Telegram trading bot Bloom in under two minutes, according to blockchain analytics company Bitquery.
The attack drained $953,000 in 94 seconds from 48 cryptocurrency wallets belonging to nine traders who had used the bot, Bitquery reported Monday.
Bitquery said each drain was a Solana (SOL) transfer signed with the affected wallet’s private key.
Bloom pledged to reimburse all affected traders in full. In a later Monday statement, it attributed the attack to a remote code execution vulnerability in a third-party module and said no private keys had been accessed or compromised.
Trading bots such as Bloom hold users’ private keys to trade on their behalf, which can leave lingering security risks even after traders stop using them. Five wallets drained in the Bloom attack had been inactive on the bot since the first half of 2025, Bitquery said.
This is not the first time Telegram trading bot users have lost funds in an attack. In September 2024, Banana Gun reported that 11 users lost about $3 million. In October 2023, users of Telegram trading bots Maestro and Unibot lost a combined $1.1 million to exploits of their router contracts.
Related: Cysic dangles a 10% bounty, hacker pours loot into Tornado Cash

articles.title: Ripple Wins Final OCC Approval for Trust Bank Behind $2.6B RLUSD Stablecoin - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- The OCC has granted Ripple final approval to open Ripple National Trust Bank, 10 months after conditionally approving the charter in December 2025.
- The bank will manage the reserves backing Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin, act as collateral trustee for holders, and offer fiduciary digital asset custody.
- The approval comes as community banks challenge the OCC's crypto charters in court, after Sen. Elizabeth Warren called them illegal.
Ripple has received final approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency to establish Ripple National Trust Bank, a federally supervised national trust bank, the company said on Monday.
The approval completes a process that began when the OCC conditionally approved Ripple's application in December 2025, alongside those of Circle, Paxos, Fidelity Digital Assets and BitGo.
Once open, the bank will manage the segregated reserves backing the Ripple USD (RLUSD) stablecoin, act as collateral trustee of those reserves for the benefit of RLUSD holders, and provide fiduciary digital asset custody services to enterprises. RLUSD will still be issued by Standard Custody & Trust Company, Ripple's limited purpose trust company regulated by the New York Department of Financial Services, so the stablecoin will now sit under both state and federal supervision.
"For years, we've said crypto and banks work better together. Final approval for Ripple National Trust Bank is what that looks like in practice," Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse said in the release. In a tweet, he added: "The revolution isn't happening outside the system. It's happening from within it."
Big news heading into @RippleSwell: the @USOCC has granted final approval for Ripple National Trust Bank.
This gives Ripple a federally supervised platform to support $RLUSD and provide digital asset custody to enterprises.
We’ve always said crypto and banks work better…
— Brad Garlinghouse (@bgarlinghouse) October 26, 2026
Launched in December 2024, RLUSD has a market capitalization of about $2.6 billion, according to CoinGecko. Ripple says the stablecoin is used across its payments network and as collateral within its Ripple Prime brokerage. BNY is the stablecoin's primary reserve custodian.
XRP, the cryptocurrency closely associated with Ripple, rose 0.5% over the past 24 hours to $1.29, according to CoinGecko, one of only two top-10 coins by market cap to gain on the day alongside Zcash.
Crypto's bank charter fight
The national trust charters the OCC has handed to crypto firms remain contested. Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) has argued, in a letter to Comptroller Jonathan Gould, that the approvals for firms including Coinbase and Ripple violated the National Bank Act. "These companies are effectively crypto banks that want to evade the fundamental safeguards and obligations that come with being a bank," she wrote.
The Digital Chamber, a crypto industry trade group, urged the OCC to "defend these charter approvals and continue developing clear supervisory expectations for trust banks."
Earlier this month, the Independent Community Bankers of America sued the OCC in federal court, arguing that the charters have become "a side door into the banking system for crypto firms" that avoid the capital requirements, consolidated supervision and FDIC insurance that bind traditional banks.
Ripple said it will keep working with the OCC, NYDFS and other regulators as the bank begins operations and as the U.S. implements the GENIUS Act's stablecoin framework.
