articles.title: Binance Files for Brazil Crypto License Ahead of Deadline
articles.text:
Binance files for Brazil crypto license ahead of Friday deadline
The exchange is delisting 22 crypto assets for Brazilian users and hopes talks with the central bank will allow it to restore some services.
Binance has applied for a cryptocurrency service provider license in Brazil, seeking to maintain its operations in one of Latin America’s largest crypto markets ahead of a regulatory deadline on Friday, Oct. 30.
The exchange submitted its application to the Central Bank of Brazil on Friday, Oct. 23, through its local entity, BBrasil, according to a statement shared with Cointelegraph.
The company said the filing would allow Brazilian users to continue accessing crypto assets, stablecoin trading, payments and investment services.
Binance has also announced changes for Brazilian users effective Tuesday, including restrictions on crypto lending, margin trading and other services. The exchange is also delisting 22 crypto assets in the country.
“We support a regulated market that considers the characteristics of virtual assets, so that access to technology and innovation continues to advance, but we hope that the ongoing dialogue with the Central Bank will allow us to offer, in the near future, other products that were discontinued to comply with current regulations,” said Thiago Sarandy, Binance’s general manager in the country.
Brazil requires existing crypto service providers to submit authorization applications by Oct. 30 to continue operating under transitional arrangements. Filing an application does not constitute regulatory approval.
Related: Binance.US seeks $1B valuation in potential $100M funding round: Report

articles.title: Polymarket reforms Bitcoin contracts and Binance trading spikes immediately drop
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Polymarket’s five-minute Bitcoin markets have used 60-second averages for both opening and closing benchmarks since Aug. 14.
- Wang’s early post-change sample found the earlier Binance settlement-time pattern subsided, without measuring current wallet losses.
- Historical wallet gains cannot establish current exposure or combined strategy profits after underlying-market trades and execution costs.
Polymarket’s five-minute Bitcoin contract sampled on Oct. 27 uses averaged opening and closing benchmarks, following an August reform that changed the incentive to move its settlement price.
The current design requires a different risk assessment from the single-snapshot rule examined in earlier research.
An estimate of about $8.2 million earned by 821 wallets in earlier pushed cycles belongs to that historical research. Guangzhe Wang’s newer study cites the finding from Dai and co-authors.
Wang’s before-and-after results instead point to a subsiding Binance trading pattern in the first weeks after averaging. That gives the reform an empirical test, while keeping separate whether an observed settlement-time pattern declined and how much traders lose under the current rule.
The Oct. 27 Bitcoin market, covering 12:20-12:25 p.m. ET, names Chainlink’s BTC/USD 60-second time-weighted average price (TWAP) as its resolution source. Up wins when the ending benchmark is at least as high as the opening benchmark, and Down wins otherwise.
The Dai, Jia and Yu working paper, submitted to arXiv on June 30, reported settlement-time spot-flow spikes and subsequent reversals after the five-minute contract’s launch. The broader finding concerns the incentive to move the underlying reference market.
Wang’s newer paper examined Binance one-second data from July 1, 2025, through Sept. 4, 2026, with 82,752 Bitcoin boundaries where only the five-minute contract settled. For each sampled five-minute window, he measured the share of Binance volume traded in its final ten seconds:
| Regime | Final-ten-second volume share | 
|---|---|
| Before five-minute contract launch | 3.05% | 
| Single-snapshot settlement | 5.68% | 
| 60-second average settlement | 3.02% | 
In the first three weeks of the 60-second regime, Wang found no systematic migration into earlier bins and no recurrence of the earlier near-strike reversal pattern.
That bounded observation is consistent with the reform’s effectiveness for the measured pattern. It is neither a current wallet-profit audit nor proof that every possible manipulation strategy has disappeared.
The study tests an observed response to the reform, and its outcome is a trading pattern.
Two averages decide the bet
According to Polymarket’s changelog, crypto up/down markets switched from single snapshots to Chainlink-computed averages on Aug. 7. Both the opening price to beat and the final settlement value moved to the applicable TWAP feed.
On Aug. 14 at 00:00 UTC, the platform extended five-minute crypto markets to 60 seconds. The October contract reflects an operating rule introduced more than two months earlier, and its five-minute duration should not be confused with its one-minute benchmark window.
Under a snapshot rule, an unusually brief move can be important if it affects the selected reference price. Under an average, its contribution depends on how much of the measurement window it influences.
The economic question becomes whether the benefit on the prediction-market position exceeds the cost of affecting that average and executing the strategy.
A historical dollar gain cannot be carried into that changed calculation without evidence that the old behavior and economics still apply.
Polymarket’s documentation says it takes the applicable average, just as it does for the closing value. Evaluating a disputed result requires the reference values used at both boundaries, along with the relevant report timing.
Chainlink’s timestamp documentation explains why the time printed on an exchange chart is insufficient. Each underlying report has a validity start and an observation timestamp, but report widths can vary, including when a later report absorbs a gap. The TWAP weights prices by the duration they cover.
The average also rolls with the latest observation rather than automatically snapping to a round clock minute. A 60-second TWAP is therefore neither the average price across the entire five-minute bet nor necessarily sixty equally weighted ticks.
What the old dollar figure cannot answer
A gain on a prediction-market position and the net return from a strategy involving the underlying asset are different measurements. If moving Bitcoin’s reference price requires trading Bitcoin, that leg and its execution costs belong in the profitability calculation.
Polymarket Institute distinguishes the decentralized international exchange from Polymarket US, with separate APIs and separately managed data.
Talos’s Oct. 27 quarterly review highlights its Kalshi integration and points to earlier analysis of potential Polymarket settlement manipulation.
The remaining measurement is financial as well as behavioral: gains and losses under the averaged rule, with the relevant underlying-market trades and execution costs accounted for.

articles.title: Bitcoin ETFs Claw Back $110M After $774M Exit
articles.text:
Bitcoin ETFs claw back $110M after $774M exit
US spot Bitcoin ETFs remained in the red for October, with about $202 million in net outflows for the month despite Monday’s rebound.
US-listed spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) returned to net inflows on Monday despite weakening market sentiment and continued volatility in BTC price.
The funds attracted $110 million in net inflows on Monday, bouncing back from $774 million in withdrawals over the previous two trading sessions, according to SoSoValue.
Despite the rebound, October remained negative, with approximately $202 million in net outflows through Monday.
Bitcoin traded at $79,595 at the time of publication and was down 2.6% over the past seven days, according to CoinGecko.
Market sentiment also weakened, with the Crypto Fear & Greed Index falling to 48 from 50 the previous day, while remaining in “Neutral” territory.
CryptoQuant data also showed retail investors sending more Bitcoin to Binance while large holders reduced their deposits.
Analyst Darkfost wrote on CryptoQuant that retail Bitcoin deposits to Binance nearly doubled to $10.8 billion over 30 days, while deposits from large holders fell to $3.8 billion. Darkfost suggested that smaller investors might be using the recent price rebound as an opportunity to sell.
Related: BTC price risks $80K loss into FOMC, earnings: Three things to know in Bitcoin this week

articles.title: Zcash's $125 million funding fight widens as Tyler Winklevoss calls to end its 'USAID'
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Zcash faces competing proposals to scrap its development fund after co-founder Sean Bowe called for ending payments to a $125 million grants program.
- Tyler Winklevoss and Josh Swihart back broader cuts, threatening a funding model Grayscale credits with sustaining Zcash's technological innovation.
- A rival proposal would preserve reduced funding until 2036, leaving Zcash divided over how to finance future upgrades as privacy adoption surges.
Zcash faces competing proposals to scrap or extend developer subsidies as growing investor interest swells the privacy network's funding reserves.
The debate intensified after Zcash co-founder Sean Bowe proposed ending automatic payments to Zcash Community Grants (ZCG), arguing that the program already controls enough resources to finance years of development without additional subsidies.
His proposal has drawn more aggressive demands from ZODL founder Josh Swihart, Gemini co-founder Tyler Winklevoss, and other ecosystem participants, while a rival plan would preserve reduced development funding until 2036.
The disagreement comes as Zcash approaches its 10th anniversary on Oct. 28, with renewed institutional interest and rising private transaction activity increasing scrutiny of how the network allocates newly created ZEC.
Zcash's $125 million treasury triggers calls to dismantle grants program
In an Oct. 26 draft proposal, Bowe called for redirecting ZCG's 8% share of block rewards into the Network Sustainability Mechanism (NSM), a protocol reserve that would eventually support future block rewards. Bowe said on X:
“It's time to turn off the ZCG funding stream.”
He added that ZCG has more than $125 million in funding and would receive millions more before the proposed cutoff, arguing that the program was never designed to manage such substantial resources.
The figure is based on approximately 91,453 ZEC, $8.8 million in dollar-denominated assets, and $2.4 million in outstanding obligations, assuming ZEC trades at $1,300.
At that valuation, ZCG's annual allocation would be worth approximately $68.3 million, compared with $6.12 million in annualized expenses based on its first-quarter spending.
Bowe's proposal would preserve the program's existing assets and leave the separate 12% coinholder-controlled funding stream untouched.
However, Maxime Desalle proposed going further by dissolving ZCG entirely, stopping new grant approvals and transferring its remaining treasury to the NSM after fulfilling existing commitments.
Desalle argued that ZCG's governance structure lets a small community advisory panel influence spending despite the wider economic costs borne by ZEC holders.
He also disclosed his involvement with Cypherpunk, a major Zcash mining company, through his work, while maintaining that the proposal was independent of his employment.
Bowe later said he would personally support considering transferring ZCG's existing treasury, though he preferred to separate that decision from his proposal to stop future payments.
Winklevoss and Swihart push for broader cuts as rival plan emerges
The dispute has expanded beyond ZCG's future.
Tyler Winklevoss endorsed ending the grants arrangement, declaring, “It's time to end the USAID of Zcash.”
Swihart, meanwhile, argued that eliminating only ZCG's allocation would leave the underlying controversy unresolved. He said:
“It'd be a mistake to kill only one part of the dev fund. If dissolved, then no half measures, dissolve it all, both the ZCG and coinholder streams.”
Swihart pointed out that the coinholder-controlled program receives approximately 216 ZEC daily, creating a similar accumulation problem as the cryptocurrency appreciates.
He proposed eliminating both funding streams and redirecting their allocations to the NSM, honoring existing grant obligations before transferring remaining eligible funds.
Swihart also suggested a one-time, coinholder-approved legal defense endowment for Zcash developers. He said:
“A half measure leaves the door open to ongoing debate and politics. Markets like certainty.”
Notably, Swihart acknowledged that his company, ZODL, recently received a retroactive coinholder grant for core protocol development and could seek additional funding if the program survived. His proposal would eliminate that potential source of financing.
Yet the push to dismantle development funding is facing an alternative.
In an Oct. 27 draft, community contributor Dismad proposed gradually reducing the combined developer allocation from 20% to 10% around the 2028 halving, then to 5% in 2032, before eliminating it in 2036.
That approach would preserve existing governance arrangements while giving developers another decade of progressively declining protocol funding.
The competing plans would therefore produce substantially different outcomes: Bowe would end new ZCG payments, Desalle would dismantle the grants institution, Swihart would eliminate the entire development fund, and Dismad would extend a reduced version beyond its scheduled 2028 expiration.
Zcash's growing popularity raises stakes for future development
The growing calls to eliminate development subsidies contrast with Grayscale's view that protocol-funded research has kept Zcash technologically competitive over the past decade.
The asset manager highlighted the network's successive privacy upgrades, including Sapling, Orchard and the recently introduced Ironwood pool, as examples of improvements supported by dedicated development financing.
Grayscale argued that continued investment would be necessary to expand transaction capacity, prepare for quantum-computing threats and address emerging cybersecurity risks.
It said future innovation “will likely require ongoing financial support for developers from a variety of sources,” alongside more efficient capital allocation.
That assessment comes as Zcash sees substantial growth in both market value and network activity.
According to ZecStats, ZEC has gained about 260% over the past year, trading above $1,200 and pushing its market capitalization past $20 billion. The token has also appreciated roughly twentyfold since the beginning of 2025, when it traded near $60.
The rally has coincided with increased usage of the network's privacy features.
ZecStats data shows that Zcash processed an average of approximately 11,300 transactions daily in late October, an increase of about 70% from a year earlier. Shielded transactions accounted for roughly 62% of activity, up from about 24% during the same period in 2025.
Meanwhile, approximately 4.96 million ZEC, representing 29% of issued supply, are held in shielded pools that allow users to conceal transaction information.
The expansion has also reached traditional investment markets. Grayscale's Zcash exchange-traded product (ZCSH) reported approximately $708 million in net assets as of Oct. 26, reflecting the scale of institutional investment exposure that has developed around the cryptocurrency.

articles.title: RedotPay Eyes Confidential US IPO Filing by Year-End
articles.text:
RedotPay weighs confidential US IPO filing by year-end: Bloomberg
The stablecoin payments company previously disputed reports that its US listing had been delayed.
Hong Kong-based stablecoin payments company RedotPay is reportedly considering a confidential filing for a US initial public offering by the end of 2026, two months after reports that it had delayed its listing plans amid regulatory and legal hurdles.
RedotPay is also in talks with investors about a potential pre-IPO funding round that could value the company at between $4 billion and $5 billion, Bloomberg reported Monday, citing people familiar with the matter.
RedotPay says it has more than 8 million users, while data from Paymentscan shows $410.5 million in 30-day stablecoin card transaction volume.
The company was first reported in February exploring a New York listing that could raise more than $1 billion at a valuation exceeding $4 billion, with JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs and Jefferies reportedly working on the offering.
However, Bloomberg reported in August that RedotPay had delayed its US listing plans amid regulatory hurdles and legal disputes involving Binance.
The company subsequently disputed that characterization, reportedly saying “there has been no deferral of our IPO,” and that the company is “continuing to work with our partners on the IPO process.”
In August, Binance-affiliated companies sued the founders of RedotPay, seeking nearly $473 million in damages over allegations that they used confidential information to build a competing payments business and divert customers.
RedotPay has denied the allegations and previously told Cointelegraph that it would “vigorously defend all claims.”
Related: Binance, RedotPay clash over fate of Singapore lawsuit

articles.title: OpenAI claims a cryptography breakthrough. Does that threaten Bitcoin?
articles.text:
Quick Take
- OpenAI claims an Exponential Time Hypothesis refutation, while researchers are organizing an independent examination of the result.
- The disclosed SAT speed-up does not establish a practical attack on Bitcoin mining or spending signatures.
- The Lean formalization covers a weaker subexponential time bound than the manuscript’s sharpest claim.
OpenAI says its AI system has refuted the Exponential Time Hypothesis, a longstanding assumption about how difficult certain logic problems are to solve. The Oct. 26 announcement has researchers organizing an independent examination. The disclosed result does not establish a practical attack on Bitcoin.
ETH here means Exponential Time Hypothesis, rather than Ether. The subject is 3-SAT, a puzzle in which a computer must find true-or-false settings that satisfy a collection of logical rules. The hypothesis says solving these problems requires exponential time in the number of variables in the worst case.
OpenAI says the result was verified in Lean, a proof assistant, although its scope note describes a weaker time bound than the manuscript's sharpest claim. The researchers organizing the community's examination have expressly declined to certify it. Their letter says, “Our involvement should not be taken as certification of the claim.”
The manuscript, dated Oct. 17 and revised Oct. 25, claims a deterministic algorithm that exactly counts the satisfying assignments of fixed-width Boolean formulas in subexponential time and polynomial space. In plain English, its running time grows more slowly than an exponential bound as the problem gets larger. That is a different promise from making the problem easy on today's computers.
The disclosed bound does not establish a polynomial-time algorithm or settle P=NP, the question of whether every decision problem whose proposed solutions can be verified in polynomial time can also be solved in polynomial time.
CryptoSlate's examination of the paper is limited to its introductory pages 1–8, rather than a review of the full proof.
Bitcoin has two different security questions
For Bitcoin, mining and spending authorization are separate tasks. Miners search for a block-header hash below a target. Signatures establish authorization to spend. Bitcoin's signature systems include ECDSA and Schnorr over the secp256k1 elliptic curve, as described in BIP340.
The security assumptions described there concern elliptic-curve discrete logarithms and hash functions. The key-recovery question is whether an attacker can derive a private key from its public counterpart. Refuting an assumption about worst-case SAT solving does not, by itself, show how to defeat those concrete mechanisms. A practical attack would still need a suitable encoding, an implementation and a cost comparison for the task being attacked.
The variable count in a SAT formula is also not interchangeable with the bit length of a cryptographic key or hash. The Lean scope measures its bound using the encoded formula's variables and input length. Substituting a familiar crypto bit count into that bound would skip the work needed to represent the actual problem.
Bitcoin's difficulty adjustment recalculates its mining target every 2,016 blocks. That concerns block production, not signature authorization. It would not make a private mining advantage irrelevant.
The distinction follows a debate CryptoSlate covered on Oct. 7, when Justin Drake urged preparations for “bunker mode” after an earlier OpenAI mathematics release. That warning concerned a possible future attack; the earlier announcement had not demonstrated a practical ECDSA or RSA break. The Oct. 26 ETH claim concerns a different result.
Ryan Williams, posting as @rrwilliams, said he, Russell Impagliazzo and Mohan Paturi had been asked to organize an open, independent examination, without NDAs or compensation.
In a separate post, @rrwilliams said he had asked OpenAI to check whether existing cryptosystems were compromised and relayed that they were apparently safe. That is his second-hand account of a check requested from OpenAI, not an independent cryptographic audit.
OpenAI itself says practical improvements require significant further research. Asked about benefits developers might feel, @rrwilliams said he did not know, allowing both for progress within 12 months and for no such development. The organizers intend to share findings as the examination progresses.

articles.title: Keystone Hackers Steal Key Used to Verify Wallets
articles.text:
Keystone breach deepens: Hackers stole key used to verify wallets as genuine
Keystone initially disclosed a leak of customer information but has since disclosed that hackers also stole a key that could allow counterfeit wallets to pass authenticity checks.
Hardware wallet maker Keystone said an attacker who breached its website last week also stole a key used to verify the authenticity of its devices, widening the scope of an incident initially disclosed as a customer data leak.
In a statement Monday, Keystone said the stolen authentication key could allow attackers to produce counterfeit wallets that pass its authenticity checks.
“These devices could then be sold or shipped to customers, who might unknowingly use them as genuine products, potentially resulting in asset theft,” Keystone said.
The incident adds to a series of attacks targeting hardware wallet manufacturers this year.
Earlier this month, Ledger asked resellers across Southeast Asia and Hong Kong to suspend sales following reports that devices sold in the region contained unauthorized implants capable of capturing recovery phrases.
In late July, Coldcard manufacturer Coinkite issued a warning to users after attackers exploited a bug that caused its devices to generate wallet seeds with less entropy than intended, resulting in the theft of millions of dollars in crypto.
Keystone to destroy more than 18,000 devices with old key
In its latest update, Keystone said the attacker exploited a vulnerability in a third-party monitoring tool used by its website to escalate privileges.
“This enabled the attacker to obtain some customer information and a key used to verify the authenticity of our devices.”
Keystone said it plans to destroy 18,835 devices in its inventory that contain the compromised key and has suspended production shipments of all devices using it.
The company said shipments would resume once it begins producing devices with a new authentication key.
Keystone said devices manufactured and delivered before the Oct. 20 incident should be considered safe and that their authenticity checks remain trustworthy.
However, it could not guarantee the authenticity of devices delivered after that date and urged affected customers to contact its support team for additional verification.
Keystone confirms 25,964 buyer records leaked
Keystone also disclosed the extent of the customer data breach, saying its website’s Shopify store had generated 51,083 buyer records.
Of those, 25,119 had been deleted per its 180-day data retention policy.
However, the remaining 25,964 records dating from 2024 to 2026 may have been stolen by the attacker. Keystone said the older entries were not deleted due to a failure in its automated tool used to handle bulk erasure of data.
“The tool did not operate reliably. Some erasure tasks failed, and we did not detect and address these failures in time, resulting in certain personal information being retained beyond the permitted period,” Keystone said.
Related: Keystone says website breach exposed hardware wallet buyers’ addresses
In addition, the attacker may have also had access to 12,873 customer checkout records retained by Shopify — information from purchases that had not been completed.
Keystone said it had contacted Shopify to request the deletion of personal information in checkout records retained for more than 30 days.
The incident echoes a June 2020 data breach at Ledger that exposed more than 1 million email addresses, along with customer names, phone numbers and physical addresses. The leaked information fueled years of phishing attempts targeting affected users.
Other hardware wallet manufacturers have also suffered breaches involving customer information and third-party services this year.
In August, Trezor disclosed a breach at its shipping partner that exposed customer information, with the number of affected users expanding to more than 80,000 in September.
SafePal also reported an order-tracking vulnerability in August that exposed data belonging to nearly 40,000 customers, while BitBox was targeted in a September phishing campaign involving a compromised third-party email provider.

articles.title: Ripple gets final US trust bank approval. What does XRP gain?
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Ripple secured final OCC approval for a US national trust bank despite objections from traditional banking groups.
- The bank is approved to manage RLUSD reserves, serve as collateral trustee and provide fiduciary digital asset custody.
- RLUSD growth need not produce proportionate XRP buying, although XRPL fees and account reserves still require XRP.
Ripple said it secured final US approval for a national trust bank despite objections from traditional banking groups concerned about crypto firms entering regulated finance.
The company announced on Oct. 26 that the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) had granted final approval for Ripple National Trust Bank to manage RLUSD reserves, serve as collateral trustee and provide fiduciary digital asset custody. Ripple put RLUSD’s market capitalization at $2.5 billion in the announcement.
Brad Garlinghouse, CEO of Ripple, said:
“We’ve spent over a decade building regulated financial infrastructure that institutions can actually use at scale. A national trust charter gives us an even stronger foundation for RLUSD and the institutional products we’re building across payments, custody and capital markets.”
However, the implications for XRP remain less straightforward, with the bank's immediate responsibilities centered on stablecoin reserves and custody rather than the token itself.
Ripple overcomes opposition from traditional banking groups
The approval follows a prolonged dispute over whether crypto companies should be permitted to establish federally chartered trust banks without meeting all the requirements imposed on conventional lenders.
In July 2025, the American Bankers Association (ABA) and four other banking and credit union groups urged the OCC to postpone applications involving Ripple and several other digital asset firms.
The organizations questioned whether their proposed activities qualified as traditional fiduciary services and argued that approving the charters could represent a significant departure from established banking practices.
The Independent Community Bankers of America (ICBA) subsequently opposed Ripple's application directly, warning that allowing nontraditional companies to provide deposit-like services without equivalent regulatory safeguards could threaten financial stability.
Despite those objections, the OCC granted Ripple conditional approval in December 2025 before completing the chartering process this week.
Ripple Chief Legal Officer Stuart Alderoty portrayed the decision as validation of the company's longstanding regulatory approach. He said:
“Final OCC approval for Ripple National Trust Bank is the result of a simple choice we made years ago: build within the regulatory perimeter, not around it.”
The charter nevertheless comes with restrictions. Ripple National Trust Bank will not operate as a conventional commercial lender offering ordinary deposit accounts or loans.
Instead, it will oversee segregated RLUSD reserves and act as collateral trustee for token holders.
RLUSD issuance will remain with Standard Custody & Trust Company, Ripple's subsidiary regulated by the New York Department of Financial Services. BNY will also remain the stablecoin's primary reserve custodian.
Institutional expansion raises questions over XRP demand
The banking approval comes as Ripple builds a broader financial services business around its stablecoin, custody infrastructure and institutional trading operations.
On Oct. 12, Standard Chartered launched institutional custody for RLUSD on the XRP Ledger for eligible clients through its DFSA-regulated DIFC branch. The bank also announced plans to work with Ripple and LMAX Group to enable the stablecoin's use as trading collateral.
The proposed arrangement would allow institutions to deploy RLUSD-backed collateral on LMAX's trading platforms while keeping the underlying assets in Standard Chartered's custody, reducing the need to transfer funds between counterparties. The planned integration remains subject to documentation, testing and applicable approvals.
Three days later, Ripple Prime expanded into real-world asset perpetual swaps, allowing institutional clients to trade products linked to equities, commodities and currencies around the clock, with RLUSD available as collateral where permitted by jurisdiction.
XRP is used to pay transaction fees and can facilitate transfers between different currencies on the network. Increased RLUSD settlement on the ledger could therefore generate additional XRP-related activity, particularly where institutions use it as a bridge asset.
Yet RLUSD also operates on Ethereum, where transactions do not require XRP. Even on the XRP Ledger, institutions can transfer RLUSD directly without converting the stablecoin into XRP, although XRP is needed for network fees and account reserves.
This distinction means that Ripple's custody and stablecoin operations can grow without requiring institutions to accumulate XRP in proportion to the value of assets they manage or transfer.

articles.title: Ripple Secures Final OCC Approval for National Trust Bank
articles.text:
Ripple wins final US approval for national trust bank
The approval clears the way for Ripple to manage reserves backing its RLUSD stablecoin and provide digital asset custody.
Ripple announced Monday that its national trust bank has secured final approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC).
The approval completes the chartering process for Ripple National Trust Bank (RNTB), which received conditional approval from the OCC in December 2025.
The federally supervised trust bank is authorized to manage reserves backing Ripple USD (RLUSD), act as collateral trustee for the benefit of RLUSD holders and provide digital asset custody services, according to Ripple.
RLUSD will continue to be issued by Standard Custody & Trust Company, Ripple’s limited purpose trust company regulated by the New York Department of Financial Services.
“We’ve always said crypto and banks work better together — this is what that looks like. Real innovation, real accountability, federal oversight,” Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse said on X on Monday.
Ripple follows Circle, which secured final OCC approval in July. Other crypto firms remain at the conditional approval stage, including Coinbase, which received its preliminary green light in April, and Crypto.com and Stripe-owned Bridge, which received conditional approvals in February.
A national trust bank is a federally chartered institution focused on holding and managing assets on behalf of clients. Unlike a typical commercial bank, most national trust banks do not accept deposits or make loans and do not carry Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation insurance, according to the OCC.
Related: Advocacy group pushes back on banks’ lawsuit against OCC over charters

articles.title: Lightning tightens invoice rules after reported attack made Bitcoin withdrawals look unpaid
articles.text:
Quick Take
- BOLT11 now requires exactly one payment hash and one payment secret, rejecting invoices with missing or repeated fields.
- A developer described how conflicting invoice parsers could make completed withdrawals appear unpaid, opening a route to further payouts.
- Released lnd versions include duplicate-hash rejection, while a proposal adding payment-secret checks remained open as of October 27.
Lightning developers tightened BOLT11, the Lightning Network’s invoice standard, on Oct. 19 to require software to reject ambiguous payment-hash and payment-secret fields. The change follows a developer’s account of an attack that made completed Bitcoin withdrawals appear unpaid.
The merged change targets software components reading the same signed payment request differently. A payment hash identifies the payment a component is tracking. Bitcoin Optech highlighted the rule change on Oct. 23.
In a Sept. 10 statement on the proposal, developer Roasbeef reported a recent hack of a Telegram peer-to-peer bot that exploited libraries choosing different hashes: some took the first payment-hash field in an invoice, while others took the last. He gave no incident date or loss figure.
In practical terms, a service could track a withdrawal under one hash while its node executes a payment using another. The service could then mistake the completed withdrawal for an unpaid one, creating an opening for further payouts. The failure sits in the connection between payment execution and the service’s accounting.
What readers must reject
The current BOLT11 specification requires exactly one payment-hash field, labeled p, and exactly one payment-secret field, labeled s. A missing field or a second occurrence requires payment failure. The rule covers both kinds of ambiguity, while the described withdrawal attack concerned conflicting payment hashes.
Readers must count field occurrences. The proposal’s invalid test cases include an invoice repeating the same hash, as well as one containing distinct hashes. Collapsing identical values into a single value would therefore miss an invoice the rule requires readers to reject.
The implementation timeline also matters. The Lightning node software lnd merged duplicate-hash rejection on Sept. 23, before the specification change. Its available v0.20.5-beta and v0.21.4-beta releases include that payment-hash fix.
The broader payment-secret checks are addressed by a separate lnd proposal that remained open as of Oct. 27. It would tighten payment-secret and other decoder checks, including rejecting a second s field. The author also explains that some invoices accepted by the decoder already face checks later in payment processing, so decoding success alone does not establish that a payment will go through.
For payment operators, the documented failure points to two checks: reject ambiguous invoices and ensure withdrawal accounting follows the same payment hash as the node.

articles.title: Iran-linked Bitcoin activity fell about 80%, then rebounded during the blackout
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Chainalysis reports Bitcoin activity in its selected everyday-use series exceeded 75% of baseline by Iran’s 2026 blackout’s end.
- Cloudflare observed partial restoration on May 26, 2026; its traffic readings use a different baseline and do not measure household access.
- Offline signing still requires a route to broadcast a transaction, while receiving Bitcoin does not require the recipient to be online.
By the end of Iran's prolonged February-to-May 2026 internet shutdown, Bitcoin transaction activity in Chainalysis's selected everyday-use series had recovered to over 75% of its baseline after an initial fall of around 80%, the blockchain analytics company reported Oct. 26.
The rebound developed while the blackout was still in place. Some Iran-attributed activity was reaching the network during severe restrictions, while the number of people with dependable access to their funds remains unmeasured.
The findings come from Chainalysis's new Middle East and North Africa analysis, covering July 2025 through June 2026. Independent traffic observations from Cloudflare document the prolonged disruption and its partial easing.
A recovery inside the shutdown
The longer shutdown began Feb. 28. Cloudflare observed traffic from Iran fall to well under 1% of previous levels, while Chainalysis reports that Bitcoin transaction activity initially fell around 80%.
The two series then followed different courses. Chainalysis says Bitcoin activity gradually climbed during the restriction period, reaching over 75% of its baseline by the blackout's end. After restrictions began easing in late May, activity rose to nearly twice baseline.
Cloudflare's account of the May reconnection, published May 27, records the subsequent network change. It observed a marked rise in traffic and DNS queries beginning around 11 a.m. UTC on May 26, 87 days after the second shutdown began, and described a partial restoration.
At its May 26 peak, traffic reached only 40% of the maximum Cloudflare had observed earlier in 2026. IPv6 traffic remained effectively zero.
January provides a shorter comparison. Chainalysis reports nearly 90% fewer Bitcoin transactions in the first week of that blackout than in its baseline period, followed by activity exceeding baseline when restrictions lifted. Cloudflare dates the first shutdown to Jan. 8, with brief traffic returns on Jan. 21 and Jan. 25 before fuller recovery began Jan. 27.
The percentages have different denominators. Cloudflare measures traffic across its network and DNS activity; Chainalysis reports Bitcoin transaction activity against its own baseline. Dividing them would not produce a measure of Bitcoin's relative resilience or the share of Iranians who could connect.
A transaction count cannot reveal whether access broadened across households or became concentrated among a smaller group that could transact repeatedly. The Iran analysis does not specify exact baseline dates, unique-holder counts or repeat-wallet concentration. Its approximate percentage comparisons remain Chainalysis's reported estimates.
Country attribution adds a further limit. Chainalysis's 2026 methodology locates personal wallets through behavioral indicators, including interaction with an exchange serving a single country. That differs from its allocation of service activity using website traffic. Transfers whose country provenance cannot be confidently assigned are excluded from its general country estimates.
An Iran-linked wallet therefore does not directly establish where its operator was when a transaction reached the network.
Selective connectivity can coexist with a severe national blackout. In a Jan. 21 analysis of the earlier shutdown, network monitoring company Kentik observed residual traffic and temporary access for Iranian universities. That January evidence illustrates the distinction between national suppression and complete disconnection.
Chainalysis suggests Starlink or other means as possible explanations for adaptation. Its Iran activity account supplies no transaction-level evidence tying recovery to a particular bypass route.
From keeping keys to using funds
For a holder, several separate steps sit between possessing Bitcoin and using it during a shutdown.
Private keys can remain stored offline. Signing a transaction can also happen offline. The Bitcoin Developer Guide separates key distribution, signing and networked broadcasting. A signing device need not connect directly to the internet, but the resulting transaction still needs a path to the network.
The guide's description of transaction relay explains how peers pass valid transactions onward.
Receiving presents another distinction. In the guide's ordinary payment sequence, a sender can pay an address supplied earlier without the recipient being online at that moment. The recipient still needs network information to observe and verify the payment, and a subsequent spend requires authorization and delivery of a new transaction.
Chainalysis separately reports that cross-border stablecoin inflows initially fell nearly 50% during the conflict, then surpassed their own baseline after the April 7 ceasefire while the second blackout continued. That inbound-flow measure covers a different asset and metric from the Bitcoin transaction series.
CryptoSlate's January analysis of Bitcoin access during Iran's blackout framed practical usefulness around connectivity and functioning exchange and payment infrastructure. The October retrospective adds the observed collapse-and-recovery pattern.
The new evidence shows that severe restrictions coexisted with substantial Iran-linked Bitcoin activity as the prolonged blackout wore on.

articles.title: Kraken opens Bitcoin and Ethereum options to eligible European traders
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Kraken has opened Bitcoin and Ether options to eligible EEA clients through existing derivatives accounts on Kraken Pro.
- Options share futures collateral, with portfolio margin enabled by default so offsetting positions can reduce required margin.
- The separate Unified Wallet remains opt-in; options sellers can lose more than posted margin and may face unlimited losses.
Eligible traders in the European Economic Area can now trade Bitcoin and Ethereum options through their existing Kraken Pro derivatives accounts on web and mobile, Kraken announced Oct. 26. The contracts use the collateral already supporting their futures positions.
That extends an options rollout Kraken began in July for eligible professional and institutional clients. At that point, European access was scheduled for later in 2026. The October announcement confirms availability in EEA countries where Kraken offers derivatives, with an options appropriateness assessment required before trading.
The contracts are cash-settled. Premium, profit and loss, and final settlement are calculated in U.S. dollars, even when collateral is posted in another accepted currency. Expiries run from weekly and monthly contracts to quarterly and semiannual maturities.
Kraken accepts 30-plus currencies as collateral. Portfolio margin is enabled by default, so offsetting positions can lower the amount required to support the portfolio. Futures and options draw on the same pool, giving existing derivatives clients a shared source of collateral for both types of trade.
The options use futures-style margining: premium is not paid upfront, while gains and losses are marked against collateral. Options do not accrue funding payments, although perpetual contracts in the same account still do.
Kraken warns that buyers can lose their entire options position value, while sellers can lose substantially more than posted margin and may face unlimited losses.
Its European derivatives risk disclosure also warns that leverage amplifies gains and losses and that clients may have to provide additional collateral on short notice. Positions can be closed when collateral is insufficient.
Trading runs through a request-for-quote system. Clients can assemble a trade with up to five components, or legs, then review quotes that expire after a limited time. They can decline a quote, but accepting one makes the trade binding.
If a portfolio becomes distressed, Kraken says it uses a sealed-offer auction rather than liquidation through an order book.
The separate Unified Wallet choice
Default options portfolio margin is distinct from Kraken’s separate Unified Wallet upgrade. As CryptoSlate reported on Oct. 19, that setting requires manual activation before eligible spot and derivatives balances are pooled. Once enabled, default cross margin can expose eligible spot holdings to futures losses.

articles.title: Japan’s services inflation split complicates the BOJ outlook before Friday’s decision
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Japan’s September services producer inflation reached 3.7%, while the rate excluding international transport held steady at 2.9%.
- High-labor-cost services price growth slowed to 2.6%, complicating the policy signal before the BOJ’s October 30 decision.
- Bitcoin funding pressure remains conditional on the policy outlook, yen strength and independently observed deleveraging across risk assets.
Freight pushed Japan’s services producer inflation higher in September while price growth in labor-intensive services slowed, complicating the policy signal for Bitcoin investors watching Friday’s Bank of Japan decision. The potential crypto risk runs through yen borrowing costs and the currency’s response to the BOJ’s outlook.
The BOJ’s preliminary October 27 release put annual inflation in its Services Producer Price Index (SPPI) at 3.7%, up from August’s revised 3.5%. Ocean freight added 0.2 percentage points to the change in annual inflation, matching the overall net 0.2-point acceleration at published precision. That is its contribution to the acceleration, rather than its share of the inflation level.
Two narrower readings were steadier. Annual inflation excluding international transportation stayed at 2.9%, while price growth in services with a high labor-cost ratio eased to 2.6% from August’s revised 2.7%.
The SPPI measures services sold to businesses and governments, so its labor-cost grouping tracks selling prices rather than employee pay. It is also distinct from consumer inflation. The BOJ’s underlying-inflation framework considers how widely consumer prices are rising alongside labor tightness, the output gap, expectations and wage growth.
Separate wage evidence adds another dimension: final August labor-survey results, released October 23, show scheduled cash earnings rose 3.8% from a year earlier across all employment types at establishments with at least five employees.
The yen-funding test
The BOJ meets October 29–30, with its policy statement and the Bank’s View section of the October Outlook Report scheduled for Friday, October 30. Its September 18 decision set the overnight call-rate target around 1.25%, effective September 24. The bank retained a path toward further increases, with their timing and pace dependent on activity, prices, financial conditions and outlook risks.
For positions financed with borrowed yen, a tighter-than-expected policy path could lift funding costs. Yen appreciation would also make that debt more expensive to repay from other currencies. Together, those conditions could force leveraged investors to reduce risk, potentially affecting Bitcoin exposure.
The Bank for International Settlements’ August 2024 analysis illustrates how leveraged equity and currency unwinds, deleveraging and higher margin requirements can amplify volatility. That historical example does not quantify current yen-funded Bitcoin positions or establish a fresh unwind.
A more persuasive warning would combine markets pricing in higher Japanese short-term rates, yen strength and independently observed deleveraging across risk assets. Yen weakness or stable funding would weaken the case.

articles.title: Bitcoin's next rally could trigger selling from holders of 874,000 BTC
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Bitcoin faces potential selling pressure near $82,500, where Bitfinex estimates investors accumulated approximately 874,000 BTC.
- US spot Bitcoin ETFs lost $663 million across three sessions, with BlackRock accounting for all $110.3 million in Monday's inflows.
- The Fed's Oct. 28 decision could determine whether fresh buying overcomes resistance or Bitcoin retreats toward its $77,500 support zone.
Bitcoin faces a potential selling hurdle near $82,500, where Bitfinex estimates investors hold 874,000 BTC.
Data from CryptoSlate shows the cryptocurrency fell as low as $79,370 over the past 24 hours after losing its $81,300 support level. It later recovered to $80,102, though further gains could face selling from holders seeking to exit near their purchase prices.
The potential resistance comes as US spot Bitcoin ETF demand remains uneven following substantial withdrawals last week, raising questions about whether buyers can absorb the available supply ahead of Wednesday's Federal Reserve interest-rate decision.
Bitcoin's $82,500 resistance looms as ETF buying remains concentrated
According to Bitfinex's Oct. 26 report, approximately 874,000 BTC was accumulated between $81,000 and $82,500, creating a substantial concentration of holdings above current market prices.
The exchange identified $81,300 as a critical price level that had supported Bitcoin for several weeks before the cryptocurrency closed below it on Oct. 22, 23, and 24.
That breakdown followed a failed recovery toward $84,930 and culminated in Bitcoin falling to $79,250 on Oct. 24, marking a 9.3% decline from its September high.
Bitfinex said the former support level has now become resistance, with investors who previously purchased Bitcoin around that range potentially using subsequent rallies to reduce their exposure.
The 874,000 BTC estimate reflects coins associated with the price range rather than confirmed sell orders. However, even a fraction of those holdings returning to the market could complicate recovery attempts if fresh buying remains limited.
The immediate concern is whether institutional demand can absorb that potential selling pressure.
Early signals from US spot Bitcoin ETFs remain mixed. The funds attracted $110.3 million in net inflows on Oct. 26, entirely driven by BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), while every other listed fund recorded zero net flows.
Monday's inflows followed two consecutive withdrawal sessions totaling $773.5 million, suggesting ETF demand has yet to broadly recover.
The three sessions left the ETFs with approximately $663 million in net outflows, underlining the challenge of sustaining a Bitcoin rebound without stronger buying demand.
Fed decision adds pressure to Bitcoin's recovery attempt
The uncertainty surrounding Bitcoin's recovery is compounded by increasing activity in derivatives markets.
Bitfinex reported that aggregate Bitcoin futures open interest increased from 645,411 BTC on Oct. 21 to 669,253 BTC on Oct. 25, even as the cryptocurrency declined.
The increase suggests outstanding futures positions grew during the sell-off, potentially amplifying volatility if a sharp price move triggers liquidations.
Bitfinex also identified liquidation concentrations around $82,300 to $83,000, creating conditions for a potential short squeeze if renewed buying pushes Bitcoin through the resistance area.
However, downside risks remain substantial.
The exchange identified another concentration of about 739,000 BTC accumulated between $77,500 and $80,000, which could provide support if the cryptocurrency sells off further.
A deeper decline would bring the $77,765 level into focus. That represents Bitcoin's True Market Mean, an on-chain measure of the average acquisition price of economically active supply.
The immediate macroeconomic catalyst is the Federal Reserve's Oct. 28 policy announcement, which could influence investors' appetite for risk assets.
Bitfinex noted that traders had substantially reduced expectations for an October interest-rate increase, with the implied probability falling to 9.4% as of Oct. 25.
Its Oct. 25 snapshot also showed futures markets assigning a 72.1% probability to a December rate increase, suggesting expectations for tighter monetary policy had shifted toward the end of the year.
That positioning leaves Bitcoin sensitive to the Fed's guidance, particularly if policymakers signal that borrowing costs could remain elevated or rise further.
Investors will receive additional economic signals on Oct. 29, when the US Bureau of Economic Analysis publishes its advance estimate of third-quarter GDP alongside September personal income and outlays data, including the Federal Reserve's preferred PCE inflation measure.
Stronger-than-expected inflation could reinforce expectations of a December rate increase and weaken demand for risk assets. Softer readings, meanwhile, could reduce those expectations and encourage renewed buying across Bitcoin and other speculative markets.

articles.title: Bitcoin simulations show why a return to $126,000 would not last
articles.text:
Quick Take
- A historical-return model puts Bitcoin's one-year crossing frequency at 50.4%, versus 34.8% for finishing above its record.
- Among simulated paths crossing within a year, median pre-crossing drawdown is 18.9%, revealing losses a terminal target cannot describe.
- Four of seven selected historical recoveries dipped below their old closing record within 30 days.
Even if Bitcoin could clear its old record, a true recovery would still be unfinished. In a CryptoSlate simulation using historical returns, 50.4% of paths closed above $126,198 at least once within a year, but only 34.8% finished above it. The gap was 15.6 percentage points: roughly one path in six reclaimed the level, then ended below it.
Those outcomes expose the question a price target cannot answer: what happens between buying Bitcoin and reaching the forecast date?
CryptoSlate's one-year Bitcoin prediction puts the median terminal price at $124,281 on Oct. 26, 2027, from an Oct. 26, 2026 reference close of $80,007. The Bitcoin page lists its record at $126,198, reached Oct. 6, 2025.
Crossing the line is only the first event
A terminal forecast represents prices at an endpoint. A crossing estimate asks whether the price clears a barrier on any earlier observation. Staying above it requires a third test, covering what follows the first reclaim.
For this analysis, we resampled historical returns in seven-day blocks to generate 100,000 paths using Coin Metrics daily prices. Coin Metrics measures a multi-market USD reference close at the end of each UTC day. The simulation starts at its Oct. 26 close of $79,950, distinct from the published forecast's origin. It uses 1,096 daily log returns from Oct. 26, 2023, through Oct. 26, 2026, preserving their historical average return. Data were captured as of 10:47 UTC on Oct. 27; Oct. 26 was the latest completed observation.
A crossing here means a daily reference close above the published record's dollar value, which may have been set intraday.
The crossing-versus-finishing frequencies were 0.15% versus 0.11% over 30 days and 6.37% versus 4.21% over 90 days, widening to 50.4% versus 34.8% over 365 days. Very small short-horizon counts warrant particular caution.
The distinction becomes sharper after the initial reclaim. In 42.1% of all paths, Bitcoin crossed and subsequently closed below the barrier at least once. Some recovered again, which is why that figure exceeds the 15.6% that crossed but finished below. Overall, 65.2% ended below the record, including paths that never reached it.
Paths that crossed the record still carried losses. Among paths crossing within 365 days, the median first crossing took 189 days. Their median maximum drawdown before crossing was 18.9%; the 90th percentile was 30.7%.
That drawdown measures a decline from a running peak, which can form after the simulation starts. A separate starting-price test found that 11.4% of those crossing paths first fell at least 20% below their initial price; 2.3% fell at least 30%.
History supplies a similar distinction without supplying a reliable probability. The Coin Metrics series identifies seven completed recoveries from drawdowns of at least 30%, using previous daily closing records established since 2013. Four slipped back below their old record within 30 days. All seven experienced a peak-to-trough correction of at least 20% within 90 days after the first reclaim, even when they remained above the old record.
Trough-to-reclaim times ranged from 20 to 771 days, with a median of 122. Maximum drawdowns between the trough and reclaim ranged from 10.9% to 61.4%. These are selected successful episodes, with troughs identified in hindsight.
The gap survives; the odds move
The specific probabilities are sensitive to assumptions. Across six separate scenarios using normal returns with zero or historical average log drift, 25% lower or higher volatility, fat-tailed Student-t returns, and the block bootstrap, one-year crossing frequencies ranged from 17.8% to 52.3%, while finishing-above frequencies ranged from 9.3% to 35.4%. Every scenario retained a gap.
A simple historical comparison also produced a gap: across 4,317 overlapping one-year windows since 2014, Bitcoin exceeded the same required percentage gain during 63.1% of windows and finished above it in 51%. Shared observations and changing market regimes prevent treating those windows as independent trials.
CryptoSlate's own one-year forecast assigns 100% weight to Student-t GARCH. Its reported CRPS edge, which scores the full distribution, is negative 0.4% against its strongest simple baseline, with a negative 5.8% lower bound. In that held-out test, the more elaborate forecast did not outperform the baseline.
The useful finding is therefore about the recovery's shape, rather than a precise chance of success. Bitcoin's next record is a threshold. A durable recovery also requires surviving the approach, holding the breakout and remaining above it when the investor's horizon ends. One price cannot stand in for all three.

articles.title: Arsenal thua sốc đội hạng Tư, lập hàng loạt cột mốc đáng quên
articles.text:
TPO - Một cơn địa chấn thực sự đã làm rung chuyển vòng 4 Cúp Liên đoàn Anh (EFL Cup) khi Fleetwood Town - đội đang thi đấu ở League Two - tạo nên kỳ tích lịch sử bằng chiến thắng 5-3 trước Arsenal trên chấm luân lưu. Kết quả chấn động này biến Pháo thủ trở thành kẻ làm nền cho những kỷ lục đáng quên.
Arsenal trở thành nhà đương kim vô địch Ngoại hạng Anh đầu tiên bị một đối thủ hạng Tư (Fleetwood chơi bóng ở hạng đấu cấp bậc thứ 4 nước Anh sau Ngoại hạng Anh, Championship, League One) loại khỏi đấu trường Cúp Liên đoàn. Đáng chú ý, đây cũng mới chỉ là lần thứ 2 trong lịch sử đại diện Bắc London chịu cú sốc tương tự trước một CLB hạng Tư, gợi lại ký ức cay đắng trước Bradford ở mùa giải 2012/13.
Ngay từ tiếng còi khai cuộc, Arsenal nhanh chóng áp đặt thế trận với sức ép liên hồi. Tuy nhiên, đội chủ nhà Fleetwood Town mới là những người tạo nên bất ngờ lớn khi bất ngờ vươn lên dẫn trước ở phút 21.
Loupalo-Bi có pha đi bóng đầy dũng mãnh, vượt qua trung vệ trẻ Marli Salmon trước khi dứt điểm hiểm hóc vào góc xa khung thành, không cho thủ môn đội khách cơ hội cản phá. Dù nỗ lực dâng cao đội hình để đáp trả, song Arsenal vấp phải khối bê tông phòng ngự vô cùng kỷ luật và kiên cường từ phía đội bóng chiếu dưới.
Arsenal đã nhận kết quả khó tin
Bước sang hiệp hai, sức ép của Arsenal cuối cùng cũng được cụ thể hóa ở phút 50. Xuất phát từ đường treo bóng khó chịu của Ceedach O'Neill vào vòng cấm, Viktor Gyokeres chớp thời cơ dứt điểm cận thành trong một pha bóng lộn xộn để đưa trận đấu về vạch xuất phát.
Pháo thủ hừng hực khí thế dồn ép nhằm hoàn tất màn lội ngược dòng. Dẫu vậy, đây lại là ngày thi đấu đáng quên của Kai Havertz. Tiền đạo người Đức liên tiếp phung phí những cơ hội mười mươi: cú sút cận chân đầu tiên bị trung vệ Rhys Bennett lăn xả chặn đứng, và chỉ ít phút sau, anh lại sút bóng đi trúng mép lưới bên ngoài ở một vị trí vô cùng thuận lợi.
Kịch tính trận đấu bị đẩy lên cao trào khi thời gian chính thức chỉ còn lại 5 phút. Max Dowman nhận thẻ đỏ trực tiếp vì hành vi phi thể thao, trở thành cầu thủ Arsenal đầu tiên bị truất quyền thi đấu tại giải đấu này sau nửa thập kỷ. Dù phải thi đấu thiếu người, đoàn quân của HLV Mikel Arteta vẫn miệt mài tấn công và tạo ra một số cơ hội định đoạt trận đấu trong những phút bù giờ. Song, sự vô duyên ở khâu dứt điểm buộc hai đội phải bước vào loạt luân lưu.
Trên chấm 11m, Arsenal thực hiện thành công cả 3 lượt sút đầu tiên, nhưng bước ngoặt xảy ra khi cú đá của Bruno Guimaeres bị thủ thành Jay Lynch xuất sắc cản phá. Bản lĩnh kiên cường giúp Fleetwood Town chuyển hóa trọn vẹn cả 5 lượt sút thành bàn thắng, ấn định thắng lợi nghẹt thở 5-3 để hiên ngang giành vé vào vòng tứ kết EFL Cup lần đầu tiên trong lịch sử.
