articles.title: Stock futures are little changed as traders await Fed decision, Big Tech earnings: Live updates
articles.text:
U.S. equity futures were little changed on Tuesday evening as investors await earnings reports from megacap technology companies and a rate policy decision from the Federal Reserve due Wednesday.
S&P 500 futures and Nasdaq-100 futures were flat.
In Asia, Japan's Nikkei 225 added over 0.7% while the Topix rose 0.3%. South Korea's Kospi gained over 2% at open, while the small-cap Kosdaq rose 1.8%. Australia's benchmark S&P/ASX 200 was 0.8% higher.
In Tuesday's regular U.S. trading, the major averages ended the session higher. Chip stocks rose again, this time powered by an announcement from Broadcom that a group of banks would provide $63 billion in financing to buy the company's chips and networking solutions to be leased to Anthropic, the company behind Claude. Broadcom rose 4%, while Advanced Micro Devices climbed 5.5% and Micron Technology rose 2.8%.
Those moves led the Nasdaq Composite to rise 1.2% on the session.
Stocks were also supported by lower oil prices, which fell following news that Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei met with the nation's top security official Mohsen Rezaei to discuss conditions for ending the war with the U.S.
On Wednesday, though, focus will turn to domestic monetary policy as the Fed wraps up its two-day policy meeting. The central bank is widely predicted to keep interest rates steady at a target rate range of 3.75% to 4%. Policymakers raised rates by a quarter percentage point at their September meeting.
According to CME's FedWatch tool, there's a roughly 92% chance that the Fed maintains the current interest rate, but some expect that Chairman Kevin Warsh will signal that more hikes are coming in future policy meetings. The decision on interest rates will be announced at 2:00 p.m. ET.
After the bell on Wednesday, though, investors will turn their focus to the AI trade, as "Magnificent Seven" giants Alphabet and Microsoft will kick off Big Tech earnings.
Tech stocks, particularly those with exposure to the AI buildout, have struggled in recent weeks amid questions over the technology's financing. However, Morgan Stanley's chief U.S. equity strategist, Mike Wilson, thinks that the recent recovery in tech stocks is a sign that trend may be nearing its end.
"Most of the correction is already over," he said in an appearance on CNBC's "Closing Bell" on Tuesday. "We've been in correction mode for four or five months.... the market I think has digested this very efficiently."

articles.title: Grand jury rejects DOJ bid to indict ex-Trump WH aide Cassidy Hutchinson: Reports
articles.text:
A federal grand jury Tuesday rejected a request by the Department of Justice to indict former White House aide Cassidy Hutchinson over her 2022 congressional testimony about President Donald Trump's conduct during the Jan. 6, 2021, mob attack on the U.S. Capitol, The Washington Post reported.
Prosecutors in the DOJ's Civil Rights Division sought to charge Hutchinson with a crime based on claims she made false statements, MS NOW said, citing two people with knowledge of the case.
Hutchinson told lawmakers a second-hand account about Trump angrily lunging at a security aide after being told he could not go to the Capitol that day.
Senior DOJ lawyer Neville Hedley, without naming Hutchinson in open court, on Tuesday told Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui that the grand jury in U.S. District Court in Washington, D.C., had rejected a requested indictment, The Post reported.
It is extremely rare for a grand jury to refuse to indict when prosecutors present evidence of alleged crimes.
But since Trump returned to the White House in January 2025, federal prosecutors in Washington have several times failed to obtain a grand jury indictment they sought.
In recent weeks, prosecutors have filed separate criminal cases in U.S. District Court in D.C. against former FBI Director James Comey and two former FBI officials with charging documents other than grand jury indictments.
In both cases, the alleged conduct occurred years earlier. Typically in such cases, prosecutors would seek a grand jury indictment.
Hutchinson testified in June 2022 to the House Select Committee that investigated the Jan. 6 Capitol riot by a mob of Trump supporters, whose attack delayed for hours the confirmation of Joe Biden's electoral victory in the 2020 election.
She said that after Trump spoke at a rally outside the White House that preceded the attack, then-White House official Tony Ornato asked her, "Did you effing hear what happened in [the president's vehicle,] The Beast?"
She testified that Ornato told her that when Trump got in the car, he was under the impression from his then-Chief of Staff Mark Meadows that they going to the Capitol, as he had claimed in his speech to supporters at the rally.
When Robert Engel, the head of Trump's security detail, said the president could not go there because the area was not secure, Trump "had a very strong, a very angry response to that," Hutchinson testified that Ornato said.
"Tony described him as being irate," Hutchinson said, noting that Trump had said something like: "I'm the effing president, take me up to the Capitol now," according to Ornato.
When Engel refused again to drive him to the Capitol, Trump "reached up towards the front of the vehicle to grab at the steering wheel. Mr. Engel grabbed his arm, said, 'Sir, you need to take your hand off the steering wheel. We're going back to the West Wing,'" Hutchinson testified.
Trump "then used his free hand to lunge toward Bobby Engel," Hutchinson said she was told by Ornato.
Correction: Neville Hedley is a senior DOJ lawyer. An earlier version misspelled his name.

articles.title: Trump administration may let more Russian diesel onto market, energy secretary tells CNBC
articles.text:
The U.S. may allow more diesel fuel from Russia onto the global market depending on Moscow's behavior, Energy Secretary Chris Wright told CNBC in an interview Tuesday.
Wright framed the Trump administration's suspension of U.S. sanctions against Russian diesel exports earlier this month as "an incentive" for Moscow to end the war in Ukraine. It will help with fuel supplies on the margin, he said.
The Russian-flagged tanker Talisman is expected to arrive on the U.S. East Coast on Nov. 9, according to the ship-tracking platform MarineTraffic. Another tanker, the Leruo, has departed Russia en route to the "Atlantic Coast" without explicitly declaring its destination as the U.S.
More tankers with Russian diesel could "quite possibly" set sail under the U.S. sanctions waiver, Wright told CNBC's "Power Lunch."
"It's trying to put a carrot in front of Russia," the energy secretary said.
President Donald Trump struck a deal with President Vladimir Putin for Russia to export 800,000 metric tons of diesel in October and November, followed by another million tons.
Trump reached the agreement with Putin as he faces political pressure to reduce surging diesel prices ahead of the U.S. midterm elections next Tuesday. Fuel prices have spiked since the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran on Feb. 28.
But the diesel volumes in the Trump-Putin deal won't materially lower prices because the shipments are small compared with total global demand of around 28 million barrels per day, analysts say.
The first shipment from Russia of 300,000 metric tons is equivalent to about 75,000 barrels per day if rolled out over one month. The second tranche, of 500,000 metric tons, equals about 124,000 bpd.
Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has sharply criticized the diesel deal. Kyiv has pounded Russian refineries this year in an effort to cut the revenue the Kremlin collects from energy exports and curtail Moscow's ability to wage war.
The strikes forced Moscow to implement a diesel export ban in July. The Kremlin has partially lifted that ban to fulfill the Trump-Putin deal.
Several Republican senators also slammed the deal, signing a letter with Democratic colleagues that condemned the agreement as "a gift to our adversary and a betrayal of our Allies."

articles.title: Chart: Anthropic's cash pile towers over nearly every U.S. company
articles.text:
Anthropic has more cash than almost every company in America.
The nearly 6-year-old artificial intelligence lab disclosed on Monday in an S-1 filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission that it had $112.4 billion in cash, plus another $19.3 billion in short-term investments, as of June 30.
Anthropic's total of $131.7 billion surpasses every non-bank U.S. company, except for Berkshire Hathaway and Alphabet, according to data compiled by CNBC and S&P Capital IQ.
As of midyear, Anthropic had more cash than Amazon, SpaceX, Meta and Microsoft. It had more than Nvidia and Apple combined.
Depending on how much the company raises in its initial public offering — and reports suggest it could top $100 billion — Anthropic could bump its hoard to more than $230 billion in cash.
So far, Anthropic hasn't shared specific details about its offering size, and it said in the filing that existing investors would also be selling into the IPO – meaning the company itself won't collect the entire fundraise. Those details are expected to be disclosed in about two weeks.
Never before has a company gone public with anywhere near this amount of cash.
Anthropic's trove underscores the fundraising prowess that has allowed it to amass an aggregate of $141 billion in private financing in just six years since its founding. However, given the company's future commitments for computing power that have yet to hit its expenses, Anthropic will have to continue accumulating cash through fundraising or generating profits to fulfill its obligations.
Anthropic's first-half compute and infrastructure expenses totaled $8.95 billion. But the company said it usually buys computing power 12 to 18 months ahead of time, and only recognizes expenses as that capacity becomes available. That means the first-half expense figure doesn't capture the full scale of its future obligations.
As of June 30, Anthropic disclosed $321.4 billion in estimated future undiscounted lease obligations and $265.6 billion in expected future fixed or minimum-guaranteed commitments — more than half a trillion total. These will commence within the next few years, with terms ranging from one year to 20 years.
Additionally, the company said that subsequent to June 30, it entered into new and amended agreements with a minimum future payment obligation of about $245 billion.
The company hasn't shared an aggregate amount of its up-to-date commitments yet.
If Anthropic's cash is king, compute is its biggest claim on the crown.
—CNBC's Ritika Shah and Nick Wells contributed to this article.

articles.title: Polymarket faces renewed CFTC probe over U.S. access to offshore platform
articles.text:
The Commodity Futures Trading Commission is investigating whether prediction market platform Polymarket violated a 2022 settlement meant to ban U.S. users from its offshore platform, according to a person familiar with the matter.
The investigation is part of a broader probe the agency opened into Polymarket earlier this year, after a Wall Street Journal expose said Polymarket paid content creators to post videos showing simulated trades and fabricated wins on dummy versions of its website.
The latest inquiry focuses on whether Polymarket previously broke the 2022 settlement, and is unrelated to the platform's present operations, said the person, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they are not authorized to speak publicly.
The federal agency is inquiring into Polymarket controls that are meant to detect where customers are located, as well as the platform's advertising in the U.S., the person added.
The CFTC is also looking into the company's U.S. platform that launched in late December, specifically in its customer onboarding processes and protection measures, according to the source. Reuters first reported the latest investigation.
The person familiar with the inquiry did not provide a start date for when the CFTC began investigating Polymarket.
News of the CFTC probe comes one week before the Nov. 3 midterm elections, with polls showing Democrats leading to take control of the House of Representatives from Republicans, and a neck and neck race for the Senate, amid escalating concern from mental health experts and lawmakers about prediction markets' explosive growth in the past year.
Polymarket declined to comment on the investigation. The CFTC did not respond to a request for comment.
In 2022, Polymarket stopped U.S. users from accessing its platform and paid a $1.4 million civil penalty to the CFTC as part of an enforcement settlement with the agency during the Biden administration.
In 2024, the CFTC opened a probe into whether Polymarket was complying with that agreement, and the Justice Department opened a related investigation. Both federal agencies closed those investigations into the platform in July 2025.
Disclosure: CNBC and Kalshi have a commercial relationship that includes customer acquisition and a minority investment.

articles.title: Stocks making the biggest moves after hours: Visa, Robinhood, NXP, Seagate and more
articles.text:
Market Insider

Enphase sees revenue ranging from $225 million to $255 million, falling short of analysts' estimate for $297.6 million, per FactSet.

articles.title: Walmart says AI training is boosting confidence with the technology among its 2.1 million associates
articles.text:
As enterprise AI investment continues to grow, companies of all sizes are trying to figure out how employees feel about the technology in the workplace.
Walmart, the biggest private employer in the world, asked its 2.1 million associates in June that exact question for the first time, trying to get a sense of how one of the most diverse workforces is experiencing AI.
What it found, based on more than 1.7 million survey responses, is that while workers have different levels of familiarity and comfort with AI, training and experience with the technology matters.
Seventy-seven percent of Walmart's office-based associates said are excited about AI's potential to improve their work, Walmart Chief People Officer for Associate Experience and Digital Maren Waggoner told CNBC's Leslie Picker at the 2026 CNBC Workforce Executive Council Summit in New York City.
And as for Walmart's U.S. frontline associates, 84% said they are confident using digital tools, a reflection of the AI-powered tools that many of them are now using in their roles, she said.
"We've given them certificates, we've given them training programs and tools, and so they're using it in their day-to-day," Waggoner said.
In the last 13 months, Walmart has partnered with both Google and OpenAI around learning and AI certification programs for associates at no cost. Waggoner said that associates who went through OpenAI training said they had a 27% confidence gain using AI.
That has helped Walmart buck some of the larger trends around AI across the country. While about 52% of U.S. adults say they are more concerned than excited about AI, according to an August 2026 Pew Research Center poll, Walmart associates report greater comfort and excitement, Walmart data showed.
"Providing the tools, providing the training; they feel more confident," Waggoner said.
While AI is perhaps the biggest technological revolution that Walmart has gone through over its 64-year history, Waggoner said the company's approach to transformation has remained the same.
"We have a pretty bold mission statement around being a people-led, tech-powered omni-channel retailer that is ultimately dedicated to helping save money," she said. "The people-led and tech-powered piece has been around for a while."
Many workers across the economy say they are afraid of AI replacing their jobs. While Waggoner said Walmart is finding ways to use AI to automate processes in fulfillment centers, for example, the retailer's efforts with the technology are to "reduce some of that friction and use robotics to help, and then really focus the work on human judgement."
In fact, Waggoner said, at the company's innovation lab in Dallas, Texas, automated efforts to reduce the physical tasks previously performed by humans have instead created more quality assurance-type roles as opposed to broader job losses.
And on the front lines of stores, Waggoner said Walmart has found that its customers "actually like talking to a human at checkout."
That has allowed associates to focus their efforts on using AI to solve customer challenges.
Waggoner pointed to a store manager in Mexico that she met earlier this year who built his own AI agent to look at reports and drive fresh produce sales.
"He's using the tool, but he's still running the store," she said. "The store manager job is still there. He's using the tools and technology to drive his business. And by the way, his fresh sales are through the roof."

articles.title: Robinhood shares fall 4% as crypto slump weighs on profits, offsetting gains in new businesses
articles.text:
Robinhood shares fell 4% in after-hours trading as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.
Here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with Wall Street estimates, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:
- Earnings per share: 51 cents vs. 56 cents expected
- Revenue: $1.42 billion vs. $1.42 billion expected
Robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year.
Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting the focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity.
Robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly important sources of transaction revenue, while the company has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings.
Transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million.
Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million.
Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading.
Net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026. Over the past year, net deposits totaled $71 billion, representing 21% growth compared with total platform assets at the end of Q3 2025.
—With reporting from CNBC's Robert Hum and Kate Rooney

articles.title: How investors can position ahead of the Fed's next policy decision
articles.text: The Federal Reserve's October rate decision has been a focus for investors and economists as Chairman Kevin Warsh has rejected traditional forward guidance. Fed officials are widely expected to keep rates unchanged, with the CME Group's FedWatch tool showing a roughly 90% chance the central bank's target range for the federal funds rate remains at 3.75% to 4%. But Warsh's tone and commentary in the news conference following Wednesday's announcement will be closely watched, with EY-Parthenon chief economist Gregory Daco calling it a "delicate balancing exercise" with real implications for the markets. "Warsh will have to dispel any impression that the policy decision was political, ahead of the midterms. Then, he will be pushed to justify a pause following the September insurance rate hike and three hotter-than-expected inflation reports," wrote Daco in an Oct. 23 note. "While he will want to avoid forward guidance, he cannot risk the Fed's credibility by saying the Fed simply wants more time to assess the data, as that would undermine the urgency of the September move and could lead to a bond market selloff." Here is how a select group of investors see the Fed and the market opportunities and challenges going into the decision. The case for commodities SoFi chief market strategist Liz Thomas said investors should increase exposure to commodities regardless of the Fed's rate path going forward. "I think what you want to do right now is have exposure to all the different scenarios," said Thomas. "If we have a scenario where inflation stays high, [and] we've got weird weather patterns through the rest of the year, commodities are a place to hedge that." Thomas said the Invesco Optimum Yield Diversified Commodity Strategy ETF (PDBC) is one way to play the commodity market. PDBC has a net expense ratio of 0.59% and is up 51% year to date. PDBC YTD mountain PDBC year to date Phil Rosen, chief market strategist at Silvia, is also bullish on oil and energy regardless of the Fed decision. "XLE, I think that's a great play for the fourth quarter and going into 2027," said Rosen. "If you believe AI is going to be even half as good as the bulls think it is, we are going to need way more power and energy," he said, adding: "I don't see the Iran conflict stopping tomorrow or even in the coming weeks or months. That is also a tailwind." Energy is the best-performing sector in the S & P 500 in 2026, surging 55% in that time, as oil prices stay elevated due to the Iran war. Marathon Petroleum , Valero , Phillips 66 and APA have more than doubled year to date to lead the gains. Playing defense George Acheampong, founder of Capitalwize, sees opportunity in defensive sectors such as healthcare and consumer staples going into the Fed decision. "My preference is for businesses with durable demand, strong cash flow and the ability to protect margins if inflation stays elevated," he said. "My filter is pretty simple, can the business create shareholder value if the Fed offers no relief. I want companies that fund their own growth." The State Street Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLP) and the State Street Health Care Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLV) are two ways Acheampong is playing those two sectors. The former is up 8% in October, and the latter has rallied 6%. Thomas also sees upside in healthcare as a beneficiary of shifts in market sentiment and portfolio rotation . "Healthcare has been and will continue to be one of the beneficiaries as investors get nervous about technology," said Thomas. "Places like biotech and pharma have been that beneficiary for a while in this cycle and I think that continues to be the case." In healthcare, Rosen said Eli Lilly is his top pick. "They are best in class at GLP-1 pharmaceutical research and they are also a massive AI beneficiary and AI adopter." Eli Lilly shares are up 19% for the year, outpacing the S & P 500's 13% advance in that time. The stock is also on pace for its 10th consecutive annual gain. Ultra high net worth perspective Charlie Garcia, founder of R360, a group for investors with net worths of more than $100 million, said the group is very bullish on the upside of artificial intelligence and the AI build-out, but is focused on a simplified investment approach. "There are about 600 stocks with AI somewhere in the pitch and nobody can sort that out. So our members asked three plain questions: 'Who powers it?', 'Who pays for it?' and 'who houses it?'," said Garcia. The group has three top picks under that framework: Constellation Energy , Blackstone and Equinix . "These data centers eat electricity like a small city, so you look at Constellation Energy. Somebody has to finance hundreds of billions of dollars of buildings and data centers, so you look at Blackstone. The computers have to live somewhere so you look at Equinix — which is the biggest data center landlord in the world. If it's the 'gold rush' you don't have to know which miner strikes gold, you just sell the picks and shovels and the land," said Garcia. Tad Fallows, founder of Long Angle, a group that holds portfolios between $5 million and $100 million, said members are divided on the impact of the Fed decision on the market. A poll of members conducted Oct. 21-22 with more than 200 respondents showed 52% are rebalancing toward safe asset with 48% saying they are not. However, sentiment toward parts of AI trade is turning more bearish, according to Fallows. In the survey, 13% of members said the AI trade is "significantly overvalued," and 46% said it is 'somewhat overvalued'. "I would say the stocks that have seen the massive runup as part of the AI bubble," said Fallows citing names such Sandisk and Oracle as two stocks the group is bearish about and members may be looking to sell. Fallows added SpaceX and Tesla are also falling out of favor with Long Angle members. "There is a consensus bearishness on the Elon trade, you've got a quarter of people who are big time fanboys, but then three quarters of people saying this is absurd."

articles.title: AI debt fears ease ahead of Oracle, Alphabet and Amazon updates. Here's what to watch.
articles.text:
Fears over artificial intelligence debt have eased after a bout of volatility. But more tests for AI debt are coming.
Oracle holds its Investor Day on Wednesday. And hyperscalers Alphabet and Amazon.com are scheduled to report quarterly results after the market close on Wednesday and Thursday, respectively.
Credit markets are on edge over a flood of AI debt, though fears have eased up a little lately. Meta Platforms' plans for a $95 billion stock offering, announced on Monday, helped bring down its credit-default swap spreads. Those spreads had risen last week when the company reported negative free cash flow in the third quarter. Other CDS spreads had moved higher too, though they have since backed off.
Investors had expected Meta to bring a large bond deal to market shortly after its earnings announcement, said Richard Cheng, head of Nuveen's investment-grade corporate sector team. The fact that it wasn't announced came as a relief.
"Just the absence of the bond deal itself is a direct catalyst for AI-related spread tightening," he said.
A credit spread is the difference in the yield between the corporate bonds and Treasurys of similar maturities. When spreads tighten, it means investors are becoming more confident about the bond issuer.
Fears 'overblown'
The market action over the last few days shows that investors are recognizing that "credit fears may have been overblown," said CNBC contributor Paul Meeks, head of technology research at Freedom Capital Markets.
"I expect that these better feelings, maybe not good but better, may continue as companies announce their quarters over the next few weeks."
Still, spreads on CDS remain wider over the past year due to a surge of debt issuance and free cash flows turning negative across the AI space. Meta's CDS spread, for instance, is still up 177% year to date, while Amazon's spread has gained 129%.
Bond yields also remain elevated.
"It's not necessarily fundamentals," said CreditSights analyst Jordan Chalfin. "It's more, I'd say, 80% driven by technicals and sentiment."
Earnings in focus
Alphabet and Amazon pose the next big hurdle for tech bonds as they update their capex plans and free cash flow forecasts. Microsoft's earnings are also due Wednesday, but the company has yet to issue any bonds to pay for its AI spending.
Both Amazon and Alphabet reported negative free cash flow in the second quarter and analysts expect that trend to continue.
Analysts expect Alphabet to report free cash flow of -$2.3 billion while spending $55.2 billion on capital expenditures in the third quarter, according to FactSet consensus estimates. Amazon is expected to report -$9.9 billion in free cash flow against capex of $58.7 billion.
S&P Global Ratings estimated in an August report that the hyperscalers will have negative free operating cash flow in 2026 and 2027.
More critical will be their outlooks, Cheng says. "The singular focus on the investors' minds is really what the capex guidance trajectory looks like across the hyperscaler space."
Meeks believes elevated capex is a sign of strong AI demand. The hyperscalers have "decided that with all the evidence they have — and they have more than you and me — that this is worthwhile spending, and not just worthwhile; it's required," he said.
CreditSights' Chalfin doesn't expect the hyperscalers to announce major new bond issuance around their earnings reports. Oracle's updates may be more critical for credit markets. The company has issued $117 billion in long-term debt and is clinging to an investment-grade credit rating of BBB-, the lowest level of investment grade above junk, according to S&P.
"It's the most important IG tech credit, just given how it's a bit more stressed relative to the A-rated names," he said. "It's trading more like a high-yield credit, even though it's IG, and so there's just a lot of investor concern on that one."
Off-balance sheet debt
One wrinkle to the AI debt story: balance sheets don't reveal the whole picture. The companies are using complicated off-balance sheet arrangements for data centers and chip financing, and they aren't fully transparent, S&P Global said in a September report.
"There are commitments they are entering into, for example, into data center leases or purchase commitments on chips that aren't necessarily treated as debt," Mark Habib, digital infrastructure sector lead at S&P Global Ratings, said on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" Monday.
S&P is trying to provide the market with more visibility on those commitments "to give a fuller picture of what kinds of obligations they're actually entering into," he added.
Oracle aside, hyperscaler credit ratings are all comfortably above A levels — reflecting the fact that they have broadly diversified revenue streams, ample coverage for interest payments, and capacity to add leverage if they choose.
Nuveen's Cheng isn't concerned, pointing out that while there has been some credit repricing, there is no credit crisis.
"They continue to have exceptional credit profiles, strong cash generation liquidity," he said of the largest hyperscalers.
"The market is really not concerned about credit quality at this point," Cheng added. "It's really just the trajectory of the capex needs and the supply of debt to fund that. Both of those are pointing in one direction — and that's up."
Correction: This story has been revised to reflect that Oracle's investment-grade credit rating is BBB-, according to S&P. A previous version mischaracterized the company's credit rating.

articles.title: Neil Young sues Trump committee for $10M for playing 'Rockin' in the Free World' at rally
articles.text:
Legendary musician Neil Young filed a $10 million lawsuit against President Donald Trump's campaign committee for infringing Young's copyright by playing his song "Rockin' in the Free World" just before the president took the stage to speak at an Oct. 12 rally in Youngstown, Ohio.
The Trump 47 Committee has caused that song, without the musician's permission, "to be played numerous times at other rallies designed to encourage Republican votes in the upcoming mid-term elections," Young's lawsuit in U.S. District Court in Richmond, Virginia, alleges.
Trump "was personally aware that a license would be required to play the Song at rallies," and that Young "has not, and would not, grant the required license," the suit filed Monday says.
Young, 80, in 2020 sued another corporation formed by Trump, Donald J. Trump for President Inc., in Manhattan federal court for copyright infringement of "Rockin' in the Free World," and another song written by Young, "Devil's Sidewalk," for having played the songs without permission at campaign rallies.
In that first case, Trump's corporation "asserted no defense and immediately settled shortly after it was served, promising that it would never again use 'Rockin' in the Free World' without a license and permission from Young," the new suit said.
CNBC has requested comment from the Trump 47 Committee about the suit, and from Young's lawyers.
The White House, when asked for comment, referred CNBC to the Republican National Committee, which did not immediately respond to an email seeking comment.
Young, who was born in Canada, is a naturalized U.S. citizen. He is a two-time inductee in the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame: in 1995 as a solo artist, and in 1997 as a member of Buffalo Springfield. Young was also a member of the folk rock supergroup Crosby, Stills, Nash & Young.
Young released "Rockin' in the Free World" in 1989.
His lawsuit describes the tune as a "blistering anthem that contrasts the hollow promises of American political rhetoric with the harsh realities faced by the poor, homeless and forgotten."
The lyrics include descriptions of a mother discarding her baby, addiction, and "garbage piling in the shadows of prosperity — while the repeated chorus delivers savage irony, celebrating freedom that clearly isn't shared by all," the suit notes.
"In short, the Song is the opposite of everything that Donald J. Trump stands for," the suit says.
In addition to the Trump 47 Committee, the suit lists five other defendants, identified by the pseudonym "Doe," whom Young believes are liable for infringing on Young's copyright.
The Oct. 12 Trump rally that is referenced in the lawsuit was also the scene of an incident that has drawn attention from local law enforcement. Videos from the rally show several attendees apparently attacking and beating a woman, Blake Miley, who had repeatedly yelled 'fascist" at Trump while wearing a shirt bearing the message "Release the Epstein Files."
Mahoning County, Ohio, Sheriff Jerry Greene reportedly is investigating three individuals in connection with the incident.

articles.title: Boeing shares slide on a disappointing cash flow update. Why this dip is buyable
articles.text: Boeing shares tumbled Tuesday after the plane maker issued disappointing long-term guidance for free cash flow, overshadowing anything good in its third-quarter numbers. The silver lining is that management took its medicine and reset investor expectations now, so the stock can mount a rebound once the dust settles. Revenue in the third quarter increased 4% year over year to $24.19 billion, topping the consensus of $23.84 billion, according to estimates compiled by LSEG. Adjusted earnings per share (EPS) was a loss of 34 cents, steeper than the 21-cent loss the Street was expecting, LSEG data showed. Free cash flow (FCF) came in at $464 million, better than the $330 million expected, according to FactSet. Shares of Boeing are down 10% Tuesday, on pace for their worst day since the April 2025 tariff panic . The stock also sank to a fresh 52-week low. Even before Tuesday's earnings report, the stock was having a tough few months in the face of the Middle East conflict and issues ramping up production of some jet models. BA YTD mountain Boeing's year-to-date stock performance. Bottom line Boeing's actual third-quarter results were not terrible. The problem is what Boeing had to say on the earnings call about free cash flow in the next three years, which made clear CEO Kelly Ortberg still has more work to do in turning around the company and delivering stronger financials. Free cash flow is the primary financial metric on which we judge the stock, given the company is still working its way back to net income profitability. FCF is calculated by subtracting a company's capital expenditures from its operating cash flow. Unfortunately, the near-term performance and the updated long-term outlook paint different pictures. Boeing's FCF in the July-to-September period beat expectations for the second quarter in a row, and the company maintained its $2 billion expectation for 2026. But markets are forward-looking beasts, and Boeing letting investors down on the cash-flow ramp in the coming years is, understandably, causing many investors to dump the stock Tuesday. The company expects to arrive at its target of $10 billion in annual free cash flow a year later than Wall Street modeled. Not ideal. On Tuesday's earnings call, Ortberg detailed the slower-than-expected cadence to reach that target: In 2027, free cash flow is expected to be $3 billion— held back a bit by the increased capex needed to support the next-generation Navy fighter jet contract the company won in September. That's well short of the $5.7 billion consensus, according to estimates compiled by FactSet. In 2028, Boeing projects FCF of $6 billion, when the Street was modeling $9.6 billion. Finally, in 2029, the company expects to hit the $10 billion target. The FactSet consensus had been at $12.9 billion. Some of the positives in Tuesday's report are that Boeing exited the quarter with a record $745 billion backlog, and that Ortberg said the company hasn't seen any changes in customer demand despite the Middle East conflict pushing up jet fuel prices and weighing on aerospace stocks in recent months. If anything, he said Boeing's more fuel-efficient new jets look like an even better purchase in this environment. With all this in mind, we think Tuesday's report represents something of a clearing event for the stock. The guidance is not what we were hoping for. But the upshot is that we did indeed get some quantitative guidance, which is important. Although Wall Street estimates are likely coming down once analysts have had a chance to sharpen their pencils and update their models, investors can take comfort in knowing that the stock is now reflecting a more realistic path in the recovery. On CNBC earlier Tuesday, Ortberg said the uncertainty around Boeing's financial performance is narrowing. Of course, we wish it was narrowing and improving to the upside, not the other way around. Nevertheless, getting three years' worth of targets is not worthless. Ortberg is likely being extra careful and practicing "UPOD" — underpromise, overdeliver —given the company's checkered past. For that reason, while clearing events are painful, we also believe this one to be buyable. The record order backlog is an indicator that once Boeing's production woes are addressed and production is able to ramp, the long-term cash flow targets are indeed achievable, even if not realized as quickly as we would have liked. We're reiterating our buy-equivalent 1 rating. However, we're lowering our price target to $225 to reflect the delayed rebound in free cash flow generation. Quarterly commentary In Commercial Airplanes , Boeing said it's well positioned for the year ahead after the final two variants of its best-selling, narrow-body 737 Max family were certified by the Federal Aviation Administration (the Max 7 in August and Max 10 last week). Boeing said "the 737 program continues to progress toward stabilized production of 47 per month." The language here matters because the key to Boeing delivering more FCF — and in turn stock price upside — in 2027 will be its ability to ramp monthly production beyond 47 and get to 52. We heard in September that it was taking longer than expected to stabilize output at the 47 level, and Ortberg reiterated that again Tuesday. Wings, in particular, are a bottleneck. "Our output of wings is improving, but we need to demonstrate sustained performance at this level and ensure we have a high confidence plan to step up to rate 52 when the system is ready," the CEO said. As a result, the ramp to 52 per month is not expected to occur until the back half of 2027. Because of the delayed ramp, the team also now expects to come up shy of its target to deliver 500 737s in 2026. High jet fuel costs are a headwind for airlines and travelers — even if they've so far been able to eat the higher costs of air travel — but it may be a tailwind for Boeing. As Ortberg explained on CNBC, the high cost of jet fuel makes more fuel efficient offerings, such as the 737 Max 10, that much more attractive as less-efficient aircraft can be retired. With the way that the Middle East conflict has hurt aerospace stocks, Ortberg's commentary here is notable. "So far, the airlines have been, for the most part, flowing the higher fuel into ticket prices," Ortberg added on the earnings call. "I think over the next coming quarters, we'll have to watch that. But again, at a macro level, I feel pretty good about our ability to manage even if we do see some softening demand on the growth market because there's plenty of customers who are looking for airplanes faster for replacement." Outside of the key 737 program, production of the wide-body 787 Dreamliner remains stable at eight per month, with the team expecting to start the ramp to a 10 per month rate before year-end. Boeing still expects FAA certification of its newest wide-body jet, the 777-9, to be received in 2027, with deliveries also expected to begin next year. 777X production is expected to hold at one per month for most of 2027. The program is also expected to be a drag on 2027 FCF before improving in 2028 and flipping positive in 2029. The commercial segment booked 300 net orders in the quarter and exited with a $612 billion backlog, representing over 6,300 airplanes. In Defense, Space & Security , Ortberg called out the company's recent U.S. Navy contract win, in which it was chosen to design, build and deliver the next-gen F/A-XX Strike Fighter. Ortberg said on the call that this will "shape the company for decades to come," and called the company's defense portfolio overall "a little bit of a sleeper." Last year, Boeing also won the contract for a new Air Force fighter jet. The team continues to target a high-single digit operating margin by the end of the decade. The segment booked $23 billion in orders during the quarter, with the backlog exiting the period at a record $101 billion, not inclusive of the F/A-XX contract win. In Global Services , revenue benefited from higher volumes, and the operating margin benefited from both volume and mix. This business consists of maintenance, repairs and upgrades, among other things such as logistics management. While the smallest of Boeing's three segments by revenue, it punches far above its weight in terms of profitability. On the call, CFO Jay Malave said that "both commercial and government businesses delivered double-digit margins in the quarter." The segment received $5 billion in orders and exited the quarter with $33 billion backlog. (Jim Cramer's Charitable Trust is long BA. See here for a full list of the stocks.) articles.text:
Australia’s annual inflation rate stood at 3.9% in Q3 2026, unchanged from the previous quarter and in line with market expectations. However, it remained well above the central bank’s 2–3% target. On a quarterly basis, consumer prices rose 1.3%, accelerating from 0.6% in the previous quarter and matching market forecasts. source: Australian Bureau of Statistics
Quarterly Inflation Rate YoY in Australia remained unchanged at 3.90 percent in the third quarter of 2026 from 3.90 percent in the second quarter of 2026. Quarterly Inflation Rate YoY in Australia averaged 4.91 percent from 1949 until 2026, reaching an all time high of 25.60 percent in the fourth quarter of 1951 and a record low of -0.70 percent in the second quarter of 1962. articles.title: Margin debt growth slows sharply as stock market warning signs build
articles.text:
The pace at which investors are borrowing money to invest in stocks has cooled substantially, raising concern that the stock market may be due for a fall.
Recent FINRA data shows the annual growth in margin debt fell to 31.4% in September from 53.7% in May, Bank of America technical strategist Paul Ciana pointed out in a Friday note. Ciana warned that slowing borrowing momentum from extreme levels has been associated with previous market peaks.
May's growth rate in 2026 was the fourth highest since 1998, according to a BofA analysis. The three higher extremes took place in 2000, 2007 and 2021 — all of which preceded stock market declines.
Earlier this year, borrowing was increasing much faster than stocks were rising. Analysts view high borrowing levels as a contrarian signal, similar to bull-bear sentiment indicators.
At $1.48 trillion, margin debt in September is 1.5% below June's record of $1.5 trillion.
High leverage can have snowball effects in a market downturn. Lower prices trigger demands for additional collateral or forced sales, which accelerate a downturn.
Individual investors can be hit hard. Tesla investor Hy Luu, for example, refinanced his home to raise $30,000 to pay down margin debt during the stock's 2022 decline.
BofA sees other market warning signs, including widening high-yield credit spreads and a rotation toward defensive sectors like healthcare and consumer staples.
Paradoxically, the rotation into those sectors has pushed them to "bubble-risk levels," BofA's equity derivatives team said in a note on Tuesday. Similar shifts occurred in the late 1990s dot-com era and Covid rally, they added. "These dynamics provide further evidence that markets continue to move towards a more bubble-like state."
The bull case is that the midterms could alleviate some of the market's uncertainty and trigger a relief rally, Ciana noted. "Typically, risk assets such as the S&P 500 rebound after midterms unless more severe downside risks materialize."

articles.title: Iran câu giờ, ông Trump như ngồi trên đống lửa
articles.text:
Iran câu giờ, ông Trump như ngồi trên đống lửa
Iran được cho là cố tình kéo dài thế bế tắc ngoại giao với Mỹ nhằm gây bất lợi cho Tổng thống Donald Trump trước cuộc bầu cử giữa nhiệm kỳ.
- 27-10-2026Mỹ - Nga bắt tay, Ukraine phải chấp nhận 'hoà bình bằng mọi giá'?
- 27-10-2026Ông Trump bất ngờ treo thưởng 1 triệu USD cho loại tin báo đặc biệt
- 26-10-2026Reuters: Mỹ có thể trở mặt với Nga ngay sau bầu cử
Iran chủ động kéo dài thế bế tắc ngoại giao?
Theo nhận định của các quan chức Iran và chuyên gia, Iran đang chủ động kéo dài đàm phán với Mỹ nhằm làm suy yếu vị thế chính trị của Tổng thống Donald Trump trước cuộc bầu cử giữa nhiệm kỳ ngày 3/11.
Mỹ muốn chương trình hạt nhân của Iran trở thành nội dung trọng tâm ngay từ đầu các cuộc đàm phán. Mỹ và các nước phương Tây nghi ngờ chương trình này có khía cạnh quân sự, trong khi Iran khẳng định mục đích của mình là hòa bình.
Ngược lại, Iran yêu cầu Mỹ đáp ứng các điều kiện trong đề xuất ngừng xung đột kéo dài 7 ngày trước khi bước vào đàm phán hạt nhân.
Đề xuất được chuyển qua các nhà trung gian Qatar bao gồm chấm dứt giao tranh, nới lỏng hạn chế xuất khẩu dầu, giải phóng tài sản bị phong tỏa và dỡ bỏ các biện pháp phong tỏa hàng hải của Mỹ.
Trong thời gian gần đây, lo ngại về những đợt tấn công mới của Mỹ và Israel, cùng sự thiếu tin tưởng sâu sắc giữa hai bên, khiến Iran không muốn nhanh chóng đạt thỏa thuận chấm dứt chiến tranh.
3 quan chức Iran và một nguồn tin am hiểu vấn đề cho biết, Iran tin rằng ông Trump sẵn sàng nối lại các cuộc tấn công để phá vỡ thế bế tắc kéo dài nhiều tháng qua.
Một quan chức Iran nói rằng nước này đang chuẩn bị đối phó với những đòn tập kích mới, thay vì đặt cược vào khả năng đạt được thỏa thuận với Mỹ.
Nhà phân tích Saeed Leylaz tại Tehran nhận định việc kéo dài đàm phán giúp Iran tác động đến cuộc bầu cử Mỹ mà không cần thực hiện bất kỳ hành động bất hợp pháp nào.
Xung đột kéo dài đã làm gia tăng sức ép chính trị đối với ông Trump, trong bối cảnh giá nhiên liệu cao khiến nhiều cử tri Mỹ bất mãn và có thể ảnh hưởng đến kết quả bầu cử của đảng Cộng hòa.
Ông Donald Trump chịu sức ép lớn trước bầu cử
Cuộc chiến với Iran đang trở thành bất lợi chính trị ngày càng lớn đối với Tổng thống Mỹ Donald Trump, chỉ một tuần trước cuộc bầu cử giữa nhiệm kỳ ngày 3/11.
Theo hãng tin AP ngày 27/10, giá nhiên liệu tăng cao, chi phí sinh hoạt leo thang và sự bất mãn của cử tri trước cuộc xung đột kéo dài đang khiến đảng Cộng hòa gặp khó khăn trong nỗ lực duy trì quyền kiểm soát Quốc hội.
Noor Dubow, một cử tri thường bỏ phiếu cho đảng Cộng hòa tại thành phố Columbus (bang Ohio) cho biết, ông đang nghiêng về phía đảng Dân chủ vì thất vọng trước quyết định phát động chiến tranh của ông Trump.
Là nhân viên điều phối tại một doanh nghiệp vận tải, Dubow nhận thấy giá nhiên liệu tăng đang gây xáo trộn hoạt động kinh tế.
“Các nghị sĩ Cộng hòa ở Quốc hội đang ở đâu? Tại sao họ không yêu cầu ông Trump chịu trách nhiệm?”, Dubow đặt câu hỏi.
Ông Trump từng mô tả cuộc chiến Iran như một “chuyến đi vòng nhỏ”, đồng thời cho rằng chi phí kinh tế mà Mỹ phải gánh chịu không đáng kể so với mục tiêu ngăn Iran sở hữu vũ khí hạt nhân.
Tuy nhiên, cuộc chiến kéo dài gần 8 tháng, trái với dự đoán ban đầu của ông rằng xung đột chỉ diễn ra trong vài tuần.
Tình hình càng phức tạp khi xung đột lan rộng. Lực lượng Houthi được Iran hậu thuẫn đã tiến hành các cuộc tấn công nhằm vào cơ sở dầu mỏ và sân bay của Saudi Arabia, trong khi liên quân do Saudi Arabia dẫn đầu đáp trả bằng các đợt tập kích vào những khu vực do Houthi kiểm soát tại Yemen.
Theo AP, giá xăng trung bình tại Mỹ đã duy trì trên mức 4 USD/gallon kể từ giữa tháng 6. Giá dầu diesel cũng ở gần mức cao kỷ lục, gây sức ép lên hoạt động vận tải, giá hàng hóa và chi phí đi lại.
Những tác động này đang khiến các ứng viên Cộng hòa tại các bang: Iowa, Kansas, Ohio và Texas phải đối mặt với cuộc cạnh tranh gay gắt hơn với đối thủ Dân chủ.
Một cuộc thăm dò của AP-NORC công bố tuần trước cho thấy cử tri thuộc cả hai đảng đều muốn Quốc hội khóa tới tập trung vào việc giảm chi phí sinh hoạt và chấm dứt chiến tranh Iran, mà đây là những trọng tâm mà người dân Mỹ đang chỉ trích đảng Cộng hòa và cá nhân Tổng thống Donald Trump.

articles.title: Amazon's anti-tokenmaxxing memo says engineers should be pickier about using AI
articles.text:
Amazon laid out its AI usage guidelines for software engineers in a memo to staffers, and discouraged employees from turning to "tokenmaxxing" in their push to embrace artificial intelligence tools.
The memo, which was circulated internally in September and posted to the company's website on Tuesday, revises how the company defines the role of software development engineers and managers in the age of AI.
"We're just seeing the beginning of AI's effect on software engineering," the company wrote. "While we have a vision for what the future looks like, there's a lot that's still emerging. We are certain that whatever future best practices are, AI will be at the center of software engineering practice."
Under CEO Andy Jassy, Amazon has rapidly integrated AI across the company's sprawling business operations. Jassy has previously predicted that AI will "change the scope and speed" of day-to-day work, and potentially shrink its corporate workforce in the next few years through automation, though he's noted it will also create "other jobs."
As employees rush to adopt AI tools, companies have grappled with the technology's surging costs and how to reliably measure whether the technology leads to a productivity boost or other valuable returns on investment.
Companies have recently cracked down on tokenmaxxing, in which developers use AI as much as possible with little regard for output. Some companies have set limits on employees' usage of tokens, or the units of data that are processed and generated by AI models, in a bid to slow rising AI bills. Others have switched to cheaper, open-source models for certain tasks.
An Amazon spokesperson said the company hasn't instituted caps on employees' token usage. Amazon in May shut down an internal leaderboard after discovering employees were tokenmaxxing to climb the ranks.
In the memo posted Tuesday, Amazon said metrics like token usage, the rate of adoption of AI tools, and code changes or reviews remain "deeply flawed" ways of measuring teams or organizations' AI usage, adding that they can lead to higher costs and too much complexity.
It stopped short of telling staffers to ignore those metrics altogether, however. Token usage and code generation should be considered "with care and judgment" alongside other data, Amazon said.
"We believe that it is best to measure, and be measured by, long-term outcomes," the company wrote.
Marc Brooker, a vice president and distinguished engineer at Amazon Web Services, told CNBC in an interview that the company has looked to metrics such as "feature velocity" to measure how AI is improving engineer productivity.
The metric looks at things like, "how many launches are we doing, how many successful changes are we making in production," he said.
"Broadly, we think about this as a return on investment," Brooker said. "If there is an important problem to solve for our customers, important problem to solve for our business, we're going to invest tools, time, tokens, human effort, etc. into those."
He added, "What we don't want to see is wasted effort where we are going and spending those tokens solving problems that don't matter and sometimes it's hard to know, so we do need to have some appetite for experimentation."
Amazon also discouraged staffers from using AI when it doesn't make sense for a given task.
"If your work does not benefit from current AI tooling, that is a finding, not a failing," Amazon said in the memo.
The company added, "An engineer who can explain where AI does not yet help their work is demonstrating the judgement we are asking for."

articles.title: 17.000 quân dồn đến điểm nóng, hơn 100 UAV nhắm Voronezh: Ông Zelensky đưa đề nghị đặc biệt tới ông Putin
articles.text:
17.000 quân dồn đến điểm nóng, hơn 100 UAV nhắm Voronezh: Ông Zelensky đưa đề nghị đặc biệt tới ông Putin
Lực lượng 17.000 quân gồm các lữ đoàn đổ bộ đường không số 79, 80 và 95, hai lữ đoàn thủy quân lục chiến số 37 và 40, cùng Trung đoàn số 3 của Lực lượng Tác chiến Đặc biệt.

- 16-10-2026Ukraine cạn tên lửa Patriot, Kiev đối mặt 3 sức ép: Ông Zelensky liên tiếp cầu viện, Nga lên tiếng

Những diễn biến mới nhất cho thấy căng thẳng đang đồng thời xuất hiện ở cả tiền tuyến, khu vực biên giới và bàn cờ ngoại giao.
Cùng lúc đó, Tổng thống Ukraine Volodymyr Zelensky tuyên bố sẵn sàng thảo luận vấn đề trao đổi lãnh thổ, nhưng với 1 điều kiện.
17.000 quân Ukraine dồn tới điểm giáp ba khu vực
Theo Đài TST (Nga), hướng Novopavlovsk, nằm tại khu vực giáp ranh giữa Dnipropetrovsk, Zaporizhzhia và Donetsk, đang trở thành một trong những khu vực được chú ý trên chiến trường.
Truyền thông Nga cho biết Ukraine đã tập trung khoảng 17.000 quân tại một khu vực chỉ rộng khoảng 25 km. Lực lượng này được cho là bao gồm các lữ đoàn đổ bộ đường không số 79, 80 và 95, hai lữ đoàn thủy quân lục chiến số 37 và 40, cùng Trung đoàn số 3 của Lực lượng Tác chiến Đặc biệt. Ngoài ra, một số lữ đoàn hợp thành khác cũng được bố trí ở tuyến sau nhằm củng cố các vị trí đạt được.
Khu vực này nằm gần ranh giới hoạt động giữa hai cụm quân Nga “Vostok” và “Tsentr”, đồng thời nối các hướng Dnipropetrovsk, Zaporizhzhia và Donetsk.
Đại tá Vladimir Antonyuk thuộc Lực lượng Tác chiến Đặc biệt Ukraine, được TST dẫn lời, cho biết vị trí địa lý và chiến thuật là một trong những nguyên nhân khiến bộ chỉ huy Ukraine lựa chọn khu vực này làm hướng phản công.
Theo ông Antonyuk, mục tiêu ban đầu của Ukraine mang yếu tố chính trị, trong đó có việc tiến tới ranh giới tỉnh Dnipropetrovsk. Sau đó, trọng tâm chuyển sang các mục tiêu quân sự - chiến thuật, đặc biệt là những nút giao thông quan trọng tại Velikaya Novosyolka và Bogatyr.
Ông cũng cho biết các mục tiêu này đã được phía Nga tăng cường phòng thủ từ trước.
Theo bài viết, sau nhiều tháng giao tranh, lực lượng Ukraine đạt được một số kết quả cục bộ tại khu vực Shevchenko và quanh Komar, nhưng chưa kiểm soát được Komar.
Truyền thông Nga cho biết một số vị trí trong khu vực vẫn thường xuyên thay đổi quyền kiểm soát, trong khi “vùng xám” tiếp tục biến động.
Hơn 100 UAV nhắm Voronezh, vấn đề vùng đệm được nhắc lại
Đêm 25 rạng sáng 26/10, tỉnh Voronezh của Nga hứng một đợt tấn công UAV quy mô lớn.
Theo Thống đốc Alexander Gusev, hơn 100 UAV đã bị bắn hạ trên toàn tỉnh, trong đó hơn 70 chiếc bị đánh chặn tại khu vực thành phố Voronezh.
Theo thông tin được phía Nga công bố, hai người thiệt mạng và 17 người bị thương, trong đó có một trẻ em. Một số tòa nhà, cơ sở công nghiệp và hạ tầng dân sự cũng bị ảnh hưởng.
Ông Gusev cho biết mảnh vỡ của một UAV rơi xuống một đoàn tàu và khiến một số người bị thương.
Sau vụ việc, câu hỏi về địa điểm phóng UAV được truyền thông Nga đề cập.
Trung tá dự bị Oleg Ivannikov, trong cuộc trao đổi với Aif.ru, cho rằng tỉnh Kharkiv có thể là một trong những khu vực được sử dụng để triển khai UAV do khoảng cách địa lý tương đối gần Voronezh.
Ông Ivannikov cũng nhắc lại nhiệm vụ thiết lập vùng đệm tại khu vực biên giới mà Tổng thống Vladimir Putin trước đó giao cho quân đội Nga.
Theo cách giải thích của phía Nga, vùng đệm nhằm đẩy các vị trí triển khai vũ khí của Ukraine ra xa lãnh thổ Nga và hạn chế khả năng tiến hành các cuộc tấn công từ khoảng cách gần.
Trước đó, Tổng thống Putin nhiều lần đề cập việc tạo một khu vực an toàn dọc biên giới Nga - Ukraine.
Ngoài Voronezh, trong những ngày gần đây, một số khu vực khác của Nga cũng ghi nhận tình trạng gián đoạn điện, nước, Internet và các dịch vụ dân sự sau những vụ UAV.
Tại Yanino, tỉnh Leningrad, một số cư dân cho biết các tòa nhà dân cư từng bị mất điện, nước và hệ thống sưởi sau một vụ tấn công bằng UAV. Người dân địa phương cũng phản ánh Internet hoạt động không ổn định trong thời gian xảy ra sự cố.
Trong một diễn biến khác, nhà quan sát quân sự Dmitry Makhaev đề cập các vụ việc liên quan đến trung tâm dữ liệu Yandex và cho rằng những sự cố đối với hạ tầng số có thể ảnh hưởng trực tiếp tới các dịch vụ thường ngày như taxi, giao đồ ăn, bản đồ và thanh toán.
Nga mở thêm hướng ở Sumy
Cùng thời điểm, phía Nga thông báo về các hoạt động mới tại khu vực Sumy.
Trước đó, có thông tin cho rằng các đơn vị Nga tiến vào Nikolskoye qua khu rừng Sumy nhưng sau đó mất liên lạc trong vài ngày, làm xuất hiện nghi vấn về việc lực lượng này có giữ được vị trí hay không.
Nhà quan sát quân sự Dmitry Degtyaryov sau đó cho biết các binh sĩ Nga đã xác nhận vẫn duy trì hiện diện tại khu vực.
Theo truyền thông Nga, việc kiểm soát Nikolskoye có thể giúp các lực lượng Nga củng cố vị trí tại khu rừng Sumy.
Trước đó, một chỉ huy của cụm quân Nga hoạt động tại khu vực Kursk cũng từng đề cập tầm quan trọng của khu rừng này đối với các hoạt động trong năm 2027.
Các nguồn Nga cho biết khu vực Nikolskoye nằm trên một trong những hướng có thể dẫn sâu hơn vào tỉnh Sumy.
The Wall Street Journal trong một bài viết khác cũng đề cập việc các tuyến đường ống và công trình ngầm cũ đang được sử dụng trong hoạt động quân sự.
Theo tờ báo Mỹ, tại những khu vực mà việc di chuyển trên mặt đất gặp nhiều rủi ro do UAV và pháo binh, các đường ống công nghiệp và hạ tầng ngầm từ thời Liên Xô được sử dụng để phục vụ việc di chuyển lực lượng.
Truyền thông Nga cho biết thêm rằng, phía Ukraine từng tìm cách sử dụng các đường ống khí đốt cũ tại khu vực Kupyansk.
Ông Zelensky nói tới trao đổi lãnh thổ, chỉ muốn bàn trực tiếp với ông Putin
Trong bối cảnh đó, Tổng thống Ukraine Volodymyr Zelensky tuyên bố sẵn sàng thảo luận các phương án mà phía Mỹ gọi là “land swaps” - trao đổi lãnh thổ - trong khuôn khổ một giải pháp hòa bình.
Tuy nhiên, ông Zelensky đặt ra điều kiện rằng vấn đề lãnh thổ phải được thảo luận trực tiếp ở cấp lãnh đạo.
“Người Mỹ từ lâu đã đặt vấn đề trao đổi lãnh thổ, họ gọi đó là land swaps. Có những phương án và đề xuất khác để thảo luận. Nếu là vấn đề lãnh thổ thì phải ở cấp lãnh đạo. Những vấn đề khác có thể giải quyết ở cấp các nhóm kỹ thuật” , ông Zelensky nói với truyền thông Ukraine.
Theo ông, những nội dung như vậy có thể được đưa ra thảo luận trong tháng 11.
Ông Zelensky cho biết Moscow yêu cầu Ukraine rút hoàn toàn lực lượng khỏi Donbass, trong đó có Slavyansk và Kramatorsk.
Tuy nhiên, ông không nói rõ phía Nga sẽ phải chuyển giao khu vực nào nếu hai bên thảo luận một phương án trao đổi lãnh thổ.
Theo TST, một khả năng được nhắc tới là các khu vực thuộc tỉnh Sumy và Kharkiv, nơi Nga hiện duy trì lực lượng và tuyên bố thiết lập vùng đệm.
Trong khi đó, Moscow tuyên bố Kherson, Zaporizhzhia, Donetsk và Lugansk là lãnh thổ Nga, dù hiện chưa kiểm soát hoàn toàn các khu vực này.
Kiev không công nhận việc Nga sáp nhập bốn khu vực trên.
Điện Kremlin cũng nhiều lần đặt câu hỏi về tính hợp pháp trong nhiệm kỳ của ông Zelensky sau khi Ukraine không tổ chức bầu cử tổng thống trong thời gian thiết quân luật.
Moscow cho rằng bất kỳ thỏa thuận nào liên quan tới lãnh thổ cũng phải có giá trị pháp lý và được ký bởi một phía có đủ thẩm quyền.
Hiện chưa có thông tin về việc ông Putin và ông Zelensky sẽ tổ chức một cuộc gặp trực tiếp để thảo luận đề xuất này.
Việt Nam hàng ngày

articles.title: What's behind the AI trade comeback — plus, our take on Intel's latest deal
articles.text: Every weekday, the CNBC Investing Club with Jim Cramer releases the Homestretch — an actionable afternoon update, just in time for the last hour of trading on Wall Street. Stocks are higher again , with the artificial intelligence buildout stocks extending their rebound from last week's sell-off. The tech-heavy Nasdaq is leading the way Tuesday, with an over 1% gain. (The Dow is flat due to an over 9% drop in Boeing stock after the company said it won't significantly ramp up 737 Max production until late next year.) One reason for the AI recovery rally may be that the market is feeling a little better about the AI funding worries that roiled markets last week. What happened this week? Anthropic's IPO filing, Meta Platforms upsizing its common stock offering to $25 billion, and Broadcom securing $63 billion in financing for Anthropic to buy its XPU AI accelerators and networking solutions. The next important catalyst for the AI buildout trade will be hyperscale earnings and their capital expenditure commentary. When Alphabet and Microsoft report after Wednesday's close, followed by Amazon on Thursday, AI bulls will want to hear management discuss the returns they are generating on their AI investments, as well as plans to continue investing in infrastructure to meet growing demand. Intel struck a new quantum deal . Late Monday, the chip giant announced an agreement to purchase Classiq, a leading provider of quantum computing software. The deal brings together Classiq's automated quantum algorithm synthesis platform with Intel's existing quantum software platform, scalable silicon spin-qubit technology, and advanced semiconductor manufacturing expertise. Intel said the combination enables it to become a full-stack quantum solutions provider. (A spin-qubit is a basic unit in a quantum computer). Terms were not provided. But reports say that Intel is paying about $2.3 billion for Classiq. Club stock Intel is up 3.5% in Tuesday's strong market for tech. Buying a quantum computing platform is not how we would prefer Intel to use the proceeds from its $20 billion common stock offering back in August. We want to see money going to expanding Intel's manufacturing capacity to support new foundry customers for its next-generation 14A production process. However, we know CEO Lip Bu Tan to be a disciplined operator who spent a lot of energy repairing Intel's balance sheet. We trust that he would not spend this type of cash on an acquisition if it were too speculative. Intel reports earnings Thursday evening. Announcing an external customer for 14A would go a long way in the market because it would put more value toward the company's foundry business. In the interim, strong demand for central processing units (CPUs) in data centers should be enough to support earnings. There are no Club earnings after the bell . But there are some major companies on the schedule, including Visa, Baker Hughes, Seagate, Robinhood, and NXP Semiconductors. SK Hynix reports overnight, and its earnings and commentary could influence sentiment of fellow memory semiconductor maker Micron . Before Wednesday's open, Club name GE Vernova , as well as GE Healthcare, Boston Scientific, Vertiv, and VF Corp report quarterly results. (Jim Cramer's Charitable Trust is long BA, META, GOOGL, MSFT, MU, GEV. See here for a full list of the stocks.) articles.title: Nữ diễn viên sống trong biệt thự 1.000 m2 về Đồng Tháp xây khu sinh thái rộng gấp 50 lần
articles.text:
Nữ diễn viên sống trong biệt thự 1.000 m2 về Đồng Tháp xây khu sinh thái rộng gấp 50 lần
Sở hữu khối tài sản khủng, nhiều người gọi nữ diễn viên là "đại gia ngầm" của Vbiz.
- 03-10-2026Bắt gặp nữ diễn viên đóng phim 1.100 tỷ làm tài xế xe buýt, diện mạo giờ đố ai nhận ra nổi
- 09-09-2026Nam diễn viên có cơ địa khổ nhất Việt Nam là đây: Lam lũ từ đầu đến chân, fan thấy mà rơi nước mắt
- 04-09-2026Căn nhà 1.000m2 của diễn viên Vân Trang
Vân Trang sinh năm 1990, quê Tiền Giang (nay là Đồng Tháp). Cô theo học Trường Đại học Sân khấu - Điện ảnh TP.HCM và bắt đầu được giao vai khi còn là sinh viên. Không mất quá nhiều thời gian để nữ diễn viên tạo được dấu ấn trên màn ảnh nhỏ nhờ ngoại hình sáng, lối diễn tự nhiên và khả năng đảm nhận nhiều kiểu nhân vật khác nhau.
Những năm đầu sự nghiệp, Vân Trang góp mặt trong loạt phim truyền hình như Đam Mê, Gia Đình Phép Thuật, Cô Gái Xấu Xi, Lối Sống Sai Lầm. Đặc biệt, vai diễn trong Lối Sống Sai Lầm giúp cô được đông đảo khán giả biết đến, đồng thời mang về giải Mai Vàng năm 2010 ở hạng mục Nữ diễn viên phim truyền hình được yêu thích nhất. Từ một gương mặt trẻ, Vân Trang nhanh chóng trở thành cái tên được các nhà làm phim chú ý.
Không dừng lại ở truyền hình, nữ diễn viên tiếp tục thử sức với điện ảnh và ghi dấu qua nhiều tác phẩm như Cô Dâu Đại Chiến, Thiên Mệnh Anh Hùng, Scandal: Bí Mật Thảm Đỏ...
Năm 2016, Vân Trang kết hôn với doanh nhân Quân Lê. Sau đám cưới, cô dần chuyển trọng tâm sang cuộc sống gia đình, đồng thời tiếp tục duy trì những công việc phù hợp với quỹ thời gian của mình.
Tổ ấm của cặp đôi hiện có bốn người con, gồm ba bé gái và một bé trai. Việc chăm sóc các con khiến lịch sinh hoạt của nữ diễn viên thay đổi đáng kể. Cô không còn nhận dự án liên tục như trước mà cân nhắc kỹ hơn trước mỗi lời mời, ưu tiên những công việc có thể sắp xếp song song với việc nuôi dạy con.
Vân Trang từng thừa nhận có những lúc chạnh lòng khi nhìn đồng nghiệp tiếp tục hoạt động sôi nổi, trong khi bản thân phải lùi lại để lo cho gia đình. Tuy nhiên, cô không hối tiếc về lựa chọn của mình. Nữ diễn viên xem những năm tháng dành cho con cái là một phần quan trọng trong cuộc đời, đồng thời vẫn tìm cách duy trì niềm yêu thích nghệ thuật thông qua các dự án phù hợp.
Vân Trang được ông xã yêu thương, chiều chuộng và nhiều lần dành tặng những món quà giá trị. Hiện tại, gia đình nữ diễn viên sinh sống trong căn biệt thự có diện tích khoảng 1.000 m2 tại TP.HCM. Cơ ngơi của vợ chồng Vân Trang gây ấn tượng bởi không gian rộng rãi, được bài trí tỉ mỉ nhưng vẫn giữ được cảm giác ấm cúng, gần gũi.
Bao quanh biệt thự là nhiều mảng xanh được Vân Trang chăm chút kỹ lưỡng. Từ khu vực cổng vào, sân nhà đến khu vườn và ban công đều có sự hiện diện của cây cảnh, hoa lá, tạo nên khung cảnh tươi mát như một khu nghỉ dưỡng thu nhỏ giữa thành phố.
Biệt thự sử dụng gam trắng làm tông màu chủ đạo, tạo vẻ thanh lịch và thoáng đãng. Nội thất được lựa chọn theo hướng tối giản, kết hợp chất liệu gỗ với những gam màu ấm để cân bằng nét sang trọng của tổng thể. Phòng khách là một trong những khu vực nổi bật với diện tích lớn, trần cao và hệ cửa kính rộng hướng ra bên ngoài.
Biệt thự rộng 1.000 m2 của Vân Trang tại TP.HCM
Ngoài ra, Vân Trang còn khiến công chúng trầm trồ khi hé lộ khu sinh thái rộng khoảng 50.000 m2 tại quê nhà. Nơi đây có sức chứa khoảng 1.000 khách. Điểm đặc biệt của nơi này nằm ở phong cách thiết kế đậm chất Nam Bộ. Các căn nhà nghỉ chủ yếu sử dụng gỗ, tre, nứa, kết hợp những món đồ quen thuộc như chén đĩa, tủ gỗ mang dáng dấp xưa cũ. Khu bếp với lò than, những hàng tre xanh trước sân và khoảng vườn thoáng đãng gợi lên khung cảnh làng quê yên bình, tạo cảm giác thân thuộc ngay từ khi đặt chân đến.
Ngay cả cách đặt tên cho từng căn nhà cũng mang màu sắc gia đình. Thay vì những cái tên cầu kỳ, Vân Trang lựa chọn cách gọi gần gũi như nhà dì Ba, nhà cậu Tư, nhà má Năm hay nhà má Sáu. Những tên gọi bình dị này không chỉ tạo nét riêng cho khu sinh thái mà còn gợi nhắc đến nếp sống và tình cảm gia đình miền Tây.
Bên trong mỗi căn nhà nghỉ, các vật dụng thiết yếu như giường, tủ và bàn ghế đều được bố trí để phục vụ nhu cầu lưu trú. Khu sinh thái vẫn giữ lại phần lớn cảnh quan tự nhiên vốn có, chỉ bổ sung các hạng mục cần thiết nhằm tăng sự tiện nghi cho khách. Sự kết hợp giữa không gian xanh rộng mở, kiến trúc mộc mạc và những chi tiết gợi nhớ đời sống miền quê đã tạo nên nét hấp dẫn riêng cho cơ ngơi của Vân Trang.
Khu sinh thái tiếp tục được nữ diễn viên cải tạo, nâng cấp thêm
Thanh Niên Việt

articles.title: Speaker Mike Johnson calls election-transfer concerns ‘absurd’
articles.text:
U.S. House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., committed Tuesday to a peaceful postelection transfer of power, calling concerns that President Donald Trump and congressional Republicans could contest the results if Democrats win control of Congress "absurd."
"We're going to follow the Constitution," Johnson said in Orangeburg, New York during a campaign stop with Republican Rep. Mike Lawler one week before the Nov. 3 midterm election. "The Constitution says when a state certifies the election of members of Congress, then they're administered the oath. That's what I'll be doing on Jan. 3 to everybody who's there," Johnson said in response to a question from MS NOW.
"I may not like some of those outcomes, but that's our system," he said. "And for anybody to suggest otherwise is absurd."
Democrats and voting rights advocates are bracing for potential challenges if control of the House flips, as is widely projected to happen, or control changes in the Senate, which is more closely contested. Republicans have a majority in both chambers of Congress.
Trump, who has continued to falsely claim that widespread fraud cost him the 2020 election, has fueled those fears by calling to "nationalize" elections earlier this year and repeatedly questioning the security of mail voting, while also suggesting noncitizens could vote in large enough numbers to skew results. His administration sued California on Oct. 15 in a fight over noncitizens voting.
The Department of Justice also sued Alaska on Oct. 22 to block the certification of its results in the event of voter confusion. GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan will appear on the ballot beside Daniel J. Sullivan, a retired teacher whom Republicans have said is on the ballot only as a spoiler candidate.
Johnson, who in the wake of the 2020 election was a key congressional ally of Trump's in his quest to overturn results, on Tuesday said questions about a peaceful transfer were "a little silly."
"Of course we'll have a peaceful transfer of power. But it will not be transferring, because we are going to keep the majority and I'm going to be the speaker of the House and I will keep steady hands at the wheel," Johnson told reporters.

articles.title: I just bought this pharma stock for its next generation of blockbuster drugs — and its dividend
articles.text: We just initiated a new position in AbbVie Inc. at around $280 a share for our Enhanced Dividend Income Portfolio. While the dividend is certainly part of the appeal, I'm really into the company's next chapter of growth. The North Chicago-based biopharmaceutical company is best known for Humira, its former blockbuster treatment for autoimmune diseases. But with Humira facing competition from lower-cost alternatives, AbbVie has had to reinvent itself. Judging by the growth of its newer drugs, that transition is paying off. Key points AbbVie's newer immunology drugs are successfully replacing revenue lost from Humira. Neuroscience business is growing rapidly, providing another source of growth. Established aesthetics franchise gives additional diversification. AbbVie's second-quarter revenue increased 10.2% to approximately $17 billion, while adjusted earnings per share jumped nearly 23% to $3.65. The company also reported an adjusted operating margin of 48.3%. That's an impressive combination of double-digit growth and strong profitability, putting AbbVie in a good position to continue growing earnings and supporting its dividend. Why I'm buying The post-Humira transition is working AbbVie faced major challenges when its best-selling prescription drug Humira lost U.S. exclusivity in 2023. But the company has successfully built two major growth engines in its place: Skyrizi and Rinvoq. In the second quarter, Skyrizi sales climbed 24.4% to $5.5 billion, while Rinvoq revenue increased 24.5% to $2.5 billion. Together, these drugs generated more than $8 billion in quarterly revenue, compared with just $756 million from Humira. Both drugs treat chronic inflammatory conditions, including Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis. As more patients adopt these treatments and AbbVie pursues additional approved uses, I see a long runway for growth. The neuroscience business is gaining momentum AbbVie's neuroscience business is growing rapidly, too. Second-quarter revenue increased more than 20% to approximately $3.2 billion. That portfolio includes Vraylar, which treats certain psychiatric conditions, as well as migraine treatments Ubrelvy and Qulipta. AbbVie also has Botox Therapeutic, used for conditions including chronic migraine, and Vyalev, a treatment for certain patients with advanced Parkinson's disease. This gives AbbVie another substantial business as its treatments reach more patients. Aesthetics adds another dimension to the business Investors shouldn't overlook AbbVie's aesthetics business. Through Allergan Aesthetics, the company owns some of the most recognizable brands in cosmetic treatments, including Botox Cosmetic and Juvéderm. ABBV YTD mountain AbbVie, YTD This isn't currently AbbVie's fastest-growing business (second-quarter aesthetics revenue was essentially flat at approximately $1.28 billion, and Juvéderm sales declined 6%). But I see it as another valuable piece of the company, with established brands and exposure to demand for minimally invasive cosmetic procedures. If consumer spending and procedure volumes improve, that could provide an additional boost to growth. Why now? AbbVie shares have rallied this year and are now trading near their 52-week high. At our purchase price of approximately $280, the stock trades at about 20 times management's latest 2026 adjusted earnings guidance. That's not cheap, but it's a reasonable price for a company delivering double-digit revenue growth and strong profitability. We're also getting paid to wait. AbbVie pays a quarterly dividend of $1.73 per share, or $6.92 annually. At our entry price, that's a yield of roughly 2.5%. The company has a long history of raising its dividend, which is exactly what I look for in our enhanced dividend income portfolio. I want companies that can grow their earnings and increase the income they return to shareholders over time. Bottom line There are risks. AbbVie is increasingly dependent on Skyrizi and Rinvoq, and competition, drug pricing pressure and future patent expirations could weigh on growth. But AbbVie has moved beyond the most difficult part of its Humira transition. We're investing in a highly profitable company with renewed earnings momentum and multiple sources of growth. AbbVie is a dividend growth stock entering its second act, and that's why we bought it. Kevin Simpson is the founder and CEO of Capital Wealth Planning. articles.title: Tất cả người dân dùng mạng xã hội chú ý, thông báo mới nhất từ công an
articles.text:
Tất cả người dân dùng mạng xã hội chú ý, thông báo mới nhất từ công an
Công an phát hiện hai tài khoản TikTok "C.X.O.N.C" và "N.N.C" thường xuyên đăng tải, chia sẻ các bài viết, hình ảnh, video có nội dung vi phạm.
- 26-10-2026Ra lệnh bắt tạm giam người đàn ông SN 1991 liên quan đến 510,9 triệu đồng tiền mua điện thoại
Công an tỉnh An Giang ngày 27/10/2026 đã ra cảnh giác trước những thông tin đăng tải trên mạng xã hội có nội dung mê tín dị đoan.
Theo đó, thời gian qua, cùng với sự phát triển mạnh mẽ của các nền tảng mạng xã hội, tình trạng lợi dụng không gian mạng để lan truyền các nội dung mê tín dị đoan có chiều hướng gia tăng, diễn biến ngày càng tinh vi, phức tạp. Nhiều đối tượng đã sử dụng các trang mạng xã hội để đăng tải các bài viết, video có nội dung như "xem bói", "soi căn", "coi âm", "gỡ bùa", "gọi hồn - trừ tà"… để thu hút sự tò mò, đánh vào tâm lý nhẹ dạ, cả tin của một bộ phận người dân.
Ngoài ra, các đối tượng thường xuyên sử dụng cụm từ "An Giang xứ sở thần tiên", "bảy núi An Giang" để gắn vào các bài viết, video có nội dung mê tín dị đoan. Những thông tin này không chỉ làm sai lệch nhận thức, gieo rắc tâm lý hoang mang, lo lắng trong cộng đồng mà còn trực tiếp tác động tiêu cực đến lối sống, nếp nghĩ của giới trẻ, làm suy giảm niềm tin vào các giá trị khoa học, gây ảnh hưởng xấu đến tình hình an ninh, trật tự của tỉnh.
Vừa qua, Phòng An ninh nội địa Công an tỉnh An Giang phát hiện hai tài khoản TikTok "C.X.O.N.C" và "N.N.C" thường xuyên đăng tải, chia sẻ các bài viết, hình ảnh, video có nội dung tuyên truyền, cổ súy hành vi mê tín dị đoan nhằm thu hút người xem và trục lợi. Qua xác minh, Phòng An ninh nội địa xác định anh Đ.M.C, sinh năm 1988 và anh N.T.N, sinh năm 1996, cùng trú tại ấp An Hòa, xã Núi Cấm, tỉnh An Giang, là chủ hai tài khoản TikTok trên.
Đơn vị đã mời hai người đến cơ quan Công an để làm việc, giáo dục, nhắc nhở. Tại buổi làm việc, anh Đ.M.C và anh N.T.N đã nhận thức được hành vi vi phạm của mình, tự nguyện gỡ bỏ toàn bộ nội dung vi phạm đã đăng tải, chia sẻ trên TikTok và cam kết không tái phạm.
Công an tỉnh An Giang khuyến cáo người dân nâng cao ý thức trách nhiệm khi sử dụng mạng xã hội; không đăng tải, bình luận, chia sẻ các nội dung tuyên truyền mê tín dị đoan, phản khoa học, cổ súy hủ tục lạc hậu dưới mọi hình thức.
Khi phát hiện tài khoản, hội nhóm hoặc nội dung có dấu hiệu tuyên truyền mê tín dị đoan, thông tin sai sự thật, người dân cần kịp thời báo cho cơ quan Công an để xác minh, xử lý theo quy định của pháp luật. Sự chủ động phối hợp của người dân góp phần ngăn chặn các hành vi vi phạm trên không gian mạng, xây dựng môi trường mạng lành mạnh, an toàn và bảo đảm an ninh, trật tự.
Thời gian tới, Công an tỉnh tiếp tục đẩy mạnh công tác đấu tranh, ngăn chặn hành vi lợi dụng không gian mạng để tuyên truyền mê tín dị đoan, cổ súy hủ tục lạc hậu. Phòng An ninh nội địa sẽ tăng cường nắm tình hình trên không gian mạng, chủ động phát hiện, kịp thời xử lý các trường hợp vi phạm theo quy định của pháp luật.
