articles.title: To make yourself 'unforgettable' in an AI-driven world, do these 5 counterintuitive things, says leadership expert
articles.text:
It used to be that to stand out at work, we needed to be fast, polished, and agreeable. In the age of artificial intelligence, all of that gets turned on its head. Now, anyone can produce anything quickly with the appearance of poise and tact.
For nearly two decades, I've coached CEOs and senior executives on how to communicate, collaborate, and stand out as leaders. But over the past few years, I started noticing something troubling: the very qualities that once made people successful at work were becoming easier to automate. If everyone has access to the same intelligence, what will actually make someone unforgettable?
For my forthcoming book, "Use Your Brain," I interviewed CEOs, scientists, artists, parents, and students across five continents. As someone who was becoming increasingly uncomfortable with my own AI use, I sought to understand what separates people who use AI to sharpen and improve their thinking from those who surrender to it and lose their point of view.
What I found was that the people who retained their autonomy and kept their work memorable had developed these counterintuitive habits.
1. They slow down at the start
I've found the best critical thinkers don't rush. When using any AI tool, they employ what psychologist Sumona De Graaf calls a "Think Sandwich" — Think, AI, Think. To build your own "Think Sandwich," take five minutes to answer three key questions before you prompt.
- What do I believe about this?
- What problem am I actually solving?
- What would a bad outcome look like?
The first one forces you to develop your own point of view before AI gives you one. The second one keeps you from getting a brilliant answer to the wrong question. And the third one makes you consider the risks and consequences that a polished AI response might overlook.
Without them, you risk solving the wrong problem, accepting assumptions you never questioned or mistaking a convincing answer for a good one.
After you answer these questions, then consider using AI to review your research or first draft. You can also invite it to attack your argument or poke holes in what you wrote. But I would also get a gut check from another human being who knows the context that you are working in.
2. They are less polished
I had a coaching client, a newly promoted senior vice president at a large company, who had started letting an AI assistant draft his email replies.
A few months later, he received his annual review from his direct reports. He told me that one colleague wrote that it had become hard to tell where he stood on anything. Another said that he sounded "polished," but didn't frame it as a compliment.
It used to be that polish signaled credibility. Now with the proliferation of AI tools, that polish can seem cheap or empty. But being less polished doesn't mean leaving bad grammar and typos in your work. It can look like:
- Starting an email or text message with a detail only you could know.
- Putting your stance on a subject in the first sentence, rather than clearing your throat with small talk.
- Naming one thing you're unsure about.
This week, before you send your next important e-mail, ask yourself: "Could anyone else have written this?" If the answer is yes, look for ways to be more specific. Authenticity will resonate more than perfection.
3. They go looking for disagreement
When everyone has access to tools that validate their thinking, we risk creating workplaces where assumptions go unchallenged and bad ideas sound brilliant. That makes healthy disagreement at work more important, not less.
The people who stand out will be the ones who are willing to challenge the thinking in the room, including their own.
Here's how to go looking for disagreement in a constructive and helpful way:
- Ask questions instead of delivering verdicts.
- Start with what you agree with and follow that to where you're stuck.
- Assign a designated skeptic in meetings to normalize pushing back.
- Critique your own work first. When you share a draft with colleagues, say, "Tell me the weakest part."
These habits make disagreement feel less like a personal attack and more like a shared effort to get to a better answer. Questions lower defensiveness, finding common ground builds trust, and inviting criticism makes it safer for others to speak up.
4. They protect their independent judgment
When I ask executives who they believe are the most at risk of handing their thinking to AI, they usually point to Gen Z or junior employees. The irony is that I see the opposite in my coaching work. This is because executives' roles have shifted from doing the work to reviewing it. Now AI makes that review process even easier, serving up polished summaries, recommendations and decisions in seconds.
The danger is that leaders who spend all their time just approving answers then struggle to identify biases in their team's work. This leads to A-level work on the surface, with C-level understanding of the issue at hand.
The higher you rise, the more consequential that loss of independent judgment becomes. To intentionally protect their thought processes, I recommend that leaders:
- Do one meaningful piece of work from scratch every week.
- Explain the core logic of anything AI-assisted out loud, without a screen or written notes from anyone else, before presenting it.
- Ask themselves the question they'd normally ask their team: "Walk me through how you got there. What assumptions is it based on? What alternatives were rejected? What evidence would change your mind? What are you missing?" If you can't answer those questions without looking at the AI-generated summary, you may be approving a conclusion you don't fully understand.
- Have team members give 90-second presentations where they explain, defend and recall their point of view.
5. They choose to have the live conversation
If your message contains emotion, conflict, disagreement or requires a hard decision, pick up the phone or organize an in-person meeting to have a real-time conversation. Don't just show up to deliver your message. Start by asking a question you genuinely don't know the answer to and listen without planning your response or rushing to a bot.
Pay attention to what's not being said, whether that is hesitation, a change in tone, or a concern someone seems reluctant to raise. Before concluding the meeting, make sure the other person feels heard by echoing what matters most to them.
I've found that the conversations people remember aren't necessarily the ones where you said something brilliant. They're the ones where you made someone feel understood, challenged their thinking with care or had the courage to say what needed to be said.
AI can help you craft the perfect message, but it can't replace the trust that you personally build in the moment.
Erica Dhawan is a leadership expert, keynote speaker, and Wall Street Journal bestselling author of "Digital Body Language" and "Get Big Things Done." Her new book, "Use Your Brain: Think Deeper in a World on Autopilot," is out Jan. 12, 2027.

articles.title: One week out, prediction markets see Democrats as favored to sweep Congress
articles.text:
The 2026 U.S. midterm election will be held a week from Tuesday, with the Republican Party looking to defend majorities in both the House and Senate, though Democrats are seen as two-to-one favorites to flip both chambers blue on prediction markets.
Speculators on platform Kalshi place a 63% chance that Democrats win control of both the House and Senate. Those odds have stayed relatively stable since the beginning of October. Meanwhile, there's just under a 10% chance that Republicans sweep both chambers, and a 29% chance Democrats win the House while the GOP maintains its majority in the Senate.
Contracts on the market are resolved using official data from the U.S. Congress.
Odds and gambling platforms do not use methodologies used by traditional political polling, and therefore are not substitutes for political polls.
On Sunday, prediction markets gave high odds to right-wing candidate Flavio Bolsonaro to win in the Brazil presidential election before polls closed, though the incumbent left-wing president Lula da Silva was re-elected. Some markets in Democratic primaries this election cycle also drew criticism for giving sky-high odds to some candidates winning who ultimately only narrowly won or lost.
Platforms, however, say that odds traders place often end up happening that exact percentage of the time. That means, essentially, that a candidate with a 20% chance to win on an event contract exchange pulls out an "upset" win 20% of the time.
Before early September, Democrats had less than a 50% chance to sweep both chambers of Congress, though their odds have risen from around 30% earlier in the year before the start of the U.S.-Iran war and higher gas prices that have hit consumers.
On Polymarket, Democrats have a 65% chance to sweep both houses.
Polls broadly show Democrats favored in the national popular vote for the House, and competitive in a series of red-state Senate races that will decide control of the upper chamber. Though House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., has cast doubt on those findings.
"We've been from coast to coast," he said in an appearance on Fox News Monday, "and I'm telling you, the polling is inaccurate."
Disclosure: CNBC and Kalshi have a commercial relationship that includes customer acquisition and a minority investment.

articles.title: Hà Nội đề xuất chi hơn 22.200 tỷ đồng tái thiết khu vực hồ Hoàn Kiếm và phụ cận
articles.text:
Hà Nội đề xuất chi hơn 22.200 tỷ đồng tái thiết khu vực hồ Hoàn Kiếm và phụ cận
Hà Nội đề xuất đầu tư 22.229 tỷ đồng cải tạo, chỉnh trang, tái thiết khu vực hồ Hoàn Kiếm và vùng phụ cận, trong đó dành gần 10.000 tỷ đồng để giải phóng mặt bằng.
- 28-10-2026Đề xuất tăng tiền đặt cọc lên tới 50% để đấu giá đất có hạn chế bỏ cọc?
- 27-10-2026Miền Bắc sắp có không khí lạnh
- 27-10-2026Siêu sân vận động lớn nhất hành tinh, rộng gấp 3,3 lần Mỹ Đình do Vingroup xây dựng: 16.000 người góp sức
UBND TP Hà Nội vừa trình HĐND thành phố xem xét, quyết định chủ trương đầu tư và phê duyệt nhà đầu tư thực hiện dự án cải tạo, chỉnh trang, tái thiết không gian khu vực hồ Hoàn Kiếm và vùng phụ cận theo phương thức đối tác công tư (PPP), loại hợp đồng xây dựng - chuyển giao (BT).
Theo tờ trình, khu vực nghiên cứu quy hoạch có diện tích khoảng 66,82ha, thuộc địa bàn hai phường Hoàn Kiếm và Cửa Nam.
Dự án nhằm hình thành không gian quảng trường quy mô lớn, kết nối hồ Hoàn Kiếm với Quảng trường Cách mạng Tháng Tám, Nhà hát Lớn, Bảo tàng Lịch sử Quốc gia và các khu vực lân cận.
Bên cạnh đó, dự án sẽ mở rộng không gian công cộng, tổ chức lại hệ thống giao thông và không gian ngầm, đồng thời bảo tồn, phát huy các giá trị di sản văn hóa, lịch sử của khu vực.
Theo nội dung tờ trình, dự án dự kiến có 3 dự án thành phần, tổng vốn hơn 22.200 tỷ đồng
Dự án thành phần 1: Giải phóng mặt bằng toàn bộ khu vực thực hiện dự án, có quy mô sử dụng đất đề xuất khoảng 30,82ha, không bao gồm các ô đất B1.6 và B4.13-HH1 thực hiện theo dự án riêng.
Dự án có sơ bộ tổng mức đầu tư 9.924 tỷ đồng, thực hiện theo hình thức đầu tư công, sử dụng ngân sách thành phố. UBND phường Hoàn Kiếm là chủ đầu tư.
Dự án thành phần 2: Xây dựng trung tâm thương mại ngầm tại khu vực công viên, quảng trường phía đông hồ Hoàn Kiếm (lô B2.5) và khu vực công viên, quảng trường phía bắc hồ Hoàn Kiếm (lô B1.3).
Công trình dự kiến có 4 tầng hầm, tổng diện tích sàn khoảng 82.608m², với sơ bộ tổng mức đầu tư 4.611 tỷ đồng.
Dự án thành phần 3: Đầu tư xây dựng công trình, cải tạo, chỉnh trang cảnh quan hồ Hoàn Kiếm và khu vực phụ cận theo phương thức đối tác công tư (PPP), loại hợp đồng xây dựng - chuyển giao (BT).
Dự án có sơ bộ tổng mức đầu tư 7.694 tỷ đồng, trong đó khoảng 3.518 tỷ đồng dành cho xây mới khu vực trụ sở UBND TP Hà Nội; 268 tỷ đồng cải tạo, chỉnh trang trụ sở HĐND thành phố và 3.908 tỷ đồng cải tạo, chỉnh trang khu vực phía đông nam hồ Hoàn Kiếm.
Dự án thành phần 2 và 3 được đề xuất do nhà đầu tư là Công ty cổ phần Bất động sản Mặt Trời Thủ đô thực hiện.
Để thanh toán cho nhà đầu tư, Hà Nội dự kiến sử dụng 6 quỹ đất “vàng” rộng khoảng 7,31 ha với giá trị sơ bộ 4.878 tỷ đồng. Các khu đất dự kiến đối ứng nằm tại phố Tràng Tiền, hai bên Bưu điện, Tăng Bạt Hổ, Lê Thánh Tông, Hai Bà Trưng và khu vực Đông Anh. Toàn bộ các hạng mục của dự án được đặt mục tiêu hoàn thành vào năm 2029.

articles.title: Cramer says something is missing in Tuesday's market rally and he's not eager to jump in
articles.text: Every weekday, the CNBC Investing Club with Jim Cramer holds a "Morning Meeting" livestream at 10:20 a.m. ET. Here's a recap of Tuesday's key moments. 1. The S & P 500 is higher Tuesday, driven by optimism around chipmakers such as Broadcom , which worked with major banks on a $63 billion deal to finance AI chip purchases for Anthropic. Though the market is holding up, Jim Cramer cautioned against getting too excited given the market's continued sensitivity to fluctuations in bond yields and oil prices. He likened those two variables to the weather, with higher crude and bond yields being like a rainy day, and tame moves representing a sunnier day that encourages buying. "We don't want to be in a market that's controlled by the weather," Jim said. "We want to be in a market that's controlled by conviction. And I don't see a lot of conviction today." While oil being lower might encourage some people to scout for buy opportunities, Jim instead preached patience. "What I want people to understand is we're not going to play that game. We are going to wait until it's actually many reasons to buy. " 2. Meta's secondary stock offering to fund its AI buildout was upsized to $25 billion from $22.5 billion, in a good sign of demand for its equity. However, Jim said that Meta's plans to sell $60 billion worth of stock at market prices beginning next year will remain an overhang on shares. Jim said the problem with these "at the money" offerings is that companies outsource the execution to brokers who usually execute them in ham-fisted manners, without always caring about how the stock is performing in a given day. With that new supply consistently coming into the market, Jim said stocks tend to trade "heavy," limiting the upside. He alluded to the fact that Alphabet's stock hasn't done well since the company announced a big stock sale, which included an at-the-market component, in early June. 3. Boeing's shares tumbled nearly 10% after delivering third-quarter earnings before the bell. The planemaker posted a revenue beat and exceeded free cash flow estimates, but revealed a bigger loss per share than expected. The stock's sell-off intensified as Boeing's earnings call got underway and management reset investor expectations for cash flow growth in the coming years. While Boeing's call didn't begin until after Tuesday's Morning Meeting ended, Jim correctly predicted that Wall Street estimates will need to come down. "There are people, unfortunately, who have a very high number for next year. They're going to have to cut their number," Jim said. The upshot, Jim said, is that this likely represents a "clearing event today" and the weakness will represent a buying opportunity once the dust settles. Keep an eye on your inboxes later Tuesday for a full analysis on the quarter. 4. Stocks covered in Tuesday's rapid fire at the end of the video were: Coca-Cola, UPS , and Corning . (Jim Cramer's Charitable Trust is long AVGO, META, and BA. See here for a full list of the stocks.) articles.title: Lula’s election win leaves Brazil facing a fiscal tightrope
articles.text:
Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's surprise re-election as Brazil's president on Sunday prompted a sharp market reaction — and showed the tightrope he must walk between pleasing his grassroots base and nervous investors who could fuel a fiscal crisis.
The country's benchmark stock index tumbled 13.9% on Monday, the sharpest daily decline since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic, and the Brazilian real fell nearly 8% against the U.S. dollar, the most since 1999.
The yield on Brazil's 10-year government bond rose 2.46 percentage points to its highest level in more than a decade.
The moves wiped out a rally in Brazilian assets that followed Flávio Bolsonaro, seen as the more market-friendly and fiscally disciplined of the candidates, winning the first-round vote in early October.
Lula, who has been in office since Jan. 1, 2023 and was president before from 2003 to 2011, now faces a host of challenges, including a heavily right-wing Congress opposed to many of his policies and hostility from the White House.
Slow growth, high inflation and rates
Economic issues will be top of the pile.
Growth is slowing in Latin America's biggest economy, and inflation and interest rates are high.
Lula has promised expensive measures that appeal to his grassroots base. Those include protections of existing benefits, minimum-wage increases ahead of inflation, expansions of housing and education support programs, tax cuts on food essentials and a reduction in the country's long working week to 40 hours without pay cuts.
His ability to deliver will "revolve around a central tension," Rafael Ch, senior analyst for Latin America and emerging markets at Signum Global Advisors, said in a note Tuesday.
Voters want "tangible improvements in household finances," and the election result will be seen as an endorsement of higher social spending, Ch said.
But bond markets are already uneasy with Brazil's growing debt-to-GDP ratio, and are likely to demand an ever-higher premium if public spending rises significantly. The Brazilian Treasury on Monday canceled two planned bond auctions scheduled for this week amid concerns over demand and soaring yields.
"Insufficiently funded fiscal expansion could leave the central bank cutting [interest rates] less, offsetting part of the relief Lula hopes to deliver," Ch said.
"We believe Lula will manage this tension through sequencing: reassure markets initially, capture the benefits of monetary easing, and subsequently seek greater fiscal flexibility to deliver his legacy agenda," he added.
Reassurance will come through signals that he is preparing measures to increase the 2027 primary surplus, including a possible constitutional amendment expanding spending freezes, and appointing a market-conscious finance minister, Ch added.
A key question will be whether markets view any fiscal discipline as temporary and whether Lula embarks on a spending spree ahead of the 2030 elections if support for the left falls, Ch said. "Even a limited easing cycle could weaken his commitment to restraint once some of its economic benefits have materialized," he said.
Lula is facing a potential fiscal crisis "largely of his own making," Elizabeth Johnson, managing director of Brazil research at TS Lombard, said on Tuesday.
Johnson also said that market-calming measures should be expected, including the curbing of civil-service benefits, reducing subsidized credit and the presentation of a proposal for a new "sin tax" — on goods such as alcohol and cigarettes — in the coming days.
Meanwhile, the president will rush to approve reforms before the new legislature convenes in February, Johnson said, which "hinges on Lula's willingness to cut spending."
"Our base case is that Lula will advance a modest fiscal reform, helping avert a major fiscal crisis in 2027," Johnson said.
In the short term, Brazilian stocks would nonetheless suffer, according to Russ Mould, investment director at AJ Bell.
"Who will foot the bill for Lula's proposed welfare spending and debt moratorium for small enterprises remains to be seen, but the 10-year bond yield is likely to rise first and ask questions later, a development that can only serve to make Brazilian equities relatively less attractive," Mould said in a Tuesday note.
Brazil's Ibovespa had been the best-performing major stock market index this year, he said, buoyed by Bolsonaro's expected victory and the country benefiting from higher commodity prices.
The latest decline "in turn may not help wider pan-Latin American indices, which investors can easily access via exchange-traded funds (ETFs). The MSCI Latin America index hit a 12-year high this year, helped by the political rightward swing, which Brazil had been expected to join," Mould said.

articles.title: Tình hình hiện tại ở Bảo tàng Đạo Mẫu của NS Xuân Hinh
articles.text:
Tình hình hiện tại ở Bảo tàng Đạo Mẫu của NS Xuân Hinh
Tình hình được NS Xuân Hinh trực tiếp cập nhật.
Mới đây, trên trang Facebook cá nhân, NSƯT Xuân Hinh đăng tải thông báo về định hướng phát triển Bảo tàng Đạo Mẫu, công trình văn hóa được ông dành nhiều năm tâm huyết xây dựng tại ngoại thành Hà Nội. Cụ thể, nam nghệ sĩ mong muốn phát triển bảo tàng theo hướng đương đại, sử dụng chất liệu văn hóa truyền thống nhưng thể hiện thông qua trải nghiệm, công nghệ và các sản phẩm sáng tạo để thu hút giới trẻ cùng du khách trong nước, quốc tế.
Thông tin nhanh chóng thu hút sự quan tâm, bởi Bảo tàng Đạo Mẫu vốn được biết đến là công trình kiến trúc đặc biệt, xây dựng từ hàng triệu viên ngói cổ và từng được giới kiến trúc quốc tế vinh danh.
Bảo tàng đã hoàn thành phần kiến trúc từ năm 2023, hiện ra sao?
Bảo tàng Đạo Mẫu tọa lạc tại khu vực Hiền Ninh, Sóc Sơn, Hà Nội. Theo hồ sơ đăng trên tạp chí kiến trúc quốc tế ArchDaily, dự án do kiến trúc sư Nguyễn Hà cùng ARB Architects thiết kế, có diện tích công bố 5.500 m² và hoàn thành phần kiến trúc vào năm 2023.
Dù vậy, công trình chưa được đưa vào khai thác như một điểm tham quan công cộng thường xuyên. Nghệ sĩ Xuân Hinh cho biết nhiều du khách trong nước và quốc tế đã ngỏ ý muốn tới tham quan. Tuy nhiên, ông chưa mở cửa rộng rãi vì công tác chuẩn bị, tổ chức đón tiếp chưa thực sự chu toàn.
Nam nghệ sĩ tiết lộ một số đoàn khách nước ngoài đến từ Hungary, Đức, Nhật Bản từng ghé thăm. Song, bảo tàng còn thiếu nhân sự giỏi ngoại ngữ để giới thiệu đầy đủ về kiến trúc, hiện vật và giá trị văn hóa của công trình.
Trong chia sẻ mới nhất, Xuân Hinh cho biết đang tìm kiếm và làm việc với những đội ngũ phù hợp để hiện thực hóa các dự định mới. Quá trình này cần thêm thời gian nghiên cứu, sáng tạo và sản xuất. Ông cũng nhấn mạnh hiện chưa thể công bố thêm thông tin. Như vậy, đến thời điểm hiện tại, lịch mở cửa rộng rãi cũng như các hoạt động trải nghiệm cụ thể tại bảo tàng vẫn chưa được xác nhận.
Công trình 5.500 m² được xây từ 5 triệu viên ngói cổ, giữ nguyên vườn cây 50 năm tuổi
Điểm khiến Bảo tàng Đạo Mẫu thu hút sự quan tâm không chỉ nằm ở quy mô mà còn ở cách kết hợp vật liệu truyền thống với tư duy kiến trúc hiện đại.
Nghệ sĩ Xuân Hinh từng dành khoảng 5 năm sưu tầm 5 triệu viên ngói cổ cùng hơn 1 triệu viên gạch thất từ khoảng 500 hộ dân để xây dựng công trình. Nhiều viên ngói vốn thuộc về những ngôi nhà cũ bị tháo dỡ trong quá trình đô thị hóa. Thay vì sử dụng ngói theo cách truyền thống, kiến trúc sư Nguyễn Hà đã biến chúng thành những bức tường, khối tháp và các lớp không gian mang hình thức đương đại.
Đặc biệt, bảo tàng được xây dựng giữa khu vườn cây ăn quả có tuổi đời khoảng 50 năm. Theo hồ sơ thiết kế của ARB Architects, nhóm kiến trúc sư lựa chọn giữ lại các cây xanh, ngôi nhà cũ, hàng rào và trụ cổng hiện hữu. Những khối công trình mới được bố trí theo vị trí cây để hạn chế tác động đến cảnh quan.
Một chi tiết thú vị khác nằm ở lối đi dẫn vào bảo tàng. Ban đầu Xuân Hinh muốn có con đường rộng rãi dẫn đến nhà gỗ trưng bày hiện vật. Tuy nhiên, kiến trúc sư Nguyễn Hà lại lựa chọn lối đi nhỏ, đi qua những bức tường ngói và các khối tháp nhằm tạo cảm giác tĩnh lặng, giúp người tham quan dần tách khỏi nhịp sống bên ngoài.
Công trình còn tận dụng ánh sáng, không khí tự nhiên và các lớp tường ngói dày để hỗ trợ cách nhiệt. Kiến trúc sư Nguyễn Hà từng cho biết thiết kế bảo tàng không sử dụng điều hòa, thay vào đó chú trọng tổ chức không gian và thông gió tự nhiên.
Bên trong, Xuân Hinh dành nhiều khu vực để thờ Mẫu, lưu giữ tranh, hoành phi, câu đối, trang phục, hiện vật dân gian cùng các tư liệu liên quan đến hát văn, hầu đồng và nghệ thuật truyền thống.
Tháng 12/2023, Bảo tàng Đạo Mẫu được tạp chí kiến trúc Domus của Italy đưa vào danh sách những công trình kiến trúc nổi bật trong năm. Đến tháng 4/2026, công trình tiếp tục xuất hiện trong số 1111 của tạp chí này, với bài giới thiệu do chính kiến trúc sư Nguyễn Hà thực hiện.
Hiện tại, nghệ sĩ Xuân Hinh vẫn chưa tiết lộ công nghệ sẽ được ứng dụng, đơn vị hợp tác hay thời gian triển khai các hoạt động mới đưa du khách tới bảo tàng để tham quan.
Song có thể thấy, từ hàng triệu viên ngói cổ được góp nhặt qua nhiều năm đến một công trình được giới kiến trúc quốc tế chú ý, Bảo tàng Đạo Mẫu đã trở thành dấu ấn đặc biệt trong hành trình gìn giữ văn hóa truyền thống của Xuân Hinh. Với những chia sẻ mới nhất, công chúng tiếp tục chờ đợi thời điểm bảo tàng chính thức mở cửa rộng rãi, cũng như cách nam nghệ sĩ hiện thực hóa mong muốn đưa di sản đến gần hơn với thế hệ trẻ.
Phụ nữ mới

articles.title: Giá trị của kiểm toán đo bằng sự thay đổi tích cực của quản trị quốc gia
articles.text:
Giá trị của kiểm toán đo bằng sự thay đổi tích cực của quản trị quốc gia
Đây là thông điệp được Chủ tịch Quốc hội Trần Thanh Mẫn nhấn mạnh tại buổi tiếp trưởng đoàn 16 cơ quan kiểm toán tối cao (SAI) tham dự Hội thảo quốc tế “Cơ quan kiểm toán tối cao trong bối cảnh mới: Tầm nhìn, Thể chế và Đổi mới”, do Kiểm toán nhà nước (KTNN) Việt Nam tổ chức, chiều 27/10, tại Nhà Quốc hội.
Mở rộng trao đổi kinh nghiệm, thúc đẩy hợp tác kiểm toán
Báo cáo với Chủ tịch Quốc hội về kết quả Hội thảo diễn ra trong sáng 27/10, Tổng Kiểm toán nhà nước Nguyễn Hữu Nghĩa cho biết, sự kiện có sự tham dự của 16 đoàn đến từ 16 SAI trong khu vực và trên thế giới, cùng khoảng 250 đại biểu. Hội thảo ghi nhận 13 tham luận, tập trung vào ba nội dung trọng tâm: thể chế, tầm nhìn và đổi mới hoạt động kiểm toán.
Các ý kiến trao đổi tại Hội thảo cung cấp nhiều kinh nghiệm thực tiễn, là nguồn tham khảo phục vụ KTNN Việt Nam xây dựng Chiến lược phát triển đến năm 2035, tầm nhìn đến năm 2045, đồng thời nghiên cứu, đề xuất sửa đổi Luật Kiểm toán nhà nước phù hợp với yêu cầu thực tiễn và thông lệ quốc tế.
Thay mặt các trưởng đoàn đại biểu quốc tế, Tổng Kiểm toán và Kiểm soát Ấn Độ Shri K. Sanjay Murthy, Chủ tịch Tổ chức các Cơ quan Kiểm toán tối cao châu Á (ASOSAI), cảm ơn sự đón tiếp trọng thị của lãnh đạo Quốc hội Việt Nam; đồng thời khẳng định quan hệ hữu nghị giữa Ấn Độ và Việt Nam được xây dựng trên nền tảng tin tưởng, tôn trọng lẫn nhau và cam kết chung về phát triển.
Theo Chủ tịch ASOSAI, các SAI giữ vai trò quan trọng trong nâng cao chất lượng quản trị quốc gia, thúc đẩy minh bạch, trách nhiệm giải trình và bảo đảm ngân sách được sử dụng có trách nhiệm, hiệu quả. Hoạt động kiểm toán không chỉ dừng ở việc xem xét tính tuân thủ trong chi tiêu ngân sách mà còn cần đánh giá mức độ đạt được mục tiêu của các chương trình của chính phủ và tác động đối với đời sống người dân.
Ông Shri K. Sanjay Murthy nhấn mạnh, giá trị của kiểm toán không chỉ thể hiện trong các báo cáo mà còn ở những kiến nghị giúp cơ quan, tổ chức khắc phục hạn chế, nâng cao hiệu quả thực thi. Trước những thách thức từ chuyển đổi số, biến đổi khí hậu và yêu cầu ngày càng cao của công chúng, các SAI cần đổi mới phương pháp, tăng cường ứng dụng trí tuệ nhân tạo, phân tích dữ liệu và nâng cao năng lực chuyên môn, từng bước chuyển từ phát hiện sai phạm đã xảy ra sang nhận diện, cảnh báo rủi ro sớm.
Chủ tịch ASOSAI lưu ý, kỹ năng số có thể hỗ trợ hoạt động đánh giá chuyên môn nhưng không thể thay thế sự phán đoán của con người. Mục tiêu cuối cùng của quản trị vẫn là phục vụ lợi ích công cộng, góp phần củng cố niềm tin của người dân đối với các thể chế công.
Khẳng định không một SAI nào có thể tự chuẩn bị đầy đủ cho tương lai, ông Shri K. Sanjay Murthy cho rằng các cơ chế hợp tác như Tổ chức quốc tế các Cơ quan Kiểm toán tối cao (INTOSAI) và ASOSAI tạo điều kiện để các cơ quan chia sẻ tri thức, trao đổi thông lệ tốt và nâng cao năng lực. Ông đánh giá Hội thảo do KTNN Việt Nam tổ chức có ý nghĩa thiết thực, góp phần tăng cường hợp tác giữa các SAI, cùng củng cố thể chế và chuẩn bị tốt hơn trước những thách thức trong tương lai.
Năm định hướng cốt lõi đối với các cơ quan kiểm toán tối cao
Phát biểu tại buổi tiếp, Chủ tịch Quốc hội Trần Thanh Mẫn nhiệt liệt chào mừng trưởng đoàn các SAI đến Hà Nội, đồng thời đánh giá cao những đóng góp của các đại biểu tại Hội thảo. Chủ tịch Quốc hội nhận định, trước những thay đổi nhanh chóng của môi trường quản trị quốc gia, các SAI cần tiếp tục đổi mới để nâng cao hiệu quả hoạt động và đáp ứng yêu cầu phát triển trong giai đoạn mới.
Theo Chủ tịch Quốc hội, ba trụ cột "Tầm nhìn – Thể chế – Đổi mới" thể hiện cách tiếp cận toàn diện: tầm nhìn xác định hướng đi, thể chế tạo nền tảng, còn đổi mới quyết định năng lực thích ứng. Đối với Việt Nam, xây dựng nền quản trị quốc gia hiện đại, minh bạch và có trách nhiệm giải trình là yêu cầu quan trọng. KTNN cần góp phần giữ vững kỷ luật, kỷ cương; phòng, chống tham nhũng, lãng phí, tiêu cực; phát hiện những bất cập trong cơ chế, chính sách và thúc đẩy sử dụng hiệu quả nguồn lực công.
Trên tinh thần đó, Chủ tịch Quốc hội nhấn mạnh năm vấn đề có ý nghĩa định hướng đối với hoạt động của các SAI.
Thứ nhất, quản trị tốt là nguồn lực, niềm tin của Nhân dân là tài sản chiến lược. Với tính độc lập, khách quan và phương pháp làm việc dựa trên bằng chứng, các SAI cần trở thành chỗ dựa tin cậy trong củng cố kỷ luật, kỷ cương tài chính, nâng cao trách nhiệm giải trình và bảo vệ niềm tin của công chúng.
Thứ hai, thể chế phải vững chắc, bảo đảm tính độc lập thực chất gắn với trách nhiệm. Chủ tịch Quốc hội cho rằng không có một khuôn mẫu thể chế duy nhất phù hợp với mọi quốc gia. Điều cốt yếu là cơ quan kiểm toán phải được bảo đảm đầy đủ thẩm quyền và điều kiện cần thiết để thực hiện nhiệm vụ khách quan, chuyên nghiệp, liêm chính. Độc lập không phải mục tiêu tự thân mà là điều kiện tiên quyết để kiểm toán tôn trọng sự thật và bảo vệ lợi ích công.
Thứ ba, giá trị của kiểm toán được đo bằng sự thay đổi tích cực của quản trị, không chỉ bằng số tiền kiến nghị xử lý. Theo Chủ tịch Quốc hội, hoạt động kiểm toán cần chủ động hơn trong phòng ngừa vi phạm, nhận diện sớm bất cập về thể chế, kiến nghị hoàn thiện cơ chế, tháo gỡ điểm nghẽn và khơi thông nguồn lực. "Phát hiện sai phạm là cần thiết, nhưng phòng ngừa từ sớm, từ xa mới tạo ra giá trị bền vững cho quốc gia" – Chủ tịch Quốc hội nhấn mạnh.
Thứ tư, chủ động đổi mới trong kỷ nguyên số, đồng thời đề cao trách nhiệm của con người. Chuyển đổi số và ứng dụng trí tuệ nhân tạo cần đi đôi với đổi mới tư duy, hoàn thiện hành lang pháp lý về dữ liệu và bảo đảm an toàn thông tin. Công nghệ giúp nâng cao tốc độ và chiều sâu phân tích, nhưng năng lực chuyên môn, đạo đức nghề nghiệp và sự thẩm định của con người vẫn giữ vai trò quyết định.
Thứ năm, hợp tác quốc tế cần thực chất, bình đẳng và cùng kiến tạo giá trị. Chủ tịch Quốc hội đề nghị tiếp tục phát huy hiệu quả các cơ chế hợp tác của INTOSAI, ASOSAI và Tổ chức các cơ quan kiểm toán tối cao Đông Nam Á (ASEANSAI); tăng cường kiểm toán hợp tác, chia sẻ phương pháp luận và đào tạo nguồn nhân lực chất lượng cao.
Nhấn mạnh sứ mệnh chung của các SAI là bảo vệ lợi ích công, nâng cao hiệu quả sử dụng nguồn lực quốc gia, củng cố trách nhiệm giải trình và phục vụ Nhân dân, Chủ tịch Quốc hội cho rằng kiểm toán không chỉ đánh giá những gì đã diễn ra mà còn phải góp phần cải thiện quản trị hiện tại và kiến tạo tương lai. Giá trị cốt lõi của hoạt động kiểm toán cần được thể hiện qua sự hoàn thiện của thể chế, tính nghiêm minh của kỷ cương bộ máy, hiệu quả sử dụng nguồn lực và niềm tin của Nhân dân.
Chủ tịch Quốc hội khẳng định KTNN Việt Nam đã từng bước trưởng thành, tiếp cận các chuẩn mực quốc tế và hội nhập ngày càng sâu rộng thông qua hợp tác, trao đổi kinh nghiệm với các đối tác quốc tế. Việc địa vị pháp lý của KTNN được hiến định trong Hiến pháp năm 2013 là dấu mốc quan trọng, khẳng định vị thế của cơ quan trong hệ thống quản trị quốc gia.
Chủ tịch Quốc hội đề nghị KTNN Việt Nam tiếp tục phát triển theo hướng chuyên nghiệp, liêm chính, hiện đại; chủ động tiếp thu có chọn lọc kinh nghiệm quốc tế, đồng thời tổng kết thực tiễn để chia sẻ với các đối tác. Chủ tịch Quốc hội bày tỏ tin tưởng các tổ chức và cơ quan kiểm toán tối cao sẽ tiếp tục đồng hành, tăng cường hợp tác với KTNN Việt Nam trong chặng đường phát triển mới./.
Báo Kiềm toán

articles.title: Oracle integrates ChatGPT, Codex into apps and expands cloud chip lineup
articles.text:
Oracle on Tuesday announced an expanded collaboration with OpenAI that brings the artificial intelligence lab's ChatGPT and Codex into the software maker's applications to make databases more actionable.
Mahesh Thiagarajan, Oracle's president of Cloud Infrastructure, told CNBC at Oracle AI World in Las Vegas that using ChatGPT "allows anybody to build an application, deploy it, manage it."
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman is set to join Oracle co-CEO Clay Magouyrk on stage for an Oracle AI World keynote on Tuesday at 12:40 p.m. ET.
For OpenAI, the announcement represents another example of the frontier lab's push into the enterprise market, just one day after its key competitor, Anthropic, filed its S-1 as it heads toward an initial public offering.
Oracle's database plays a crucial role in underpinning businesses across healthcare and finance in logging and securing data.
Thiagarajan said his team observed OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra model get trained at Oracle's Stargate data center campus in Abilene, Texas, and could see the real-time benefits.
"More businesses are choosing OpenAI as we make it easier to put AI to work through the tools and systems they already use," said Greg Brockman, president and co-founder of OpenAI, in the press release.
Oracle also said Tuesday that it is making different hardware accessible on its cloud infrastructure, including Google's tensor processing unit AI chips and OpenAI's Jalapeño chip.
"Now customers can actually have infinite possibilities in terms of how they can drive AI," Thiagarajan said.
It is the first time Google's custom chips will run on another hyperscaler's cloud, and illustrates how the companies are increasingly looking for opportunities to get their hardware in the hands of the frontier labs.
Thiagarajan added that the scarcity of chips remains an ongoing issue and that customers such as OpenAI can benefit from having different accelerators to choose from. When asked whether this marks a pivot away from Nvidia GPUs, Thiagarajan said no, adding that Nvidia chips are "the best, most fungible," and that the AI market remains incredibly large.
OpenAI's Jalapeño chip and Cerebras will also run on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. The Cerebras deal is material, but the AI chipmaker won't be disclosing the scale because it's in a quiet period, a Cerebras spokesperson said.
Cerebras stock climbed about 8% following the news. Oracle shares were up nearly 5% on Tuesday.
The announcement comes seven months after market-leading cloud Amazon Web Services announced plans to bring Cerebras hardware into its data centers, a major point of validation.
Thiagarajan also addressed Oracle's multibillion New Mexico data center dubbed Project Jupiter and the ongoing pushback it's receiving from the local community. He said Jupiter represents just one of the 30-40 different data center projects in development, per quarter, for the company.
"We're actually not too worried about what we're doing because I think we're building global infrastructure," he said.
A hearing to address air quality permitting is scheduled for Dec. 7 in Sunland Park, where the controversial data center has already broken ground. The political pushback tied to the project prompted Oracle to deliver a force majeure notice to its backer Blue Owl Capital last month. Right now, Oracle maintains that the project is on schedule.
Investors are now counting down to Oracle's investor day, where investors will want to see if the company can back its fiscal year 2030 revenue targets and if the margin profile of its cloud deals has changed due to the rising cost of capital.
Bank of America analysts wrote to clients that updates on Oracle's major data center projects are among the topics they expect clarity on at the meeting.
Oracle shares are down more than 30% this year due in part to concerns about how the company plans to finance its ambitious digital infrastructure pipeline.
— CNBC's Jordan Novet contributed to this article

articles.title: Vũ Thuý Quỳnh sinh con đầu lòng
articles.text:
Vũ Thuý Quỳnh sinh con đầu lòng
Từ chia sẻ trên trang cá nhân của Vũ Thuý Quỳnh, nhiều người gửi lời chúc mừng.
Từ khi công khai thông tin mang thai con đầu lòng, Vũ Thúy Quỳnh vẫn đều đặn xuất hiện tại một số sự kiện, đồng thời chia sẻ những khoảnh khắc đời thường trên mạng xã hội. Trong hành trình này, người đẹp nhận được nhiều sự quan tâm từ khán giả, đặc biệt là những cập nhật liên quan đến cuộc sống gia đình và em bé sắp chào đời.
Mới đây, Vũ Thúy Quỳnh đăng tải một đoạn clip quay cận mặt với diện mạo xinh xắn, thần sắc tươi tắn. Tuy nhiên, điều khiến cư dân mạng bàn luận không chỉ là nhan sắc của người đẹp mà còn nằm ở một số chi tiết xuất hiện trong khung cảnh phía sau. Cụ thể, netizen soi ra trần nhà và miếng lót chén trong đoạn clip có nét tương đồng với không gian trong một buổi tiệc chúc mừng mẹ tròn con vuông ở bệnh viện quốc tế tại TP.HCM. Đây là hình thức tổ chức thường được các gia đình lựa chọn sau khi em bé chào đời để người thân, bạn bè cùng đến chung vui.
Vũ Thuý Quỳnh xuất hiện trong không gian như tiệc riêng tư để chúc mừng "mẹ tròn con vuông" tại một bệnh viện quốc tế ở TP.HCM
Bên cạnh đó, một số story gần đây của Vũ Thúy Quỳnh cũng được cư dân mạng nhận xét có bối cảnh tương tự trung tâm chăm sóc sau sinh mà cô từng được cho là sẽ lựa chọn để ở cữ. Trong tầm 10 ngày qua, Vũ Thuý Quỳnh cũng chỉ đăng clip cũ chứ không cập nhật hoạt động mới. Tổng hợp những chi tiết này, không ít khán giả gửi lời chúc mừng đến Vũ Thúy Quỳnh và Đức Phạm.
Vũ Thúy Quỳnh là gương mặt quen thuộc với khán giả yêu thích các cuộc thi sắc đẹp. Người đẹp từng lọt top 10 Siêu Mẫu Việt Nam 2018, top 10 Hoa hậu Hoàn vũ Việt Nam 2022, sau đó giành danh hiệu Á quân 3 tại The New Mentor 2023. Tại Hoa hậu Hoàn vũ Việt Nam 2023, cô lọt top 5 chung cuộc. Đến Miss Universe Vietnam 2024, người đẹp gốc Điện Biên tiếp tục ghi dấu ấn khi đăng quang Á hậu 2. Đức Phạm được biết đến là một doanh nhân có điều kiện kinh tế và từng vướng ồn ào liên quan đến cuộc hôn nhân với một cựu người mẫu nổi tiếng. Mối quan hệ giữa anh và Vũ Thúy Quỳnh nhận được nhiều sự chú ý khi cả hai công khai hẹn hò vào cuối năm 2025.
Hồi cuối tháng 8/2026, Đức Phạm gây chú ý khi trở lại mạng xã hội sau khoảng 7 tháng vắng bóng. Trong bài đăng, Đức Phạm bày tỏ mong muốn thay đổi để trở thành chỗ dựa vững chắc cho những người thân yêu. Nam doanh nhân viết: "Con biết điều bố lo lắng con sẽ ra sao nếu bên cạnh con không có ai nữa. Con biết đến lúc con phải thay đổi vì trách nhiệm của con là phải trở thành điểm tựa để bảo vệ con của con như cách bố bảo vệ con. Cảm ơn bố mẹ đã chỉ cho con cách bảo vệ gia đình của mình. Con yêu đừng sợ, đã có bố đây rồi".
Thanh Niên Việt

articles.title: CNBC 2026 Workforce Executive Summit takeaways: How AI is transforming jobs, hiring, and employee benefits
articles.text:
This was CNBC's live coverage of the seventh annual CNBC Workforce Executive Council Summit.
CNBC Workforce Executive Council members speak with CNBC's Sharon Epperson at the 2026 CNBC Workforce Executive Council Summit in New York City on October 27, 2026.
CNBC
Today's workplace faces a litany of challenges. Whether it's shifting power dynamics between employers and employees, the accelerating impact of artificial intelligence on how we work and the skills we need, or the financial stresses that employees of all ranks are feeling, these issues and more are challenging the cohesion of workplace communities.
To address these issues, CNBC convened its premiere council of human resource executives in New York City on October 27, 2026 for the annual CNBC Workforce Executive Summit. The event is exclusive to members of CNBC's Workforce Executive Council.
The things Dan Harris says people should do when panicking
Dan Harris, author, podcaster and former ABC News anchor, spoke with CNBC's Susan Caminiti at the 2026 CNBC Workforce Executive Councill Summit in New York on October 27, 2026.
CNBC
Dan Harris once had a panic attack on national television while on Good Morning America.
As a result, the former ABC News anchor discovered meditation and became an advocate for others to do the same.
Closing out the 2026 CNBC Workforce Executive Council Summit, Harris told CNBC's Susan Caminiti there are several things that people should do when they are feeling anxious or sense that their inner critic is getting louder.
Switching from being a critic to being a coach. Harris said while a coach still pushes you, a good coach "knows your limits and knows how to talk to you like a real human being, something that most of us don't give ourselves."
Take care of your nervous system. Figure out what you need to stay regulated and do it with regularity, Harris said. If that means taking a walk or exercising, do it consistently. "Pick one thing in the bucket of self-care and understand it's not selfish; it's a public service because when you take care of yourself in the right way, you become easier to live with," he said.
When you're freaking out, never worry alone. Harris said his view of self-love is "intensely and inextricably entangled with love writ large ... learning how to love yourself helps you love other people, and loving other people is a form of self-love because we need it."
Harris also offered two relationship hacks, which he said are critical to all of these efforts:
Reinforce the power of micro-interactions. Harris said that research points to the positivity of little passing interactions throughout the day, whether it's with colleagues, someone on an elevator or at a store. "These little moments are massively additive to overall well-being. You're leaving money on the table when you overlook them," he said.
Reflective listening. The power of making people feel seen and heard around you is massive, Harris said, and he said he practices reflective listening to ensure that. To do so, Harris said you need to listen intently to what someone is saying, and when they are done "state back to them briefly and in your own words the core of their message ... it is the most effective benevolent manipulation tactic you will ever learn."
— Ian Thomas
2 Hours Ago
Silencing your inner critic and celebrating your inner coach
watch now
VIDEO3:5503:55
Dan Harris on how to shift from being an inner critic to an inner coach
This era of optimization and hyper-productivity may be doing more harm than good, both at work and in our personal lives.
So how do you learn to be a little kinder to yourself while still being kickass effective?
Dan Harris, author, podcaster and former ABC News anchor, said the challenges that the social media landscape, amplified by the loneliness epidemic and other factors, make listening to that inner critic very easy.
However, he said, that can be done by rewiring what he called "your talk track."
"Learning how to rewire your inner talk track is just something you can do as you move through life. Next time you notice yourself kicking your own ass, just pause and say what you would say to a good friend," he said.
For added emphasis, place your hand on your heart or giving yourself a hug, and use your own name when you speak to yourself, he said.
"You don't have to be stuck with the inner dialog that you are now stuck with. You can consciously rewire it," he said.
— Ian Thomas
3 Hours Ago
The difference between a good and great leader in the AI era
watch now
VIDEO3:3503:35
What sets leaders apart when AI drives the workplace
As AI technology evolves, people who thrive in ambiguity and are willing to experiment are becoming increasingly attractive to companies across all industries.
That includes at the senior leadership level. Two CNBC Workforce Executive Council members — Care.com CHRO Wes Burke and The Team Managing Director Amy Segal — told CNBC's Sharon Epperson about how their organizations have shifted their views on executive hiring in the age of AI.
Burke said more emphasis is being put on what he called the "ability to problem solve very quickly and collaborate within that," something that his company learned from the way it had been hiring engineers.
"That now shows up in a hiring process where we give the same sort of prompts and we say, 'Look, there's no right or wrong answer. We're just curious how you're going to approach this and what you think about it,'" he said. "We do that assessment process with other employees who join them there. So it goes from the traditional, 'Tell me about a time,' to 'Help me solve this problem and let's talk about it together.'"
In Segal's role, she is often tasked with helping find leaders for rising sports leagues or organizations that are aiming to create new revenue lines.
"People have really talked about adaptability, but I think understanding how to challenge the status quo is super important. It used to be that everyone just looked for the experiences that someone had, and that that was really enough," she said. "While a perspective on the way things have been done before is helpful, really understanding how to use those experiences to disrupt is what's differentiating good from great."
— Ian Thomas
3 Hours Ago
What WEC members think about the rapidly evolving workplace
CNBC Workforce Executive Council members attend the group's 2026 Summit in New York City on October 27, 2026.
We asked CNBC Workforce Executive Council members for their take on the rapidly changing workplace. Some of their answers are as follows:
What are you doing to help employees adapt to change while keeping them engaged and supported?
"I think it's just level-setting with employees so they understand that they are the most important asset. While the tools are there and the technology is available, really centering our people and reminding them that they matter and that this helps us all overall. It really has helped to not only boost morale but drive more innovation and creativity with employees to start to lean into the tools a little bit more, recognizing that the tool is nothing without the human intelligence aspect of it. So it's just education, lowering the barriers a little bit and creating a safe space for people to feel comfortable trying and getting things wrong."
-Sandy Choute, J.P. Morgan
How is AI changing the way you think about skills, hiring, and career development?
"I think it's changing a lot. First of all, we're looking at hiring in a little bit of a different way. I think we're trying to hire folks that have more curiosity and adaptability, because we know that they're going to need to do a lot more learning as the tools and the technology change at this at this rapid pace ... I think we're also looking at ways that we can put more power in the hands of our employees by deploying some of these AI tools and giving them that freedom and permission to experiment, because the folks that are going to be able to solve some of these challenges are the ones that are closest to the action."
-Mason Argiropoulos, Paychex
How is AI changing the way you think about your skills, hiring, or career development at your organization?
"We're thinking about the future. What does the future recruit look like? We're thinking about how do we need to attract our talent, how do we need to develop and train our talent, and ultimately, what do we need to engage and retain them? So we are considering all those factors right now as we go through this stage of technology."
Theresa Richardson, Withum
3 Hours Ago
Can New York City lead the way on responsible AI regulation?
watch now
VIDEO3:2803:28
New York City Council speaker on how cities can help regulate AI
New York City Council speaker Julie Menin is hoping New York City can provide a blueprint for other localities when it comes to regulating AI.
"The best would be for the federal government to regulate," Menin told CNBC's Leslie Picker. "So you have one uniform regulation, and you don't have different regulations based on varying jurisdictions, but let's be clear: there has been really no federal regulation of AI emanating from the federal government, and even at the state level," she added.
Menin said that New York City has introduced 10 different bills. One of them, she said, would set up third-party validation free of conflict of interest.
"The conflict of interest part is very important because you can't have an independent third-party test that is basically captive to the company, that is basically truly not independent," she said.
Another bill, Menin said, would pay whistleblowers a significant amount of penalties. "If you have a swarm of 5,000 or 6,000 or 7,000 AI agents, it's $25,000 per AI agent. So these penalties will indeed add up, and our bill gives the whistleblower a significant portion of those penalties."
"The regulations that we are looking, the laws that we're looking to pass here in New York, can be a national paradigm, really, for what responsible, sensible AI regulation looks like," Menin said.
-Colleen McKown
3 Hours Ago
The challenges different aged workers face in the AI era
watch now
VIDEO4:5004:50
How workers of all ages can succeed in the AI age
The introduction of AI into the workplace has introduced workplace challenges for workers for all ages.
For young workers, are there still opportunities to learn from company veterans or long-held processes?
For older workers, are they able to reskill with these new tools?
Three CNBC Workforce Executive Council members — Care.com CHRO Wes Burke, Cotiviti Chief People Officer Kerri Eskin, and The Team Managing Director Amy Segal — spoke with CNBC's Sharon Epperson about how their organizations are ensuring workers are succeeding with AI, regardless of age or experience.
— Ian Thomas
4 Hours Ago
Why a 'human-in-the-loop' AI strategy should be replaced by 'human-in-the-lead'
Jill Bruning, Amentum Chief Technology Officer, speaks with CNBC's Susan Caminiti at the 2026 CNBC Workforce Executive Council Summit in New York City on October 27, 2026.
CNBC
Amid the rise of AI, a prevailing strategy has been to keep a human in the loop, or essentially allowing human judgment, review, or intervention over any AI action.
But Jill Bruning, chief technology officer of Amentum and a member of the CNBC Technology Executive Council, said at the CNBC Workforce Executive Summit that strategy should be evolved to be humans in the lead.
"There's an AI curve, and we see it. It's going up and it's going fast and has a lot of attributes to it; it's quicker than anything we've seen before," Bruning told CNBC's Susan Caminiti. "So when you think about people on that curve … that gap is getting bigger every day."
Bruning said she doesn't know if leadership is adapting fast enough to the technology, and that is creating additional challenges with upskilling as well as what tasks are being delegated to AI.
"So your delegation skills are different, and then how do we tell the agents what to do? How do we define that role? She said. "That's human over the loop, not in the loop. We're still in charge."
— Ian Thomas
4 Hours Ago
Walmart says AI training is boosting confidence with the technology among its 2.1 million associates
Maren Waggoner, Walmart senior vice president and chief people officer for associate experience and digital, speaks with CNBC's Leslie Picker at the 2026 CNBC Workforce Executive Council Summit in New York City on October 27. 2026.
CNBC
As enterprise AI investment continues to grow, companies of all sizes are trying to figure out how employees feel about the technology in the workplace.
Walmart, the biggest private employer in the world, asked its 2.1 million associates in June that exact question for the first time, trying to get a sense of how one of the most diverse workforces is experiencing AI.
What it found, based on more than 1.7 million survey responses, is that while workers have different levels of familiarity and comfort with AI, training and experience with the technology matters.
Seventy-seven percent of Walmart's office-based associates said are excited about AI's potential to improve their work, Walmart Chief People Officer for Associate Experience and Digital Maren Waggoner told CNBC's Leslie Picker at the 2026 CNBC Workforce Executive Council Summit in New York City.
And as for Walmart's U.S. frontline associates, 84% said they are confident using digital tools, a reflection of the AI-powered tools that many of them are now using in their roles, she said.
"We've given them certificates, we've given them training programs and tools, and so they're using it in their day-to-day," Waggoner said.
In the last 13 months, Walmart has partnered with both Google and OpenAI around learning and AI certification programs for associates at no cost. Waggoner said that associates who went through OpenAI training said they had a 27% confidence gain using AI.
That has helped Walmart buck some of the larger trends around AI across the country. While about 52% of U.S. adults say they are more concerned than excited about AI, according to an August 2026 Pew Research Center poll, Walmart associates report greater comfort and excitement, Walmart data showed.
"Providing the tools, providing the training; they feel more confident," Waggoner said.
— Ian Thomas
4 Hours Ago
The actual cost of rising GLP-1 costs
watch now
VIDEO5:0905:09
How companies are dealing with rising GLP-1 costs
Skyrocketing demand for GLP-1 drugs are driving up healthcare costs for companies.
James Lucania, HealthEquity CFO, told CNBC's Annika Kim Constantino, "we've seen employers do different things, whether that's restricting coverage, dropping it altogether, expanding it."
Lucania said that around 40% of companies are covering GLP-1s for weight loss, and that almost all companies cover it for diabetes indications.
"Those of you who are still paying for it, I mean, it's a wonderful blessing for your teammates to be able to have this. But we can see it getting out of control," he said.
"We had a meeting with the CEO of one of our large clients who told us their GLP bill is $350 million dollars on a $3.5 billion total claim base. So it is a huge percentage of it, and obviously that's growing way faster than than even their 10% medical claims inflation."
When asked what companies can do, Lucania said they can take baby steps, like creating an HRA product where they cover it in a different manner outside of the plan.
Or, he said, "You can you can just rip the band-aid, do it inside the HSA, and make up the difference with the contributions. So we're seeing a lot of that, more and more changing each year."
"I do think the right way, the right way forward is that it should be a cash pay sort of structure, and when people have skin in the game, they will take more control over their health outcomes," he said.
-Colleen McKown
4 Hours Ago
How Walmart is leveraging AI across its stores
watch now
VIDEO4:5504:55
How AI is changing the retail experience at Walmart
While AI is perhaps the biggest technological revolution that Walmart has gone through over its 64-year history, Waggoner said the company's approach to transformation has remained the same.
"We have a pretty bold mission statement around being a people-led, tech-powered omni-channel retailer that is ultimately dedicated to helping save money," she said. "The people-led and tech-powered piece has been around for a while."
Many workers across the economy say they are afraid of AI replacing their jobs. While Waggoner said Walmart is finding ways to use AI to automate processes in fulfillment centers, for example, the retailer's efforts with the technology are to "reduce some of that friction and use robotics to help, and then really focus the work on human judgement."
In fact, Waggoner said, at the company's innovation lab in Dallas, Texas, automated efforts to reduce the physical tasks previously performed by humans have instead created more quality assurance-type roles as opposed to broader job losses.
And on the front lines of stores, Waggoner said Walmart has found that its customers "actually like talking to a human at checkout."
That has allowed associates to focus their efforts on using AI to solve customer challenges.
Waggoner pointed to a store manager in Mexico that she met earlier this year who built his own AI agent to look at reports and drive fresh produce sales.
"He's using the tool, but he's still running the store," she said. "The store manager job is still there. He's using the tools and technology to drive his business. And by the way, his fresh sales are through the roof."
— Ian Thomas
4 Hours Ago
The future of wellness spending versus sick care in benefit plans
HealthEquity CFO James Lucania speaks with CNBC's Annika Kim Constantino at the 2026 CNBC Workforce Executive Council Summit in New York City on October 27, 2026.
CNBC
Healthcare costs are soaring, placing a heavy burden on both U.S. companies and individual employees.
James Lucania, HealthEquity CFO, told CNBC's Annika Kim Constantino that he sees the healthcare market moving towards wellness.
"I'm wearing an Oura ring. I see seeing a bunch of Whoop straps today. Lots of Apple watches."
"[People] are taking control of their health more and more each year," he said. "So I view this market as a wellness spending market. People are going to spend for their wellness out of their own pocket, or their HSA, or their FSA in a tax advantaged manner."
Lucania thinks insurance will evolve to be more about sick care, "like your health coverage is for when you end up in the hospital or you end up in the urgent care," he said.
"Wellness, which I would put with GLP-1s, medical weight loss, and skin health and sleep studies and all these diagnostics and the functional health ... many of these are going to be cash pay markets, and I think that's the right solution, and it will help manage the cost structure in your benefit plans."
-Colleen McKown
4 Hours Ago
How to evaluate new hires in an AI era
Steve Cadigan, Human Advantage Framework Creator and Author, speaks at the 2026 CNBC Workforce Executive Council Summit in New York City on October 27, 2026.
As the scope and scale of jobs shift as AI rolls out across the workforce, companies need to change how they hire, former LinkedIn chief human resources officer Steve Cadigan said at the CNBC Workforce Executive Council Summit.
"I think we all agree there's promise [with AI] … but how do we realize that requires a complete change in how we think about our relationship to work on every level in the organization," Cadigan told CNBC's Leslie Picker. "Instead of your job being to do, your job is to rethink how you do what do you."
Cadigan said that view, which is "so orthogonal to how we think about every employee's relationship to work," is what scares a lot of people.
"It's not just deliver now; it's change what you do," he said.
That's why, he said, the hires of the next five years will not be about "what they know, but more based on what they can learn, because jobs are changing that quick."
Cadigan said the companies he's working with now are assessing the ability of new hires to learn new things, and are trying to find out if these people are early adopters, have taught themselves something new, or perhaps pushed themselves in different ways, like living in a different country or learning a different language.
"Do I have a high belief in your ability to adapt? I think that's what we're going to start to look for," he said.
— Ian Thomas
5 Hours Ago
The benefit workers want the most? "Paid on time," says DailyPay's Chai
DailyPay CEO Nelson Chai speaks with CNBC's Sharon Epperson at the 2026 CNBC Workforce Executive Council Summit in New York City on October 27, 2026.
CNBC
The majority of Americans are living paycheck-to-paycheck. DailyPay CEO Nelson Chai told CNBC's Sharon Epperson that in light of this, their top priorities are not benefits like "the gym membership or pet insurance or some of those things that are things they can add on to."
"They mostly want to get paid on time. They need to figure out how to get to work. They need to figure out how to put food on the table," he said. "So those are the things we're really focused in on."
The way companies provide health insurance, too, Chai said, is already beginning to evolve. "Healthcare is continuing to migrate to a menu where [companies] give them healthcare dollars and you pick out how you're going to allocate your dollars," he said.
Over time, he said, "it'll be more efficient for employers to not offer things that don't really add value, and it'll be way more impactful for the folks who need access to their paychecks."
-Colleen McKown
6 Hours Ago
Steve Cadigan: Mistake companies are making is "using the old tech playbook"
watch now
VIDEO4:5104:51
Steve Cadigan: The real value of AI is in finding ways to create more
As AI integrates itself into workplaces, Steve Cadigan, Human Advantage Framework creator and author, told CNBC's Leslie Picker that companies are struggling to realize the promise of the technology.
"I think the mistake a lot of us are making is we're using the old tech playbook, which is to use technology to go faster, do more, and save money," he said. "Do I think AI can deliver, go faster, do more, save money? 100% it can. But I think where the real value is is in finding ways to create more."
Cadigan pointed out that leadership is more burnt out than ever.
"It's an all-time low. I mean, it's blinking red, flat line, code red, and we have a growing level of distrust," he added.
He pointed to another decades-old technology — email — that we haven't completely figured out how to leverage for productivity yet either, which should caution executives as to the quick impact that AI could have.
"Half of you right now are sitting here going, 'Man, how many emails are we going to have to deal with?' We've weaponized it to get more behind, and so we're walking a million miles an hour towards this AI nirvana, and we haven't even solved email productivity yet."
What tech should do, Cadigan said, is "deliver a more beautiful world experience. Isn't that what we want technology for? More beauty, more joy, more time. And now we're seeing more anxiety, more depression, more suicide, more people freaking out."
"The creation, the ability for us to create new technology, and that dissonance, I think, is a big, big problem," he added.
-Colleen McKown
7 Hours Ago
DailyPay's Nelson Chai: On-demand pay can help workers with financial strain
watch now
VIDEO2:5802:58
How companies can help employees stay financially afloat: DailyPay's Nelson Chai
Americans are increasingly finding themselves strapped for cash amid the rising costs of groceries, gas and everyday expenses.
That is leading more companies to begin to offer earned wage access as a benefit, which allows employees to access money they've already earned ahead of payday
Nelson Chai, the CEO of on-demand pay platform DailyPay, told CNBC's Sharon Epperson about how the company's model works.
"We have over 2,000 of the largest companies, including many that you've heard of, and we really go in and partner with them," he said.
"If you had to wait 14 days to get paid, tomorrow you could go in and you could have access to your wages," he said.
Employees are able to access their wages in a few different ways, he said. One option is to use the Daily Pay debit card, another is to do an ACH transfer, and another is to do a transfer to the bank of the employee's choice.
"After you've taken out what you want to take out, then we send you the remainder of pay at the time of the normal paycheck," he said.
"It's about meeting the workers where they are," he added.
-Colleen McKown
7 Hours Ago
Digital transformation is “two of the worst words ever used in the history of work” – former LinkedIn CHRO Steve Cadigan
Steve Cadigan, Human Advantage Framework Creator and Author, speaks with CNBC's Leslie Picker at the 2026 CNBC Workforce Executive Council Summit in New York City on October 27, 2026.
CNBC
When Steve Cadigan was LinkedIn's chief human resources officer, he told CNBC's Leslie Picker at the 2026 CNBC Workforce Executive Council Summit that a common trope at the networking platform was that whenever another company announced it was going through a digital transformation, that meant job cuts were on the horizon.
"Let's look at all the people in the company that just announced a digital transformation and see who's looking for a new job," Cadigan told Picker. "When you tell employees we're going through a digital transformation, you're basically saying, 'Well, we care about the technology, not about you.'"
While companies have heavily invested in AI tools, Cadigan said many have not "built the trust to get people to the point where they can say, 'Yeah, just go ahead and reinvent your job; we got your back.'"
As more companies signal AI-driven job cuts, Cadigan said many employees see the first implementation of AI as "cutting people in the name of AI."
Instead, Cadigan stressed that organizations need to promise to workers that they are investing in their growth and development, and that while they can't predict how AI will change their jobs or their future employment, these companies will "grow and develop you … we're going to make you a better human being and a better professional, and if things don't work out here, you're going to be a better person on the other side."
"That's a bigger promise," he said.
— Ian Thomas
7 Hours Ago
The CNBC Workforce Executive Council Summit is underway!
The entrance of the 2026 CNBC Workforce Executive Council Summit in New York City on October 27, 2026.
CNBC
The programming has kicked off here in New York: first up is Steve Cadigan, the creator and author of the Human Advantage Framework, a research-informed framework for understanding, assessing, and developing the human capabilities that matter most in the age of AI.
Cadigan will be speaking with CNBC's Leslie Picker about how AI is reshaping work and how employers need to equip employees to adapt to this fast rate of change.
8 Hours Ago
Health insurance costs are growing, with no end in sight
watch now
VIDEO10:0310:03
Rising costs of health benefits: Total cost per employee expected to rise 8.2% in 2027
Most Americans under age 65 — about 166 million people — get health insurance via employer-sponsored health plans.
That is generally subsided by their employers, who cover a large portion of the monthly premium payments workers pay. The average worker paid $6,850 of annual premiums in 2025, while employers contributed more than $20,000 per worker, according to KFF.
In 2027, the cost for employers to provide health benefits will rise by an estimated 8.2% per worker, on average. That represents the largest increase since 2003, even with additional cost-reduction measures by employers, according to Marsh.
Aon, another consulting firm, expects employer costs to jump 9.5% in 2027 — the fourth consecutive year of "elevated" healthcare costs, "extending one of the most sustained periods of health care inflation employers have faced in decades," the firm said in a press release in August.
Growth in the cost of deductibles and family premiums has each outpaced inflation over the past decade, rising 54% and 53%, respectively, versus an overall inflation rate of 36%, according to KFF.
All of those cost increases are likely leading to cuts in benefits next year for workers who are covered by plans from their jobs: Nearly 6 out of 10 employers — 59% — plan to make cost-cutting changes to health benefits in 2027, including by adding higher deductibles, according to Marsh. It polled more than 1,800 employers from June 10 to August 10.
HealthEquity CFO James Lucania will be speaking later today at the CNBC Workforce Summit about how CHROs and benefits managers can use AI to streamline healthcare costs, and at the same time, make out-of-pocket payments easier for employees to understand and manage, all while helping each of them get the care they need.
8 Hours Ago
AI is fueling uncertainty in the job market
A sign on the Microsoft campus in Redmond, Washington, US, Oct. 26, 2026.
David Ryder | Reuters
There are many forces changing the workplace. But few are having the impact that AI is, shifting roles and job expectations, as well as headcount.
Microsoft announced this week that it is offering voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees, a measure that comes as the company strives to balance a costly AI build-out with efficiency.
The software company has been ramping up its spending on data centers to accommodate high AI computing demand as it supplies cloud services to a number of AI companies. The offer follows a voluntary retirement program announced at Microsoft this past spring and 4,800 jobs cut in July.
American Express said last week that it would be cutting thousands of employees as the leading credit card company prepares for artificial intelligence to take over more of its internal processes.
Amex is eliminating 5% of its global workforce and taking a $336 million restructuring charge, CEO Stephen Squeri told analysts Friday on the company's third-quarter earnings call. The firm had almost 77,000 employees at the end of 2025.
Chief Financial Officer Christophe Le Caillec told CNBC in an interview that the restructuring was to make American Express "leaner, more agile, and also to prepare for AI."
"You don't want to automate processes that are not optimally structured," Le Caillec said. "So what we're doing here is to reduce layers and increase spans of controls, so that we can automate and take advantage of AI in the coming quarters and the coming years."
The Amex announcement reflects a broader trend across financial services, where banks are working to replace repetitive roles with AI automation. On Thursday, Barclays confirmed plans to trim 5,000 jobs — also roughly 5% of its staff — in another tech-driven cost initiative. The moves come even as the sector is enjoying robust profits from growing consumer spending and resilient credit.
Earlier this month, the New York City Council held a legislative investigation concerning artificial intelligence safety risks, with senior leaders from Anthropic, OpenAI,Google and Metatestifying under oath about the potential dangers of the technology and outlined current safety measures.
The hearing took place amid the intense debate surrounding the risks posed by advanced AI models. It also came as the questions over who is responsible for keeping the technology in-check also grow.
With concerns over the federal government's oversight of AI abound, cities are stepping up. New York City Council speaker Julie Menin opened that hearing by singling out the federal government's light-touch approach to AI after President Donald Trump signed a voluntary accord with tech leaders in Washington last week.
"The idea that artificial intelligence is going to self-regulate defies all reason," she said at the hearing.
Menin, who is appearing at today's Workforce Executive Summit, told CNBC's Kelly Evans on "The Exchange" following the hearing that one of the biggest takeaways was that the AI labs "really weren't able to answer some of the most rudimentary questions, such as what is the risk of a cataclysmic event happening? What do they feel the risk is? Will they agree, for example, not to release any new model that hasn't passed an internal or third-party validator safety check?"
"I think what really came out of the hearing is the need for regulation," Menin told Evans. "We have to remember that the pharmaceutical industry doesn't self-regulate; they have the FDA. The airline industry doesn't self-regulate; they have the FAA, and similarly, we need to ensure that with artificial intelligence, we have smart safeguard rails in place."
Menin told Evans that much of the responsibility when it comes to legislating AI will fall to localities, and she hopes that some of the legislation New York City is putting into effect will serve as a blueprint for other jurisdictions.
"We certainly hope the federal government will opt to regulate," she said, adding that she sees one of the most important regulations as the issue of third-party regulation. "You cannot have these companies self-select a validator," she said.
Menin added that she does not want to stifle innovation, but cautions that "with innovation, really comes responsibility, and I think it actually instills faith and confidence in the products that these companies are releasing, the new models that they're releasing, if we have smart and sensible safeguards in place."
-Colleen McKown
9 Hours Ago
What's on the agenda at CNBC's 2026 WEC Summit
Jada Pinkett Smith in conversation with CNBC's Carl Quintanilla at the Workforce Executive Council Summit in New York City on Nov. 14, 2023.
CNBC
CNBC has convened workforce leaders and industry experts to discuss the variety of forces changing the workplace.
Here are some of the discussions on today's agenda:
Steve Cadigan, Human Advantage Framework creator and author, is joining CNBC's Leslie Picker for a conversation about how AI is reshaping a workforce ready for change, how leaders can bolster the people skills AI cannot provide and ways to equip employees to successfully adapt and adjust to the rapid pace of change.
Nelson Chai, DailyPay CEO, will join CNBC's Sharon Epperson to discuss the challenges employees face staying financially afloat amid the rising costs of groceries, gas and everyday personal expenses. Chai will share ways employers can help workers deal with ongoing financial strain.
Maren Waggoner, Walmart's chief people officer of digital & associate experience, will speak with CNBC's Leslie Picker about why Walmart is "people-led and tech-powered," why AI is a work design issue and not a technology issue and how talent leaders can ensure that they're not just deploying AI to employees but rather giving them the ability to use AI to redesign their own work.
Jill Bruning, Amentum chief technology officer and Jacob Pat, Lovesac chief technology and digital transformation officer, two members of CNBC's Technology Executive Council, will join CNBC's Susan Caminiti to share their tech-centric perspectives on how companies can harness the power of AI while keeping the human needs of the workforce front and center.
James Lucania, HealthEquity CFO, joins CNBC's Annika Kim Constantino for a discussion on ways CHROs and benefits managers can use AI to streamline healthcare costs, and at the same time, make out-of-pocket payments easier for employees to understand and manage, all while helping each of them get the care they need.
Wes Burke, Care.com CHRO, Kerri Eskin, Cotiviti chief people officer, and Amy Segal, The Team managing director, join CNBC's Sharon Epperson to discuss how AI is redefining what makes a great employee and how they're attracting the right workers in this tech-powered moment.
Julie Menin, New York City Council speaker, recently brought leaders from the biggest AI companies together to answer questions under oath on safety and the risks of things going wrong. She'll join CNBC's Leslie Picker to discuss what cities can do if the federal government fails to act.
Dan Harris, author, podcaster and former ABC News anchor, will join CNBC's Susan Caminiti to discuss how we can turn down the volume on our inner critics, let go of the relentless push to do more and learn to be a little kinder to ourselves while still being effective.

articles.title: Ngôi nhà ven biển Hội An 'nâng' toàn bộ phòng nghỉ để đón gió
articles.text:
Ngôi nhà ven biển Hội An 'nâng' toàn bộ phòng nghỉ để đón gió
Nằm sát biển Hội An nhưng bị một đồi cát cao 3,5m che khuất tầm nhìn, công trình lưu trú được thiết kế với tầng một thông thoáng, các phòng nghỉ hướng ra biển và hệ đường dốc thay thế cầu thang. Giải pháp này giúp du khách cảm nhận được gió biển ngay từ khi bước vào, dù chưa nhìn thấy mặt nước.
Công trình nằm trong khu vực tương đối yên tĩnh, thu hút nhiều du khách nước ngoài lưu trú dài ngày và tìm hiểu văn hóa địa phương. Trong quá trình khảo sát, nhóm thiết kế nhận thấy một đặc điểm đáng chú ý: tại những khu đất trống, gió biển thổi mạnh dù tầm nhìn bị đồi cát chắn lại. Ngược lại, khi đi qua các công trình kinh doanh xây dựng khép kín, cảm giác về gió gần như biến mất.
Từ quan sát này, phương án thiết kế được phát triển theo hướng giải phóng không gian tầng một, tạo điều kiện để gió biển đi sâu vào công trình. Thay vì bố trí các phòng nghỉ chiếm toàn bộ mặt bằng, tầng thấp nhất được dành cho những khoảng mở và các mặt sàn có cao độ tăng dần về phía đồi cát.
Tuy nhiên, việc để trống tầng một đặt ra bài toán về số lượng phòng nghỉ. Công trình phải đồng thời đáp ứng yêu cầu của chủ đầu tư, giới hạn mật độ xây dựng, chiều cao và quy định sử dụng mái dốc.
Để giải quyết, các không gian được bố trí ở nhiều cao độ khác nhau, tận dụng phần diện tích dưới mái dốc. Hệ cầu thang thông thường được thay bằng một đường dốc kết nối các khu vực trong công trình với cảnh quan xung quanh.
Mặt bằng hình chữ U cũng được lựa chọn để các phòng nghỉ đều có tầm nhìn hướng biển, khắc phục hạn chế về tầm nhìn từ lối vào ban đầu.
Một chi tiết khác là bể bơi được tạo hình như con thuyền treo giữa không trung. Tại lối vào chính, hệ kết cấu vượt nhịp dài 14m tạo khoảng mở lớn, tương phản với hệ cột tròn ở phía trong.
Từ một khu đất sát biển nhưng bị chắn tầm nhìn, công trình khai thác gió như yếu tố dẫn dắt trải nghiệm không gian. Du khách có thể cảm nhận không khí biển ngay từ tầng một, sau đó dần tiếp cận cảnh quan qua các đường dốc, khoảng mở và phòng nghỉ trên cao.
Tiền phong
